teaching: The lessons of the book Anwaar al-Latifah are composed of the lofty 'sciences of realities' ('uloom-e-haqa'iq), interpreted on the basis of the sciences of the prophets (anbiya') and saints (awliya').
These lessons were recorded with the explicit permission (ijazat) of Hadrat 'Abdullah Sahib and by the command of the speaker's Aaqa, then deposited in the treasury of the Da'wat Sharief.

It is forbidden to email, exchange on the internet, copy, transmit, or modify these lessons without permission, lest they fall into the hands of the undeserving (ghair-mustahiqqeen); doing so is a sin for which the doer alone bears responsibility on the Day of Judgment.
The Awliya' of Allah have warned of a most severe punishment ('azab) — described as the punishment of cold iron — for those who fail to safeguard these lofty sciences ('uloom-e-'aliya).

The title 'Suradiq' (also Sardaq) means a curtain, palace, large tent (shamiyana/khaima), or grand encampment; the book is structured as five Suradiqs, each containing five chapters (babs), each bab containing five sections (fasls).

The book's stated purpose is to express a pure reality (haqiqatan mahdatan) about the noble affections leading to the noble obligations, without ta'weel (esoteric interpretation), without ramz (symbol), and without ishara (allusion).

Through the gnosis (ma'rifah) of all existing things, obedience to and love of the Awliya' Allah, drawing near to Allah through them, and adhering to their appointed hudud from the Qa'im, one is guided to the tawhid of Allah.

Access to the tawhid of Allah is attained through two things: wilayah (allegiance/love, muwalat/muhabbah) and 'amal (action); by these the ranks of the afterlife (ma'ad) are elevated and salvation from this world of being and corruption is achieved.

The original homeland (watan-e-asli) of humanity is the world of spirits ('alam al-ruh), and the goal is to return (qawd) to the origin (mabda') from which the noble beginnings came and to dwell with the Awliya' in dar al-quds (the Abode of Sanctity).

All creatures circle around the knowledge of the origin (mabda'/asl) in bewilderment but cannot reach it, except a few who held fast to the Imams from the progeny of Muhammad and committed to their blessed hudud.

Allah Ta'ala is so transcendent (muta'ali) that no indicator's indication (ishara) can fall upon Him and no thought (khatir), imagination (tawahhum), or contemplation (tafkir) can dare toward Him — this is the foundation of correct beliefs.
Imam Ali, when asked by Ibn al-Kawwa' whether he had seen his God, replied that he could not worship a God he had not seen, and that he saw Him not with the eyes but with insight (basirah).

Names and attributes do not fall upon Allah because names/attributes fall only upon their like (la taqa'u illa 'ala misliha), and they are created (muhdathah) by humans, while a created thing cannot fall upon its creator in a like manner.

The names and attributes are negated from Allah Ta'ala and instead fall upon His origination (ibda') — which is the First Intellect ('aql al-awwal), the first existent (mawjud al-awwal), and the first emanation (sadir al-awwal).

Inadequacy ('ijz) is comprehensive over the entire world of intellect and world of sense; the powerful and the overpowered, the sensed and the intelligible are all equal in their inability to know the Originator.

Our saying 'Allah' is merely an expression arising from the bewilderment (ilhan/walah) of the First Intellect about the Originator; Allah is the center of the circle around which the bewildered circle revolves, the revolving being the energy of bewilderment.

The First Intellect first negated divinity (la ilaha) from itself and its genus — affirming it could not create itself — then affirmed divinity for the Originator (illa Hu), as the Qur'an states 'Allah testifies that there is no god but He.'

The created intellects were given 'total knowledge' (ilm al-kulli) of life — knowledge of hayat, 'ilm, quwwah, and ikhtiyar — but were NOT given knowledge of the essence of Allah, as Sayyidna Mu'ayyad explains.
Allah, after giving existence, does not take back existence — just as a human who gives something does not take it from another; and though Allah can do everything, He does not do injustice (zulm).

Naming Allah is a 'sin coupled with seeking forgiveness' (dhanbun mashfu'un bi-al-istighfar): being compelled (idtirar) to address Him by an inadequate name is a sin, but it is paired with istighfar and accepted because of human helplessness.

The Da'i's terminology of shafa', witr, and julus has esoteric referents: shafa' (two paired rak'at) refers to the Prophet and Lady Fatima, witr (single rak'at) refers to Imam Ali, and julus (two rak'at sitting) refers to Imam Hasan and Imam Husayn.

There are ten spiritual ranks (maratib) ascending to the highest: Imamate of spirituality, Hujjiyyah, Hijabiyyah, Khayaliyyah, Fathiyyah, Jiddiyyah, Anza'iyyah, Qa'imiyyah, Jussiyyah, Ahadiyyah, Samadiyyah — culminating in Ilahiyyah and Huwiyyah as the final rank.

True Tawhid is the gnosis of the hudud (ma'rifat al-hudud) — knowing that every had (rank) is unique in its own place and recognizing its station — NOT considering Allah as one, which would be shirk since Allah admits no number or definition.

Tawhid has three branches: Tawhid (gnosis of the hudud), tanzih (negation of divinity / ilahiyyat meaning the power of originating beings, ibda' al-zawat, from the hudud), and tajrid (divestment of all names and attributes from Allah).

The knowledge of Tawhid is the highest of all knowledge (ajall al-'ilm); since Allah created innumerable beings (zawat), there is innumerable gnosis, and a person's station (martaba) and haykal-rank are established according to how much gnosis they attain in life through 'ilm and 'amal.
Salvation (najat) is a good end (khatima bil-khair); gnosis is attained both by one's own effort (juhd) and by the grace (fazl) of those above.
The limit (nuqta-e irtifa') of the Prophet is Hijabiyyat, of Janab-e Fatimah is Hujjiyyat, and of Abd al-Muttalib is Jaddiyyat (which itself has ten stations).

Gnosis of the hudud is of two kinds: outer gnosis (ma'rifah zahirah) by which the person and station of a had are known and in which friend and enemy are equal; and inner gnosis (ma'rifah batinah) of the beginning, end, and return of a had's existence, specific to the people of truth (ahl al-haqq).

Inner gnosis — knowing the beginning, level, and end (ma'ad) of a had's essence (khamira) — can be attained only by the Imam al-Zaman and by the disciplined (murtazin) and verifiers (muhiqqin); one whose gnosis is deficient has no Tawhid at all.
The closest had to us is the Mukathir; what is established for the lower of the hudud is established for the higher (ma thabata fi al-dani thabata fil-'ali).

The ranks below the hudud are Mustajib (one who takes the noble pledge with his tongue, with ten levels graded by the intensity/hiddat of the pledge) and Mu'min (defined as profession with the tongue, affirmation with the heart, and action with the limbs — al-qawl bil-lisan wa al-tasdiq bil-jinan wa al-'amal bil-arkan, with ten levels).

The Mukathir is the first rank within the hudud; 'mukathir' derives from kasr (breaking with proofs/hujjat), and he must first break his own self (kasr-e nafs) by binding his every word, action, and intention to the command of Allah and the Prophet — requiring acquisition of knowledge ('ulum).

Although the Mukathir and ordinary humans share the same outer composition (flesh, blood, bones, nerves, veins), they are not the same: the Mukathir's temperament has become refined (talattafa mizajuhu) and his essence pure (safa jawharuhu), ascending through many stations to the highest ranks of humanity, which are the first ranks of the spiritual world (malakutiyya).

The Mukathir is the place of descent for Allah's revelation (mahbat li-wahyi Allah) and a house from His houses (baytun min buyutihi), because he keeps the command of Allah and the Prophet before him in thought, word, and deed.

The Qur'anic 'houses' in which Allah permitted His name to be exalted (fi buyutin adhin Allahu an turfa') are the hudud, and the 'men whom commerce does not divert from the remembrance of Allah, prayer, and zakat' refers to establishing the da'wah (iqamat al-da'wah).

The pillars of religion have esoteric (ta'weel) meanings: wilayat = repenting in the world of motes; taharat = purifying from the filth of Iblis through the knowledge of the Tenth; salat = acting on the commands of the Tenth/Imam in whose sphere one is; zakat = giving a portion of the knowledge given to you.

Further esoteric pillars: sawm (fasting) = concealing knowledge from the undeserving; khums = giving a fifth of knowledge received unexpectedly (as Imam Husayn gave the khums of his salary); hajj = preparing oneself to go toward the bab al-batin (Imam al-Zaman is the House of Allah); jihad = sacrificing or slaying the commanding self (nafs).

One who does not establish prayer (iqamat al-salah) declines from the first principle, is pushed back below the thousand-fold human form (surat al-alfiyya), becomes more astray than cattle, and ends in the barzakh al-khawf — while the Mukathir who establishes inward prayer ascends.

Lawful (halal) animals are like the ascending pure human/Mukathir — they become food, take intimacy with man (the caliph of Allah), and ascend on the straight path (sirat al-sawiyy, the human person) toward the first principle; predatory (forbidden) animals are averse and proceed in decline away from the first principle.

When a seeker (mustafid) receives the spiritual speech (al-kalam al-malakuti) and divine knowledge from the Mukathir, his intellect is bewildered and the Mukathir becomes for him a 'god' (ilah) and master of his neck — 'god' meaning the center of the circle around which he revolves in bewilderment, NOT the creator of beings.

The mu'min verifies that the Mukathir himself needs and is bewildered before the had above him, ascending through the hudud to the Imam, then to the abstract intellects (al-'uqul al-mujarradat), until reaching the First Intellect, which is bewildered before its Originator — then he negates divinity from all and affirms it for Allah alone (la ilaha illa Hu).

In the spiritual world the da'wah formed nested circles: each circle has a center (the sabiq/forerunner); those who joined repented with him (tawabu bi-tawbatihi) and ascended; the final individual left was commanded to give the da'wah, becoming the center of a new circle — establishing the circles of Imam, Bab, Hujjat, etc., all on the first pattern.

The word 'ilah' is composed of alif-lam-ha encoding three conditions present in every circle: alif = precedence without an inspirer (aql al-awwal); lam = advancing by seeing/repenting with another's repentance (munba'ith min al-awwal); ha = the da'wah given by the seven uqul (the 'ashir did not).

The created 'gods' (aliha) — created, invented, originated — each carry the name of a nourisher (murabbi) above them and a need calling them upward; the only true God (la ilaha siwahu) is the one beyond the limited physical hudud and the unlimited spiritual hudud, from whom even names and attributes are stripped.

The Qur'anic verse 'O tranquil soul, return to your Lord, well-pleased and well-pleasing' (irji'i ila rabbiki radiyatan mardiyya) means the soul ascends to the top then returns to its mufid (Lord), its tranquility (itmi'nan) lying in what it has known and its pleasure in its Lord's command.

The summary of the Qur'an's teaching about the Originator is Surah al-Fatiha, in which the three classes of people are mentioned: the favored/repentant (an'amta 'alayhim = nadimin), those who incurred wrath (maghdubi = the insistent/musirrin), and the astray (dallin = the bewildered/mutahayyirin).

The reality of Allah cannot be understood, as proven by the Qur'an 'Glory be to Him above what they describe' (Subhan Allah 'amma yasifun) — whatever attributes are ascribed to Him, He is pure (tanzih) from them.

Allah Ta'ala created the worlds of origination — alluded to by seven names: 'alam al-amr (command), 'alam al-'aql (intellect), 'alam al-quds (sanctity), 'alam al-safa (purity), 'alam al-latafah (subtlety), 'alam al-ruhani (spiritual) — in a single instant (daf'atan wahidatan), not in time, with no prior matter (hayula), no accompanying thing, and no place.
Ibda' (origination) is creating from nothing; khalq (creation) is forming a new composite from pre-existing things by changing their arrangement.

Allah originated the existents from non-existence ('adam) purely as a favor (tafaddul), generosity (jud), and bestowal (tatawwul) — not from need nor for sport — since it is the nature (shimah/sajiyyah) of the Generous and Mighty to bestow; Sayyidna Mohyuddin establishes this by negating all other purposes.

The originated beings were brought into existence as luminous imaginal forms (ashbah suriyyah nuraniyya) possessing thousand-fold statures (qamatin alfiyya) like the human corporeal stature — in reality the human stature is patterned on them — distinct from their later material (hayulaniyya) souls and dark bodies.

The luminous forms were created equal in the first perfection (kamal al-awwal) — which is existence (wujud), life (hayat), strength (quwwah), and ability/knowledge (qudrah/'ilm) — with no disagreement, preference, or distinction among them, as an act of justice (adl) from Allah.

The equal creation of all beings is anchored on the Qur'an 'And if it had been from other than Allah, they would have found therein much contradiction' (wa law kana min 'indi ghayrillahi la-wajadu fihi ikhtilafan kathira), and matches Sayyidna Hamiduddin's statement in Rahat al-'Aql.

In the abode of origination and emanation (dar al-ibda' wa al-inbi'ath) there is no obstacle, because the forms are pure (mahdah) and free of obstructing matter (maddah); thus the existence of all existents was in a single instant, like light filling air from the sun or a fire illuminating a dark house.

The intellects existing in actuality (bi-l-fi'l) and in potentiality (bi-l-quwwah) existed together at one time, so no period of time separated the first perfection (kamal al-awwal) from the second perfection (kamal al-thani).

In the state of first perfection all beings are equal but NOT infallible (ghayr ma'sum) from error; the 'error' (khata) is failing to attain the second perfection — delay in invitation, refusing the call, misleading others; the perfect/infallible state is only the second perfection.

One of the luminous forms looked with his essence at his essence and at his kind (nazara bi-dhatihi ila dhatihi), knew there was an Originator unlike them, negated divinity from himself and his kind, and affirmed it for the Originator — thus performing tawhid, tajrid, and tanzih all together as Sahib al-Tawhid.

He acknowledged the Originator's Lordship, glorified Him, humbled himself, and crucially sought the means (tawassul) of the Originator's own greatness toward Him — taking His greatness as the means to reach Him, since His greatness cannot be reached directly.

As a result, divine supports (mawad ilahiyya) and confirmations of oneness (ta'yidat wahdaniyya) reached him, and the flowing knowledge ('ilm al-jari) and spreading light (nur al-sari) connected with him — which is the Word of Allah (kalimatullah), namely 'La ilaha illa Allah.'

The kalimah 'La ilaha illa Allah' (also named al-amr, the command) is above the intellect and below the Originator (fawqa al-'aql wa dun al-mubdi'); it is the continuous link between Originator (mubdi') and originated (mubda'), and through it flow knowledge and light, lasting as long as creation remains.

The first perfection's gifts (existence, knowledge, power, freedom) cannot be taken away by Allah once given; the being is ghayr ma'sum in that state but retains those powers, and must use them correctly to journey toward and activate the second perfection — and humanity is currently in a fallen state of the first perfection, journeying toward the second.

Through the kalimah the First Intellect encompassed all things in knowledge ('ilm) and knew what was and what will be (ma kana wa ma sayakun); it had to negate itself (affirm it was not its own creator) before obtaining the kalimah and its light.

The kalimah 'La ilaha illa Allah' is composed in numbered layers: negation+affirmation (2); three letters alif-lam-ha (3); four words la/ilaha/illa/Allah (4); the world ended at seven luminous forms because of its seven muqatta'at (where pen/tongue stops); twelve are the ascending spirits — and seven plus twelve equal nineteen, as in Bismillah al-Rahman al-Rahim.

Bismillah al-Rahman al-Rahim encodes the week of the seven Imams (Bismillah, seven letters) each with twelve naqibs (al-Rahman al-Rahim), per Sayyidna Muhammad Taher; the additive construction (tarkib-i-idafi) is more excellent than the descriptive (tarkib-i-tawsifi).

The First Intellect increased in humility, submission, bewilderment, and reverence (khushu') after obtaining the kalimah; this is why the Qur'an says 'Indeed, only those of knowledge among His servants fear Allah' (innama yakhsha Allaha min 'ibadihi al-'ulama'), fear being acknowledgment of His greatness.

Allah took the First Intellect as a veil (hijab) and gate (bab) for Himself, through which alone one may seek means (tawassul), have intimate discourse (munajah), or declare Him One (yuwahhad); thus the First Intellect became His Greatest Name (ism al-a'zam) and most noble station.

The Second Emanation (munba'ith/mumbai al-thani) failed to attain the second perfection because, while acknowledging the First Intellect's superiority, he was deceived by the notion of equality (wahm-e masawat) — claiming his vision equaled the First Intellect's; in the first perfection all are equal, but in the second perfection none can be equal.

The circle of the First Originator (mubdi') is the circle of oneness (da'irat al-wahdat) which no other being can enter; the First Intellect possesses the veil (hijab), and Sayyidna Sadiq explained that 'oneness' here is a special honorific and that quds is also called a circle encompassed by the First Intellect.

The limit of the intellect ('aql) — and of all three essences/powers (jawahir: hayat, 'ilm, ikhtiyar) given to the created essences — is bewilderment (hayrat), because the intellect cannot attain the gnosis of its God though created by Him.

Two of the luminous forms emanated from the noble First Intellect, called the two First Emanations (munba'ithayn al-awwalayn); though they emanated simultaneously, one preceded the other (sabaqa ahaduhuma al-akhar) — the term munba'ith deriving from alif yielding lam and fa.

The First Emanation (munba'ith al-awwal / second intellect) looked at his essence and kind just as the First Intellect did, knew there was an Originator unlike them, negated divinity from himself and his kind, affirmed it for Allah, and glorified/sanctified the First Intellect — acknowledging its precedence, virtue, and nobility.

Before their emanation, the First Intellect had two established gazes: the nobler gaze (nazar-e ashraf) born of its tawhid/tanzih/tajrid and resulting luminosity, and the lower gaze (nazar-e adna) of joy at its firstness (awwaliyyat); the First Emanation's gaze was toward the nobler, the Second's toward the lower.

The greatest crime established against the Second/Third Intellect (the 'ashir, the Tenth) was the delusion of equality (wahm-e masawat) — claiming his gaze equaled the First Emanation's because they emanated together — even though he understood the difference of gaze; this halted his rank.

The First Emanation, having the nobler gaze and acknowledging the First Intellect's precedence, received divine light (nur ilahi) and infinite knowledge from it, reached the second perfection, and became an eternal (azali), perfect, complete, infallible (ma'sum), excellent intellect — differing from the First only by the rank of precedence (rutbat al-sabq).

In the second perfection (kamal al-thani) no being can surpass another and no circle can surpass another — the ranks are locked, the seventh intellect can never overtake the sixth; the only ikhtiyar (choice) to surpass one's mufid exists in the fallen first-perfection state of munba'ith and other cycles (karrat), not in the luminous second perfection.

The difference between First Intellect and First Emanation is that the First is ibda' (origination — advancing on its own from its essence) and the Second is inbi'ath (emanation — advancing by seeing another); ibda' cannot be like inbi'ath, as Sayyidna Hamiduddin states in Rahat al-'Aql.

The First Intellect rushed upon the tawhid, tanzih, tasbih, and taqdis of its Originator from its essence, for its essence, with its essence (min dhatihi li-dhatihi bi-dhatihi), with no prior or predecessor — thereby deserving all the noble names that belong to no other except him.

The First Intellect is named: al-ibda', al-mubda' al-awwal (first originated), al-wujud and al-mawjud al-awwal, al-haqiqah and al-haqq al-awwal, al-wahdah and al-wahid al-awwal, al-tamam, al-kamal, al-azal, al-'aql, al-'ilm, al-qudrah, al-hayat, al-sabq, al-'ismah, and mudahhir al-duhur (the one who rolls out the ages) — each as the first of its kind.

The name 'mubda'' (originated) applies to the First Intellect and all his kind (the whole cosmos), but the name 'ibda'' is specific to the First Intellect alone, because he rushed upon and initiated the tawhid of his Originator by an act he alone performed.

The First Intellect bears the names al-'alim al-awwal (first connected with flowing knowledge), al-qadir al-awwal, al-hayy al-awwal (first connected with the spirit of true life, given eternal life), al-sabiq al-awwal, al-mu'tasim al-awwal (first protected from error by hablillah — the rope of God, the kalimah), and al-dahr al-awwal.

The First Intellect is mudahhir al-duhur, muwahhid al-muwahhidin, and mu'azzil al-mu'azzilin (the one who enables doers, teaches tawhid to unifiers, and grants eternity) because the 'ages' (duhur) are the higher hudud (al-hudud al-'alawiyya), whom he aids with divine light; the physical hudud are named 'years and eras.'

The First Intellect is in continuous evolution: Allah's treasures (bounties) have no limit, so the First Intellect's splendor, perfection, intellect, and power only increase forever (only rising, never falling); how much he will rise is knowledge of the unseen ('ilm al-ghayb).

In 'Allahu la ilaha illa Huwa al-Hayy al-Qayyum,' Huwa is the Originator (mabda'), al-Hayy is the First Intellect (station of unity/wahdat), and al-Qayyum is the First Emanation (munba'ith al-awwal), with whom are gathered all the second perfections to be attained in the future.

The First Emanation's state was a quality other than the quality of origination: he contemplated that the First Intellect's greatness came from its preceding action and its tawhid/tanzih/tasbih/taqdis of the Originator, then that contemplation emanated in his own essence, so he stood as the First Intellect stood, taking it as his Imam (musta'imman).

The First Emanation is called 'al-munba'ith al-awwal' because what the First originated (ibtada') emanated within him; 'sending forth' (ba'th) requires existence, then effacement (durus), then a second existence — from which is derived the resurrection of the dead (ba'th al-mawta) on the Day of Judgment and the truth that resurrection from graves is real.

The First Emanation is also called al-tali (the follower, following the First Intellect in action), al-'aql al-thani (the second intellect in tawhid/tanzih/tajrid), al-lawh (the tablet, receptacle for the rays of al-qalam = the First Intellect, the pen), and al-nafs al-kulliyya (the universal soul, noblest existent after the First, a 'whole' to whom all return).

The end (intiha) of all the intellects is toward the First Emanation, not the First Intellect: the Garden of Abode (Jannat al-ma'wa) — everyone's paradise — is the First Emanation, located near Sidrat al-Muntaha (the self of the First Intellect); none can attain Sidrat al-Muntaha except the First Intellect, who affirmed from his own self.

The Second Emanation (inbi'ath al-thani) emanated and looked just as the First Emanation, negated divinity and affirmed it for the Originator, glorified the First Intellect — but did NOT glorify or sanctify the First Emanation nor acknowledge its virtue and precedence; rather he transgressed (takhatta'ahu) and thought himself equal (musawat/mumathila), which was a slip (zalla) and sin (khati'a).

The principle of precedence: each being must acknowledge the precedence of those before it; one whose vision (nazar) sees the reality/principles (asl) is noble (ashraf), while one who sees only the branches (furu') is lower (adna) — and being noble of vision elevates, while seeing branches lowers.

Because of his claim of equality, the bounties, glances, confirmations, and blessings (mawaddat, lahazat, ta'yidat, barakat) of the First Emanation were cut off from the Second Emanation, who did not attain the second perfection — the same action done by both differing only in the reality of vision and intention.

The difference between the two emanations is illustrated by 'two joys' (masarratayn): the higher joy (masarrat al-'ala) of worshipping God (the core reality) versus the lower joy (masarrat al-adna) of superiority over others; the First Emanation's vision was on the higher, the Second's on the lower, yet he still claimed equality.

The First Intellect united with the First Emanation, taking it as a veil (hijab) and a gate (bab) to its obedience and the obedience of its Originator; the First Intellect established the da'wah in that world and addressed all through the First Emanation.

In the parallel structure, the Imam corresponds to the First Intellect (advancing on his own through the gnosis of the 'ayn 'azima, who is the Imam of the Imam), the Bab al-inbi'ath corresponds to the First Emanation (advancing by seeing the Imam), and the hidden gates advance through da'wah.

Seven luminous forms (sab'at ashbahin suriyya) responded to the First Intellect's da'wah one after another; each affirmed the unity of his Originator, acknowledged the lordship, precedence, and rank of the First Intellect and the First Emanation, and glorified his own limit (had) at which he stood.

The world ended at seven because Allah placed seven muqatta'at (disconnected letters, where pen/tongue stops) in 'La ilaha illa Allah'; the seven circles were predestined in the kalimah, which is between the Originator and the originated — beings had absolute choice in advancing on their own but not in where the count ended.

Each of the seven intellects acknowledged the limit of the one above it in ascending sequence, until the seventh acknowledged the prior six, the First Emanation, the First Intellect, and the Originator; a divine light and endless knowledge flowed from the First Intellect to the second and continued to them, by which the second perfection (kamal al-thani — salvation, infallibility, success, bounty) is attained.

Sayyidna Hamiduddin states in Rahat al-'Aql that existence is from the First Intellect, the First Emanation, and seven intellects, and the existence of each is from the last (siwa al-munba'ith al-awwal) ascending to the First Intellect; later authorities counted eight bearers of the Throne (hamalat al-'arsh) from the seven muqatta'at plus 'La ilaha illa Allah' itself.

In each da'wah circle there is a center (chief) and twelve chiefs (ru'asa'), because the letters of 'La ilaha illa Allah' number twelve; when a circle is completed (e.g. at 28 limits, predestined in the kalimah), the last individual is commanded to give the da'wah and forms a new circle.

The First Intellect (al-Natiq), the Asas (foundation), and the seven uqul transmit the kingly luminous light (nur-e shahshani / nur-e shashani ilahi) downward; whatever happened, happened, and the hudud are made just ('adilan) between them and the other intellects.

The believer (mu'min) in the period of occultation (ghaybah), upon attaining the state of nur-e shashani, becomes Ahl al-Bayt; the ghaybah is itself a great blessing (ni'mah), and the knowledge of the Awwal and Thani is obtained through intellect while knowledge of the Imam comes through the knowledge of his occultation, call, and summons.

The Qur'anic 'Allah witnesses that there is no deity except Him, and the angels and those of knowledge' (shahida Allahu... wal-mala'ikatu wa ulu al-'ilm) means three give witness: Allah, the angels (al-mala'ikah = al-Sabiq, the first-sent precedent), and the people of knowledge (ulu al-'ilm = al-Mumaththal al-Awwal / ahl al-da'wat al-sahihah).

The Mumaththal al-Awwal (First Representative) establishes the call and is above the Sabiq; the Sabiq (precedent) is the first to respond to the call (mujib li-da'watihi); no indication toward the Originator is possible except through the Nabi (Prophet) and Wasi (Successor).

True existence (wujud haqiqi) is the second perfection (kamal al-thani); the first existence is only life (zindagi). This world is called 'alam al-amr, 'alam al-ruh, 'alam al-arwah, 'alam al-ibda', 'alam al-'aql al-kull, and 'alam al-quds — all due to its relation to the command of God (amrillah).

The world of subtlety ('alam-e latafat) and world of attributes ('alam-e sifat) have no physical density; the eight worlds are 'alam-e ruhani, 'alam-e abdan, 'alam-e 'aql, 'alam-e nafs, 'alam-e latafat, 'alam-e sifat (and the world of bodies and existence) — the souls being a later, fallen degradation of the luminous forms and the bodies an even more fallen form.

From one divine command (hukm) seven forms emerged, and from those seven came innumerable forms (suwaran kathiran); after the first seven, the gate of permission closed, and within each of the seven many forms appeared through response (ijabat) — the last form of the first circle being superior to the second circle.

In every da'wah cycle the chief is like an Imam (he is to them as imam, they to him as ma'mum), like a boundary (had) to which they are the bounded (mahdudin), and like a chief (ra'is) to whom they are subjects (mar'usin); each chief is one form, and his circle, once drawn (beginning meeting end), is connected to him as center.

The seven intellects, by the sharpness (hiddah) and speed of their vision, linked heaven with the seven 'qurubiyyah' (the Kurubiyyin / Angels Brought Near, called the chiefs/ru'asa'); those under their charge are named the spiritual angels (al-mala'ikah al-ruhaniyyin).

The hierarchy of angels: highest are the Mala'ikah Kurubiyyin (seated from the beginning), then the Mala'ikah Ruhaniyyin in their circle, then the Mala'ikat al-Muqarrabun (the Angels Brought Near) — those ascending from below the tenth had toward them, called Muqarrab because they are 'coming near'; the tenth had ('ashir) are the people of the barzakh (ahl al-barzakh).

Above the barzakh is the Jadd, which remains above every Imam as his hujjat (above all 24 Imams); the Jadd is the Lisan al-Hikmah (Tongue of Wisdom) and the Lisan al-Imamah, while the Lisan al-Shari'ah is the tongue of the law by which the soul is reformed.

The Third Intellect (third shibh / Second Emanation / al-tali), when he erred concerning the First Emanation and thought himself equal (masawat), had his supply (madda) cut off, his essence became dark, and he was distanced and became the Tenth ('ashir) in the horizon of the Ninth Intellect, after having been the Third.

The Tenth ('Ashir), seeing the decline of his rank while the nine spheres attained the second perfection, awoke from heedlessness (ghaflah), knew he had fallen into error, contemplated the cause, turned to the nearest (Ninth) Intellect supplicating, confessed his error, repented (taba), and humbled himself (anaba).

The 'Ashir's denial of his preceding limit (had al-sabiq) came from arrogance (istikbar) and ignorance; he sought intercession (tawassul) through all those preceding him to his Lord (the First Intellect) and sought forgiveness, whereupon all his sins were forgiven.

The abstract intellects showed kindness (hannat) to the 'Ashir and cast their rays upon him in mercy; the distant promises (mawa'id qusiyya) and higher supports (ta'yidat 'ulwiyya) connected with him, his essence shone totally, he was stripped of darkness into a luminous intellect, and he reached the second perfection (kamal al-thani) — attaining infallibility ('ismah) and stations of mercy.

The Qur'an 'O reassured soul, return to your Lord, well-pleased and well-pleasing; so enter among My servants and enter My Paradise' (ya ayyatuha al-nafs al-mutma'inna...) is spoken by the First Intellect (from the circle of oneness) and refers to the 'Ashir; the 'Paradise' (jannah) is the First Emanation's circle.

The 'Ashir is the spiritual Adam (Adam al-ruhani); the Qur'anic story of Adam refers to him, and 'Then Adam received words (kalimat) from his Lord and He relented toward him' means the kalimat are the seven abstract intellects whose intercession Adam received.

The First Intellect alone is the true Kalimah (Kalimatullah), who established the world by uttering the kalimat al-ikhlas before every speaker; the seven intellects are called 'kalimat' only metaphorically by attribution to him, just as the worlds of intellect, origination, and holiness are named by attribution to him.

The First Intellect has two worships: practical worship ('ibadah 'amaliyya) = uttering the kalimah/testimony (his testimony for his Originator in His origination), and gnostic worship ('ibadah 'ilmiyya) = what came into existence for him from his Originator's divinity and oneness (his thought); gnostic worship is more noble (ashraf), practical worship is lower (adwan).

The First Intellect surpasses the abstract intellects in virtue, nobility, splendor, and perfection by his precedence, action, worship, knowledge, and deed; however much they advance they cannot surpass the one above them, and Allah's treasures have no deficiency, so his joy and bounty keep increasing forever.

Those distanced by the 'Ashir's distance (a large group in his category) divided into three sects (firaq): the first negated divinity from itself and its kind and affirmed it for the Originator but erred regarding the First Emanation (like 'Ashir) — this is the spiritual Adam's spouse (zawj, Hawwa', his receptive faculty), per the Qur'an 'O Adam, dwell, you and your wife, in Paradise.'

The second sect affirmed the Originator but 'left' (denied the precedence of) the First Intellect and First Emanation, thinking themselves equal to them (masawat/mumathalah) — they remain in the first perfection and never enter the second.

The third sect established a da'wah in the abode of origination, denied, were arrogant, did not affirm the oneness of their Originator, and adhered to none of the intellects — claiming they created themselves from nothing; they are the most severe of the sects in disbelief (kufr) and the greatest in opposition and denial, and from this sect Iblis was born.

After the Tenth Intellect's repentance, the Originator obligated him to deliver (khalas) the three groups and tasked him, because he was a chief for them and a cause of some of their error — per the principle 'he who breaks a bone, upon him is its mending' (man kasara 'azman fa-'alayhi jabruhu).

The Tenth Intellect was established among the three groups in the station the First Intellect held in the world of origination, and was commanded to deliver them; he addressed them, but they refused, were rebuked and admonished, turned away in arrogance, increased in darkness, and so deserved descent (hubut), degradation (tasafful), and the fall (suqut).

The groups mixed together like accumulating clouds (sahab) and moved from their own selves with a first motion producing length (tul), beginning with heat/Aries (hamal) and ending in coldness/Libra (mizan) — creating four constellations: tali', hamal, gharib, mizan.

A second motion produced breadth ('ard), beginning with moisture/Capricorn (jady) and ending with Cancer (sartan)/dryness; a third motion sought to remedy themselves and produced depth ('umq) — all three motions by intentional divine grace ('inayat ilahiyya) directed by the Tenth Intellect.

The Tenth Intellect determined there was no deliverance for the fallen except through coming into Hanafiyyah human forms similar to the imaginal forms (since the human form is the best and noblest of forms), and that this requires the establishment of a da'wah similar to the original da'wah of origination — but, unlike the original, with place, time, great trial, and test (imtihan).

The wise say 'man is the first of thought and the last of action' (al-insan awwal al-fikr wa akhir al-'amal): through the test, that which has risen and is pure (taraffa'a wa safa) is separated and ascends, while that which remained base and harsh falls back (yartakisu).

When the accumulated/mixed matter formed, the more transparent and subtle part became the form (surah) and the more obscure and dense part became prime matter (hayula); divine grace made some an active instrument like the male (al-dhakar) — the world of spheres ('alam al-aflak) — and some passive like the female (al-untha) — the world of mothers ('alam al-ummahat).

When the three dimensions (length, breadth, depth) gathered in the form of the cross (salib), the spheres (aflak) were made from the purest of the mingled matter — and these spheres are the first group, which affirmed the Originator's oneness, glorified the First Intellect, sanctified it, and acknowledged its right.

The first group, when the Tenth Intellect addressed it along with the other two groups, insisted with their insistence (the equality view), was arrogant and descended with them, becoming dense and ignorant of subtleties — but at the moment of falling it became aware, regretted, and sought repentance; since full descent was no longer possible, it was made into spheres, stars (kawakib), and constellations (buruj).

From the two remaining groups (the polytheists and atheists, mushrikin wa mulhidin) the rest was extracted; the order of densities formed step by step (shay'an ba'da shay'in): first the sphere of the encompassing celestial sphere (falak al-aflak/muhit) of imaginary density (kasafat wahmiyya), then the sphere of constellations (denser), then the seven planetary spheres, then the four mothers (fire, air, water, earth).

The ordering of the world of spheres ('alam al-aflak) is like the gradual creation of man (thing after thing); the first thing acted upon (munfa'il) and formed from the spheres was the Sun (Shams), because it is connected to the heart of man (qalb al-insan) and is the center of innate heat (al-hararat al-ghariziyya).

The Sun is the center connected to the point of the compass (nuqtat al-barkar); innate heat is emitted from it to the three planets above it (Saturn/Zuhal, Jupiter/Mushtari, Mars/Mirrikh) and the three below it (Mercury/'Utarid, Venus/Zuhrah, Moon/Qamar) and the four mothers (ummahat); it is the origin of the first motion.

The encompassing sphere (falak al-muhit, the Atlas) is the most subtle, of conceptual/imaginary density, containing nothing; the sphere of constellations (falak al-buruj) holds all the fixed stars (which revolve in their own orbits), while the seven planets (sayyarah) revolve around the Sun as center.

The Sun is connected to the heart, the Moon (Qamar, center of moisture and coldness) to the head, and Saturn (Zuhal, center of coldness and dryness) to the two feet; the whole world of spheres became like a single body called the Absolute Body (al-jism al-mutlaq), the counterpart to the human body.

The encompassing sphere (falak al-muhit) was made a spirit (ruh) for the Absolute Body because it is the most subtle and noble; it is the mover (muharrik) of the Absolute Body and the very essence of space and foundation (al-makan wa al-usquss), turning the body every day and night with a single divine turn (qalabah ilahiyya).

The Sun follows the encompassing sphere in nobility and virtue because it was the first to repent and seek forgiveness (after the falak al-muhit) while in descent, and the first to glorify the First Intellect and declare Allah's oneness after the falak al-muhit; its radiant light filling heavens and earth was made as a reward for what it did.

The lights of the stars and zodiacal signs are each given according to what preceded from each (the measure of its repentance); the scale of justice (mizan al-'adl) is established, leaving neither small nor large thing without reward or punishment — what we see with the apparent eye is only the shell (sadaf).

After the lines of the cross formed, a center arose from accumulated matter at the meeting of length and width — the first depth ('umq al-awwal); there a splitting space (al-jaww al-munfaqih) formed in which temperament (mizaj) and the tempered (muntazij) became balanced, yielding eight temperaments (combinations of heat/cold with dryness/moisture).

The earth is the rock (sakhrah), the densest, darkest, and murkiest of all, formed from the third group (firqa-e-thalithah) which denied the creator, did not affirm the Originator's oneness, and adhered to no intellect; the four mothers (fire, air, water — the second group) and soil revolve around and above it.

The aflak groups map to the three sects: the spheres (falak al-muhit etc.) are the first group; the mothers — fire, air, water, earth — are the second group (believed in Allah but not the First Intellect/Emanation); the rock (sakhrah) is the third group (denied the creator).

When the sphere turned a conceptual revolution (dawra wahmiyya), all planets cast their rays on the rock but found no passage (the rock was stubborn and accepted nothing); a subtle smoke (dukhan latif) remained around the rock from the first group, kept distinct by intentional divine grace (the second intention from the 'Ashir).

When the planets' rays could not penetrate the rock they returned to their origins, and a portion of the subtle smoke (its own affinity) united with each ray, forming a shell (sadaf) for each planet; the rays-and-smoke together became the bodies (ajram) of those conceptual (wahmi) planets, which clothed them.

The 'alam al-aflak (world of light/nadimin/penitents) is composed of those who repented in the luminous world and became dense; the elements descend easily but rise with difficulty because the rock accepts nothing — the human's descent is upon the rock, from which he must make progress.

In a second, weaker motion the stars cast rays toward the rock, found no passage, and (being weaker than the first motion) were cut off before returning to their origins, stopping mid-way and mixing with the body of air; from this mixing the sphere of the breeze (kura-e-nasim, the breathable atmosphere, ~100 miles) formed — cool, moist, moderate — by which plants and animals have life.

The four mothers/elements (ummahat, called the pillars/arkan) are the second group: fire, air, water, earth; the breeze connecting to the earth's caves congealed into water, producing perpetual springs aided by spring-water and rain.

The world of substance ('alam al-jirm) and world of body ('alam al-jism) together are called the Absolute Body (al-jism al-mutlaq), where corporeality (jismaniyyat) began; collectively they are prime matter (hayula) and form (surah) — hayula being in reality the world of mothers (fire, air, water, earth) and surah being the world of spheres from the muhit to the moon.

The aflak are in the station of fathers (aba') and the ummahat in the station of wives/spouses (azwaj — four, as four wives are permitted in Shari'ah), and the offspring (awlad) born in the world are minerals (ma'dan), plants (nabat), and animals (hayawan).

The world of mothers is in reality the Greater Vegetative Soul (al-namiyat al-kubra), its limit being from the sphere of the moon to the center (of the rock); the world of spheres is the form (surah), called the fathers (aba') and in reality the Greater Sensitive Soul (al-hissiyat al-kubra), from the muhit to the sphere of the moon.

The sphere's first universal motion imparted intense heat and dryness near it, forming the sphere of fire (kurat al-nar / kurat al-athir, ether); a more distant, moderate heat with moisture formed the sphere of air (kurat al-hawa); when motion became distant and parts static, coldness and dryness formed the sphere of the frozen (kurat al-zamharir) — like waves around a swimmer, strongest near, motionless far.

When the mothers were arranged (called the pillars/arkan) and their smoke rose and mixed, every abstract intellect looked toward one sphere among the nine spheres (falak al-muhit, falak al-buruj, and seven planets); the First Intellect's attention was on the falak al-muhit, the second on the falak al-buruj, and so on — the tenth's attention on the earth, which is separate from the nine planets.

Divine providence made the seven planets the managers/arrangers (mudabbir) of the world of mothers and the generations (mawalid); the world of mothers is called the world of generation and corruption ('alam al-kawn wa al-fasad).

The whole arrangement of spheres, mothers, and rock exists for the rock (the earth) because man's descent is upon it; things descend easily from the spheres but cannot climb up from the rock (which accepts nothing) — man is in the world of mud, and the entire process is to enable his ascent.

The whole cosmic process unfolds in three divisions: first division = length, breadth, depth; second division = the shell (sadaf) was created; third division = the trenches/valleys (khudd) were created — all to enable the final creation (man) to be purified gradually through trials, which the original luminous world (without time-constraint) could not accomplish.

The seven planets were appointed managers (tadbir) of the world of generation and corruption, each for a duration of fifty-one thousand years and a little more (nif); their effects elevate the corrupt parts of the mothers so things ascend from falak to falak al-muhit, to the world of life, to the world of light — beginning purification.

Ascent to perfection proceeds through nested temples (haykal): preparation for the Millennial Resurrection (qiyamat al-alfiyyah) raises beings into the Sensible Divinity (lahut al-mahsus), then from haykal to haykal — Imam, Qa'im, Hujjat, Mawla — and finally from the world of life to the world of light ('alam al-nur).

The seven planets are: Zuhal (Saturn), Mushtari (Jupiter), Mirrikh (Mars), Shams (Sun), Zuhrah (Venus), 'Utarid (Mercury), Qamar (Moon); all are made from the penitent/repentant ones (nadimin/ta'ibin), but Zuhal and Mirrikh retained the quality of inauspiciousness (nuhusat) because their companions had listened to Iblis before repenting.

Governance began with Zuhal (Saturn) because it is the highest planet; its place was assigned for its coldness, dryness, inauspiciousness, and power of annihilation — its function is to demolish and level everything first (a demolition squad), which is its specific action, not its essence (it is itself a penitent/tawwab).

The entire world of spheres ('alam al-aflak) is of a fifth nature (tabi'atun khamisah) — a special combining nature from which the four natures (heat, dryness, moisture, coldness) emerged; each planet is associated by approximation with the action that issues from it.

Each planet's 51,000-year reign begins with 1,000 years of solitary governance (mufarrad), after which each remaining planet serves as its minister (wazir) for 1,000 years successively; Zuhal's first minister was Mushtari (saf'd al-akbar, softening dryness, sowing every praiseworthy thing via takhmir), then Mirrikh (generating coldness/dryness and the evil/vile things via takhannuth), ending with Qamar.

Takhmir is sowing/fermenting good things (placing seed-parts in the earth) and takhannuth is sowing corrupt/vile things; the cycle (dawr) of each planet completes 357,000 years plus 3,000 nif = 360,000 solar years (400,000 lunar), called the lesser cycle (kawr al-asghar).

A thousand years equals one day with Allah (per the Qur'anic measure); a person's spiritual manifestation in the luminous world ('alam nurani), where his pledge (bay'at) was taken, corresponds in time to his worldly manifestation — if not fully manifested in a thousand years, part of it definitely manifests.

The greatest cycle (kawr al-a'zam) is 360,000 (or 400,000 lunar) years multiplied by itself; after one kawr al-a'zam the bonds (magnetic pulls) of the spheres loosen — this is the total resurrection (qiyamat al-kulliyya), in which the entire world of things is annihilated while the falak al-muhit remains safe and continues governing.

At death, only vapors leave the body, but the subtle nafs and sensory soul (nafs hissi) ascend; the major dense part of a being remains and is gathered later through successive returns (karrat) — gathered with the Imam, then the Qa'im, then a greater Qa'im — the spirit (ruh) acting as a magnet drawing one's scattered parts together into a single unit.

At the end of a kawr, governance returns to the first sphere as the first form, after the devastation of all inhabitants of the earth's surface — fine and heavy clouds, snow, sleet, and severe cold spread (Zuhal's function) — fulfilling the Qur'an 'As We began the first creation, We shall bring it back; a promise upon Us.'

Resurrection (husayb) is initiated at the beginning of every kawr (not in the very first kawr, which was only preparation); 400,000 kawr al-a'zam make one death (mawt), and after each death a total governance (tadbir kulli) occurs in which the spheres' shells and constellations are transformed.

In Zuhal's solitary first millennium the world had severe cold, accumulated snow, light and heavy clouds, thick fog, abundant rains, the occurrence of mountains and stones, and atmospheric darkness; in the second millennium (Mushtari as minister) rains dried, stones and mountains broke, the atmosphere warmed, and the earth became a wet plain across the twelve islands.

In the third millennium (Mirrikh as Zuhal's minister) coldness and dryness generated whole crawling creatures of the earth (harashat), scorpions, snakes, geckos (wazagh), lizards (zab), Banat Wardan, locusts (jarad), and water creatures — produced as complete organisms, unlike the first-cycle fermentation (khamair).

Next came predatory animals (siba'), wolves (zi'ab), clawed and tusked beasts (the disobedient/arrogant, who tear apart), and every hard mineral originating from iron and copper — generated by the conjunction of the two inauspicious ones (Zuhal and Mirrikh), which are the two magnets most specific for the vile and base; iron and copper are why wearing them in prayer is forbidden.

Ra's and Dhanab (the two 'slow ones,' the jawzahar / 'uqdatayn, head and tail of the dragon) are imaginary calculations with no ascended physical body; they are parts of those who hastened in the 'Ashir's repentance then became most disobedient, so they were kept high (beneath the moon's sphere, near the two hujjats) rather than among the base, by special divine intent to preserve Allah's justice.

Ra's and Dhanab are the two opposites for the two worlds (earthly nature and the world of light), especially the enemies of the two luminaries (Shams and Qamar), causing the killings and vile things spread in the world; their effect on the sun and moon is the eclipses (kusuf and khusuf), and the dragon/tail (Dhanab) is more severe than Ra's.
The second surah of Kitab al-Anwar comprises five chapters, of which the first chapter contains five sections.

The term yajma'u ('it gathers') is morphologically distinguished: jama'a is transitive 'to gather,' tajamma'a (form tafa''ul) is the intransitive 'to be gathered,' and ajma'a 'to cause to be gathered' yields the noun ijma'.
When the third millennium was completed, Zuhal (Saturn) took up the administration of the fourth millennium accompanied by Shams (the Sun).
Zuhal (Saturn) administers a full grand cycle of 51,000 years, divided into successive thousand-year periods each accompanied by a different planet.
In the celestial-sphere correspondence, Shams (the Sun) occupies the station of the heart (qalb).
The Sun's qualities are heat (harara) and dryness (yubusa).
In the fourth millennium occurred the leavening (takhmir) of the kings, gold, and ruby — meaning their seeds were sown into the dimensional world though they were not yet born.
Four technical terms describe stages of coming-into-being: khamira (the seed being sown), tawallud (birth/generation), takwin (formation/development), and in'iqad (conception/coming-together).

Khamira (leaven) is analogized to sowing a seed in the earth, while tawallud (birth) is the seed growing into the tree — only the parts destined for the present sphere are born, the rest manifesting in later spheres.

The seed-of-action couplet ('Khuld se tukhm-i amal ban ke yahan aye the...') teaches that souls came from Paradise (khuld) as the sown seed of action, remain here as trees, and must travel onward as the flower's fragrance — the fragrance being the form and the sensory soul.
Hazrat Fazlullah Shah Mukarram habitually recited the couplet 'Bu-i gul ban ke abhi aur kahin jana hai' at the end of his discourses.
Takwin (formation) denotes progressive development: first the vegetative soul is formed, then the sensory soul, then the rational soul, advanced through knowledge and action.

In the Realm of Intentions ('alam al-niyyat), certain entities accumulated good deeds that generated kingly/ownership qualities, and the reward for those deeds is now received here as polity (siyasat), dominion, caliphate, and worldly comforts.
The leaven of kings came on earth because in this era Shams accompanied Zuhal, and Shams is the king among the celestial spheres.
Whereas an intention written in the Realm of Intentions is fixed like a mark on stone, the leavens (khamira) derived from a single intention continuously change and develop across successive spheres.
The intention made in one sphere becomes an action in that sphere, and that sphere's intention in turn becomes the action/administration of future spheres.
The one on the straight path (mustaqim al-sayr) must traverse 360,000 spheres (karrat), each sphere lasting one thousand years.
Before the soul's journey and manifestation, Allah prepared all necessary provisions for man, just as a traveler prepares supplies before a journey.
By the third millennium, under the Sun's ministry, the clouds and deep fog of Zuhal's early solitary period dissolved (tahallalat) and the atmosphere became clear (safa al-jaww).
A near warmth (sukhuna qariba) appeared alongside the intensity of cold — the cold belonging to Zuhal and the warmth arising from the ministry of Shams.

In the fourth millennium (Shams's accompaniment) the first small four-legged animals were born — such as rabbits, foxes, cats, and mice — and these are all forbidden (haram) animals because of Zuhal's accompaniment, no permissible animals existing yet.
Also in the fourth millennium the noble minerals (al-ma'adin al-sharifa) were formed — gold, silver, and transparent jewels of various kinds — until the fourth millennium ended.
Gold and silver were the origin of all minerals.
The transparent jewels include crystal (billor), carnelian (aqiq), ruby (yaqut), and emerald (zumurrud).
The predatory beasts (siba' al-dawari) and the like (e.g. dinosaurs) had not yet appeared and will only come in the first era of Zuhal.
In the fifth millennium Zuhal took up administration accompanied by Zuhra (Venus), an auspicious (sa'd) star.

In the fifth millennium moderate rains began at non-permanent intervals (unlike Zuhal's solitary era which had a continuous thousand-year rain or none), and nourishing (ghadhiya) winds blew though intensely cold.
In the fifth millennium plant life began: rivers flowed, trees grew, flowers and blossoms (azhar, anwar) opened, pure fragrances spread, and delicious-tasting fruits appeared.
Azhar (flowers) and anwar/nawr (buds/blossoms) are distinguished as flower versus bud.

In the fifth millennium were born the praiseworthy (mahmuda) and permissible-beneficial (muhallala nafi'a) animals — cattle, sheep/goats, horses, and camels — which are safe from evil and helpers to mankind.
The animals were born from caves (maghara), as later also the Dhu Sa'id al-Da'i and his parts would emerge from caves.
In the sixth millennium Zuhal took up administration accompanied by 'Utarid (Mercury) sharing in the administration.
In the sixth millennium the life-giving and nourishing winds that pollinate (mulqiha) plants and trees became numerous, and animals nourishing for human bodies multiplied.
Pollination (liqah) denotes the meeting of male and female (in plants and animals) from which a third thing is born.
Date palms require human-performed pollination because they do not self-pollinate.
Across the first four planetary thousand-year companions (Shams, Zuhra, 'Utarid) Zuhal remained the king but all its ministers were auspicious, so no harshness came from the ministers.
Jism (plural ajsam) and jasad (plural ajsad) are distinguished, with jism applying to the human body.
Every kind of animal and tree, whether permissible or forbidden, appeared as a prelude (muqaddaman) to the human species before man himself came.
After all else, the administration (tadbir) of man was then initiated.

Man's genesis began when a subtle, moderate vapor (bukhar latif mu'tadil) ascended from the purest, sweetest, most pleasant and most balanced of the sweet (non-saline) waters and seas, not from saline water.

The vapor for which permission was given (from the remnants of the males toward establishing physical forms) deserved its precedence because it had preceded in remorse (nadam) over its prior state while in the state of falling (inhidar).
When the command 'descend' was given a 'Big Bang' (inhidar) occurred, and whoever repented first in the state of falling had their parts manifest first and highest.
Adam al-Ibda'i (the Primordial Adam) belongs to the Realm of Life, while his veil/counterpart (hijab), the Dhu Sa'id al-Da'i, is the one who appears in the world.
The Prophet's name is Ahmad in heaven and Muhammad on earth, meaning Muhammad is the hijab (veil) of Ahmad.
From the ascended vapor a subtle cloud (sahab latif) formed, which propelled itself (indafa'a) as a light rain upon a land of pure soil.
The receiving land was pure soil: safe from every unpleasant taste, pure in color, of sound light dust, loose and uncompacted (mutakhalkhila), free of prior stickiness.
The pure land contained shallow (not deep) caves, and Allah set the standard of a grave for the great ones such as the Dhu Sa'id al-Da'i at no more than six cubits depth.
The water remaining in the caves was the like of a woman's semen (nazir mani al-imra'a), being the earlier water from snows and the rains of the preceding epochs that flowed in those caves.
The water springing from the earth (from earlier snows and rains) constituted the woman's part, while the rain descending now from the clouds constituted the man's part (the man's semen).

The two waters mixed in a complete mixing (imtizaj kulli), so that formation occurred in those caves just as the drop of semen (nutfa) is formed in the wombs — the caves themselves becoming wombs (arham).
An inner, earthly heat (harara batina ardiyya) from below then heated the mixture, just as the womb's heat acts upon the embryo.

At the moment of man's formation all the planets were in their houses of honor (buyut sharafiha), as if attending a wedding in their finest, and the Sun specifically was in the house of Aquarius (burj al-dalw), its most noble house.
Because the Sun was in Aquarius (its house of honor, with maximal heat-sending power), the inner earth was intensely hot (hamiyan) yet its heat was gentle and moderate (layyina mu'tadila).
The water repeatedly rose attracting heat, then upon meeting coldness became heavy and descended to its resting place, ceaselessly wavering up and down (mutaraddidan sa'idan wa munhadiran).

Through this repeated ascent and descent the water progressively densified and was acted upon bit by bit until it became an oily, moist, flowing, moderate substance — like a man's semen, completing the creation of the semen.
The birth/formation of the Dhu Sa'id al-Da'i occurred within Zuhal's 51,000-year grand cycle, specifically in the sixth millennium during the era of 'Utarid (Mercury).
The planetary companionship sequence of Zuhal's cycle is: Zuhal (alone), Shams, Zuhra, 'Utarid, Mushtari, Mirrikh, Qamar.
It is a common misconception that the creation of the Dhu Sa'id al-Da'i occurred in the era of Qamar; no book of the Da'wat Shareefa mentions Qamar — all mention 'Utarid.
The complete formation of the Dhu Sa'id al-Da'i occurs in the era of 'Utarid, and he emerges from the cave in the subsequent era of Qamar.
The 'thousand' (alf) in these accounts is understood not as a literal thousand years but as one epoch.
Pending any explicit statement from Mawla, the believer's conception must be based on the book: the birth of the Dhu Sa'id al-Da'i happened in the sixth millennium in the era of 'Utarid.

When the primordial water reached the state previously described and the sun entered the zodiac sign of Jauza, the air grew hot, the bawarih (hot summer winds) blew, and the earth's surface heated, causing the oil-like substance to dry and congeal.
Divine providence (al-inayat al-ilahiyyah) outlines and forms the human shape out of heat and cold as God wills.
Every star (kawkab) was placed in charge of forming a specific member of those primordial bodies.
The human form was engraved (naqasha surat al-insaniyyah) when the governance reached Utarid (Mercury) with the assistance of Zuhal (Saturn) and Qamar (the Moon).

The first man grew from the earth, rising from its place little by little like a fetus, seated with chin on knees and arms wrapped, as the Quran states 'Allah grew you from the earth as a [progressive] growth.'
The nafs al-namiya (vegetative soul) is what governs the being in the womb, and its center/origin is the moon (Qamar).
At birth into the world God blew into man a life-giving divine spirit (al-ruh al-muhyiyah) connected to the rays of the sun and moon, which is the nafs al-hissiyyah (sensory soul).

Amir al-Mu'minin Ali ibn Abi Talib, asked about the nafs al-hissiyyah, defined it as a celestial power (quwwah falakiyyah) whose origin is the celestial spheres, whose union with the body is at physical birth, whose seat is the heart, and whose action is sensation, movement, assault, and dominance.
The cause of the nafs al-hissiyyah's separation from the body is the disharmony of the four humoral materials (safra, sawda, balgham, damm), and on death it returns to the sun whence it began.
Each of the seven planets governs (tadbir) for 51,000 years in sequence beginning with Zuhal (Saturn), then Mushtari, Mirrikh, Shams, Zuhra, Utarid, and Qamar.

The creation/impression of the human form (naqsh surat al-insaniyyah) occurred in the governing cycle of Utarid with the companionship (murafaqat) of Zuhal and Qamar, after roughly 250,000-300,000 years of celestial revolutions.

The celestial revolutions before human creation are an uncounted period (fatrat) of preparatory arrangements for the Juz' al-Ibda'i; the dawr al-kashf is counted only from the beginning of human creation.
When man appeared, Zuhal began the governance of the seventh millennium (tadbir alf al-sabi') with the participation of Qamar.

Human forms appeared with the millennial stature in each of twelve islands (jaza'ir) according to the variety of their races: Arabs, Persians, Indians, Romans, Sindhis, Ethiopians, Berbers, Khazars, Zayalis, Slavs, Turks, Zanj, and others.

On the island of Sarandib (on the equator) many humans appeared, among whom twenty-eight individuals were the purest, most refined, most noble, and most perfect of all creation, the pinnacle of the human species.
The twenty-eight individuals correspond to the twenty-eight abjad letters (huruf al-mu'jam) and to the twenty-eight lunar mansions (manazil) of the moon's monthly cycle, to which they are attributed.

These first human individuals reached perfection of body, speech, and action without passing through ordinary maturation (ihtilam), turning their vision toward the Tenth (Ashir) with divine assistance.

The Ashir (Tenth) is the ancestor of the final ancestor, Adam al-Hayat, who carries out the governance, occupies the station opposite the First Intellect in the world of origination (alam al-ibda'), and is the place where the rays of the First Intellect fall.

The most virtuous single person among the twenty-two/twenty-eight individuals is, among the kingdoms, like the red ruby among mineral gems, pure gold among malleable bodies, the date palm among plants, and man among animals, yet more noble, subtle, and exalted than all.
This virtuous person is the quintessence (zubdah) and choicest of the two worlds, the celestial (jirmani) and the physical (jismani).

The first man, looking at himself, his kind, and the heavens, earth, stars, rivers, spheres, night and day, came to know by his own self that there is a Creator unlike them, negated divinity from all created existents, and affirmed it for their Originator alone, bearing witness to His oneness (wahdaniyyah).

Through this witnessing the man connected with the divine sources, the radiant lights, and the angelic supports, reached the second perfection (al-kamal al-thani), was supported, illumined, and made to know all the arts and what was and what will be (ma kana wa ma sayakun).

He stood in the world of bodies in the station of the First Intellect / Tenth Intellect, unique in the rank of oneness (wahdah), marked with origination (ibda'), and called the twenty-seven persons to the oneness of Allah (tawhid), purification (tanzih), and abstraction (tajrid).

He took confirmed covenants from them, taught them the lawful and forbidden, the rulings and laws, legislated the laws of religion (qawanin al-diyanah), and commanded them to marry forbidden women whom the sunnah made permissible so as to populate the world.

He chose sixteen persons: a Bab, a Hujjah, two da'is (da'i balagh and da'i mutlaq), and twelve made hujaj al-layl kept in his presence; the remaining eleven (and a twelfth in his own island) were stationed in the islands as preserved ranks until the end of time.

Each of the chosen ones was commanded to conduct the mission (da'wah) in his assigned island and given twelve hujaj al-nahar; these hujaj are free of the afflictions of falsehood and of veiling/deception owing to the loftiness of their ranks.

The twenty-eight individuals are the 'possessors of knowledge' (ulu al-'ilm) and people of witnessing whom Allah mentioned in 'Allah bears witness that there is no god but Him, as do the angels and the possessors of knowledge,' where Allah=First Intellect, angels=other intellects, and ulu al-'ilm=the twenty-eight.
key_terms: shahida Allahu annahu la ilaha illa huwa

teaching: The twenty-eight exist upon originating bodies (al-jasad al-ibda'iyyah) without procreation (bi-ghayri tanasul); their head, the negator-affirmer-unifier who established the shari'ah, is opposite the First Originator and learned tawhid without any teacher preceding him, by his own self.
With every Imam the twenty-eight individuals manifest: the Imam (Dhu'l-Sayf Da'iyah) with twenty-seven, and the Qa'im with twenty-eight; Allah established this pattern (naqsh) to recur perpetually.
Allah created the world in six days, and one day with Allah equals one thousand years, so creation occurred over six thousand years.

The kalimah 'La ilaha illa Allah' has twenty-eight letters/qualities and structures the ranks: nafi=Bab, ithbat=Dhu'l-Sayf Da'iyah, with the common letters and the four words mapping to the Imam's hierarchy.
Between the Originator and the originated is a Word (bayna al-mubdi' wa al-mubda' kalimah), the light of the kalimah 'La ilaha illa Allah,' which is higher than the First Originated.
The Pillar of Light (amud al-nur) is the knowledge flowing from Allah to the First Intellect, then through each successive intellect down to the Tenth Intellect, the governor of the world of nature.

Whoever connects with the Pillar of Light through the noble covenant (ahd al-sharif) attains success (fawz) and grace and becomes among the people of mercy; it is the strong rope of Allah and the firmest handhold (al-urwat al-wuthqa) that never breaks.
The Pillar of Light is spiritual, not physical light; it descends not upon the body but upon the rational soul (nafs natiqah), which is present at the time of the noble covenant.
The Pillar of Light is a magnet (maghnatis) that attracts the forms of the beneficiaries to the forms of the benefactors, holding and preserving their forms and souls after death.

From the hypocrite (munafiq), apostate (murtadd), and the one who incurs wrath (maghdub alayhi), the divine form connected to them is snatched away by the appropriate pillar, and their soul returns deficient and base into the body.

The Pillar of Light preserves and conveys to each person only the portion of food/sustenance (his ma'bar) destined for him, distinguishing it from others and extracting it from wherever it may be; this is divine providence and divine decree.
The Pillar of Light is reserved for those who take the noble covenant and possess wilayah (devotion), and the wilayah of Mawla Ali is necessary for it.

It is called the flowing knowledge, the pervading light, the spirit, and the Word; all forms of spiritual and physical existence from the First Intellect to the respondent are connected and joined to it, as in 'a person will be resurrected with whom he loves' (al-mar'u yuhsharu ma'a man ahabba).
The forms cling to the Pillar of Light like flies stuck to an extended stick smeared with honey, since it carries, attracts, and elevates them at the time of their ascent.

When one of the ranks or respondents has intimacy with his spouse, the divine forms turn away and deviate from him, returning only after completion (state of purity is restored by ghusl), as a kindness and mercy from Allah.
The Prophet said 'in every hair there is janabah' (fi kulli sha'ratin janabah), so one must wash every hair thoroughly in ghusl, and clothes worn during intimacy should not be worn for prayer.
Jibra'il is part of the Pillar of Light; the Natiq of the sixth era (Muhammad) at the beginning of his affair would faint from the greatness of the angel's light when he saw the form named Jibra'il.

The opponents and disbelievers mistook the Prophet's fainting (al-ghashyah) for jinn-possession or epilepsy (junna/sara'), while Waraqa bin Nawfal, a scholar and soothsayer awaiting the sixth Natiq, recognized it as prophethood.

Waraqa instructed Khadija to test the visitor: an angel (true Natiq's messenger) turns away from the private parts and would say 'I see nothing,' whereas a jinn would say 'yes' when the head/hair is uncovered.

Because angels do not look at private parts, a woman's prayer without covering her hair is not accepted; the same principle explains why Amr ibn al-As escaped death by uncovering his private parts before Ali at Siffin.
The Pillar of Light is cut off when private parts appear before it; the Prophet's connection (ittisal) with the Pillar of Light is established through Jibra'il.

The Quran alludes to the Pillar of Light in 'He sends down the Spirit (al-ruh) by His command upon whom He wills of His servants'; the Spirit (Pillar of Light) is the reality of revelation (haqiqat al-wahy).

Revelation flows in three modes per the verse 'It is not for any human that Allah should speak to him except by wahy, or from behind a veil, or by sending a messenger': these correspond to the ranks of Jadd, Fath, and Khayal.

Above every Imam (and Natiq, Prophet, Ayn Azimah, Wali) stand three higher ranks, Jadd, Fath, and Khayal, through which divine commands are conveyed; the rank of Jadd is the highest, flowing without intermediary from the Ruh al-Quds.
The rank of Fath is revelation 'from behind a veil' (min wara'i hijab): perception of things through pure thought and struck parables (amthal madrubah), conveying meaning in veiled, non-public form.
The rank of Khayal is the angel sent appearing as a well-proportioned man with power flowing from the Abode of Holiness (Dar al-Quds), perceived either as a heard voice or a form seen by the eye.
The flowing power connecting from Dar al-Quds is the limit flowing from Ruh al-Quds (the First Intellect), forming a luminous chain through which Khayal is heard or seen.

Sayyidna Ibrahim bin al-Husayn al-Hamidi, the second Da'i, at the passing of Sayyidna Ali bin al-Husayn said 'al-laqab al-sari ta'allaqa bi'l-jari' (the flowing title became attached to the flowing), indicating the deceased was drawn into the Pillar of Light.

When one connects with the flowing grace he appears to the people of bliss in the manifest presence, the gathering place of pure parts; when the number is fulfilled and the term reached, the next paradise (Abbasid dome) appears at the gate of the Imam's veil (Jannat al-Ma'wa).
The ascending rational soul (nafs natiqah) of one with a good end joins and connects its light/virtues to the Pillar of Light according to its portion.

The virtuous person (second ibda'iyyah) established his mission until he brought forth a son who deputizes in his place, designated al-inbi'ath (the Emanated), counterpart to himself who is designated al-ibda' (the Origination).

In the world of nature the second ibda'iyyah (at the Imam's rank) is the counterpart of the First Originated, and his son the first Emanated (munba'ith al-awwal); every rank thereafter is called ibda' and its extracted son inbi'ath.

After conferring the ruling of Imamate (nass) on his son, the virtuous person passes to the rank of the Tenth Intellect to govern the world of nature, remaining until one like himself succeeds him in that lofty station.

The intellects ascend successively: the Tenth passes with its subordinates to the rank of the Ninth, the Ninth to the Eighth, and so on up to the Second Intellect (Jannat al-Ma'wa), above which is only the First Intellect, the rank of oneness (Sidrat al-Muntaha) reachable by no other intellect.

All rewarded souls, spiritual and physical, ascend by this transition over the passing of cycles and aeons (adwar wa akwar), to which the Quran alludes in 'At the Lote-tree of the utmost boundary, near it is the Garden of Abode.'

The Prophet said of paradise: 'In paradise there is what no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and what has not occurred to the heart of a human,' for the greatness Allah prepared therein for His friends.
The Torah reports Allah saying 'Obey me, O son of Adam, I will make you like me: living, you will not die; mighty, you will not be humiliated; rich, you will not become poor.'

Only the Qa'im al-Qiyamah, who comes at the last mawr, can pass to the rank of the Tenth at a single stroke because he was originated standing in oneness like the First Originated, becoming the quintessence of all worlds.
All the lights of the speakers (nutaqa'), foundations (asas/usus), and Imams gather in the Qa'im al-Qiyamah; relative to him every station is a part and he is the whole (kull).

The son designated by nass establishes the mission, calls to the oneness of Allah for the salvation of souls drowned in the sea of primeval matter (hayula) and the prison of the physical world, then brings forth his successor and passes to the Tenth's horizon, his duties being only governing the physical world and appointing a successor.

Souls passing from each rank become stopped (mawquf) with their predecessor until their number completes and their period passes; this stopping-place is the barzakh, to which the Quran alludes: 'And behind them is a barzakh until the day they are resurrected.'
key_terms: wa min wara'ihim barzakhun ila yawmi yub'athun

teaching: The completion of their number is 124,000 forms (surahs) and their period is 7,000 years (the dawr al-kashf); upon completion their Qa'im, extracted from his father's mission, rises and the stopped stations in the barzakh connect with him.
key_terms: mi'ah wa arba'ah wa 'ishrun alf surah

teaching: Each of those stations becomes a limb of the Qa'im's luminous subtle structure (haykal nurani latif), his subtle self being to them like the spirit to the body, so together they form one luminous divine structure and he becomes a holy abstract divine intellect.

The Natiq of the cycle said 'Indeed for Allah there are 124,000 prophets,' alluding to this noble great structure, and the Quran alludes in 'Say: indeed the first and the last will surely be gathered for the appointed time of a known day.'
key_terms: mi'ah wa arba'ah wa 'ishrun alf nabiyyin
qul inna al-awwalina wa al-akhirina la-majmu'un

teaching: The 'known day' is the dawr al-kashf, which is 50,000 years, as the Quran says 'in a day whose measure is fifty thousand years'; at the rising of this Qa'im the reckoning, reward, and punishment occur before him.
key_terms: fi yawmin kana miqdaruhu khamsina alf sanah

teaching: Upon completion of every 7,000 years a Qa'im arises like the previous one, continuing until the completion of 50,000 years (the seven Qa'ims of the dawr al-kashf).

The governance (tadbir) of the primordial body (jussa ibda'iyyah) of the first mawr extends over the entire kawr, including all natural laws and even partial phenomena like viruses and plagues, which are corrupted particles drawn to one by magnetic affinity from a prior connection.
Allah forgives His own due (sins against Him), but debts and wrongs between servants must be settled by the servants themselves or compensated through other means.

When the seventh Qa'im of the dawr al-kashf rises he has power, honor, and grace not possessed by the preceding six, gathering all six Qa'ims with him, since he stands for them in the station of the 'other creation' (khalq al-akhar) which is the spirit to the body and the culmination of the dawr al-kashf.

Upon the seventh Qa'im's passing the dawr al-sitr begins; his son rises after him, weakness (du'f) enters the mission, the dawr al-kashf reaches its term, and the mission goes into concealment (tasattur), known only secretly among its people through symbols and indications.

In the dawr al-sitr no apparent knowledge exists except mathematical sciences (engineering, astronomy, and the like), the Imams are in extreme taqiyyah and concealment, and the hands of opponents are dominant for the first 3,000 years.

The first of the concealment-cycle (mutaqa'idi dawr al-sitr) was Adam (the mustawda' Adam, Abdullah bin Tayjun), established as Natiq by the command of his Imam (Hunayd), each Natiq governing by the command of the Imam of his time.

Each Natiq establishes laws and a shari'ah whose outward rites are symbols pointing to knowledge of God's spiritual and physical limits (hudud) and His oneness, and appoints a wasi/asas to interpret the inner meaning, the Imamate continuing in succession.

The succession of Natiqs in the dawr al-sitr: Adam (opponent unnamed), Nuh (Imam Hud, opponent Awj bin Unaq), Ibrahim (Imam Salih, opponent Namrud bin Kan'an), Musa (Imam Ud bin Udad, opponent Fir'awn), Isa (Imam Khuzayma), and Muhammad (Imam Abu Talib, opponents Abu Lahab and Abu Jahl).
Every prophet has an opponent (zidd/enemy), as the Prophet said, since every light has a shadow.
