Tawhid, tanzih, and tajrid are distinct: tawhid is recognizing the createdness of all hudud, tanzih is purifying Allah from all attributes and names, and tajrid is abstracting the state of ibda' from all creatures (a state none can perform).

The wasis of the Natiqs: Adam's was Shith (after Habil), Nuh's was Sam, Ibrahim's was Isma'il, Musa's was Harun, Isa's was Sham'un al-Safa, and Muhammad's was Ali ibn Abi Talib, who designated Hasan as mustawda' and Husayn as mustaqarr.
Basis of precedence (awwaliyyat) is not the light but who reaches the homeland (watan) first; despite Natiqs being established first but appearing later, the first remains first.

The line of Imams ran to Muhammad ibn Isma'il (the seventh, Natiq al-Sadis), then the a'immat al-khulafa' beginning with Abdullah ibn Muhammad ibn Isma'il, completing with al-Mu'izz li-Din-illah; then the dawr al-ashhad beginning with al-Aziz billah, completing with al-Imam al-Tayyib Abi'l-Qasim; then the a'immat al-abdal beginning with the son of al-Tayyib.
Muhammad ibn Isma'il is the Natiq al-Sadis and gatherer of the six nutaqa'; his rank is very high and his lights are acquired from the Prophet's horizon, from Imam Hasan and Imam Husayn.

In the Tayyibi era 'Bismillah al-Rahman al-Rahim' is interpreted of the Imams: Allah=Muhammad ibn Isma'il, the ism=Imam al-Tayyib (21st Imam), and al-Rahman al-Rahim=Ma'add (14th Imam al-Mu'izz) and Ma'add (28th Imam Ahmad).
After al-Tayyib's line, the Hujjah of the Qa'im al-Qiyamah rises and the 7,000 years of the dawr al-sitr (the dunya) complete, as the Natiq said 'the age of the dunya is 7,000 years.'

The book Anwaar al-Latifah was copied by Sayyidna Da'ud bin Ahmad, the first mansub (buried in Ahmedabad), who marked two places where Sayyidna Ja'far derived proofs (hujjat) by istimbat from the original text.

The original Natiq al-Sabi' is the Qa'im al-Qiyamah who gathers all six nutaqa'; but because Muhammad ibn Isma'il's rank rose to hijabiyyah (the veil of Ayn Azimah), higher than Natiq al-Sabi', the point of that rank was conferred upon him.
The Prophet's final station is hijabiyyah (the maqam mahmud), the veil of Ayn Azimah, giving him superiority over all mustawda' and mustaqarr Imams up to the Qa'im.

The noble stations connect with the Qa'im as the gathered forms near the Bab (bab al-abwab) connect with the soul of the born Imam, his soul becoming a spirit (ruh) for them and forming one luminous structure and holy intellect.

All people of the dawr al-sitr, first and last, are gathered to the Qa'im, who takes account of each, makes them stand upon their deeds, and personifies every Imam with the people of his cycle, per 'the prophets and witnesses will be brought forward and judged with justice.'
key_terms: qul inna al-awwalina wa al-akhirina la-majmu'un

teaching: The believer will be shown a record (kitab) accounting every small and great deed ('what is this book that leaves neither small nor great but has accounted for it'), and the Qa'im is the Lord who rewards and punishes, the total reward and punishment being established before him.
key_terms: ma li hadha al-kitab la yughadiru saghiratan

teaching: Accepted supplications (du'a) in this world are recompensed in the world; supplications not accepted are stored and rewarded at the reckoning, leading the believer to wish that none of his prayers had been hastened ('layta innaka lam tu'ajjil li shay'an').
key_terms: layta innaka lam tu'ajjil li shay'an

teaching: Every rank (Imam, Bab, Hujjah, Da'i, Ma'dhun) is a partial (juzwi) Qa'im al-Qiyamah for those who return to it, while the rank above is its universal (kulli) Qa'im, ascending until all reach the Qa'im of the entire resurrection, master of the greatest resurrection (qiyamat al-uzma) and the greatest seizure (batshat al-kubra).

The perfected form (the luminous intellect / haykal nafsani) is prepared in 7,000 years in the dawr al-kashf (where there is purity and openly manifested wisdom-sciences), whereas the Qa'im al-Qiyamah's form takes 10,000 years in the dawr al-sitr due to density, doubts, turbidity, and abundance of trials.

In the dawr al-kashf a Qa'im (qiyamah) occurs every 7,000 years (seven Qa'ims), but in the dawr al-sitr one Qa'im comes after 10,000 years (the 7,000 of sitr plus the 3,000 of fatrat), because the 3,000 fatrat years belong to the domain of dawr al-sitr thought.

Wiping the hand over the face after Bismillah signifies connecting the five lower (adwan) ranks with the five higher (ashraf) ranks; the face's five (intellect, soul, jadd, fath, khayal) are non-repeated (achieved second perfection), while the hands' fives are repeated (manifested in the world: Imam, Bab, Hujjah, Da'i, Ma'dhun).

All points appearing until the universal resurrection are present in the primordial initial body (jussa ibda'iyyah) of the first mawr; their manifestation occurs in appointed time, and the one holding the mawr governs its qawr until he prepares a successor like himself, whereupon he is elevated.

When the Imam manifests in the world of intention his Bab manifests with him in a dual capacity (qiran), and ranks subordinate to the Qa'im (jadd, fath, khayal, and his physical kin such as Abd al-Muttalib, Abu Talib, mothers) correspond as a reflection of the original assigned points.

Man's existence is from two ways: as a plant grown from the earth and through inter-marriage/lineage (munakahat), per 'Allah grew you from the earth as a plant' and 'We created man from an extract of clay, then made him a drop in a firm resting place.'

The formal apparitions (ashbah suwariyyah), having fallen into the three dimensions through their slip and error, became distant, dense, and turbid; divine providence dispersed (tabdid) them into the spheres and elements to purify them through trials, as gold is purified by fire.

After punishment and trial, divine providence gathers what was prepared and manifests it as the gnostic human form (qamat al-arafiyyah) from the earth as a plant, then by a second, faster, closer way encompasses the three kingdoms (mineral, plant, animal) as food.

The primordial body eats these foods, taking the subtle and discarding the dense, making them flesh and blood combining the four natures (the four humors); the body so formed is a physical veil over the primordial body.

At intimacy between man and woman the subtlest extract descends from both bodies, ascends to the brain to be refined and whitened (from dense blood drawn from every organ), then descends from both into the womb to become a single entity gathering the four natures.

Within that single entity is a complete vegetative life hidden like fire in flint-wood, named tabi'ah, the primordial leaven (khamirah ibda'iyyah), the vegetative soul (nafs namiyyah), and the (growing) form (surah).

When the entity is balanced in temperament and given permission to manifest, it settles in the pure balanced womb, faced by the ascendant, descendant, tenth, and fourth astrological houses by the decree of the cosmos, fermenting like rennet and milk becoming cheese.

The first organ formed from the drop (nutfah) is the heart (the point of the compass, nuqtat al-birkar), whose nature is the sun's action (heat and dryness); it attracts the subtle entity and becomes its house and center, after which the remaining organs form.

The fathers (planets/kawakib) act upon the forming organs and the mothers (wombs/spheres) nurse them; each organ receives its share of nourishment through its mother's corresponding organ, missing nothing.

The sun, heart of the celestial sphere, provides aid to what is above and below it step by step; likewise the sun of the world of religion, the Natiq, gives the divine sciences and angelic confirmations to the hudud above and below him.

Each of the seven planets governs (tadbir) the fetus for one month in sequence (Zuhal, Mushtari, Mirrikh, Shams, Zuhra, Utarid, Qamar), so it is born complete in the seventh month under the moon's governance.
The heart's formation and movement occur in the fourth month under the sun's (Shams) governance, which is why the fetal heartbeat is felt then.

If the child is not born in the seventh month it remains until the eighth, when governance returns to Zuhal (the inauspicious star, nahs al-falak) whose action is coldness and dryness (the nature of death), so a child born in the eighth month appears dead.

If the child remains until the ninth month it comes under Mushtari (the greater good fortune, sa'd al-akbar) whose action is heat and moisture (the nature of life), so it is born alive; the nayyirayn are Shams and Qamar, the sa'dayn are Mushtari and Zuhra, and Utarid is the scribe of the sphere (katib al-falak).

Amir al-Mu'minin Ali defined the nafs al-namiyya (vegetative soul) as a natural power (quwwah tabi'iyyah) whose origin is the four natures, whose union is at the deposit of the drop, whose substance is from refined foods, whose action is growth and increase, and whose separation is caused by disharmony of materials, returning to the moon whence it began.

Everything beneath the sphere of the moon down to the point of the earth (the rock, sakhrah) is the Greater Vegetative Soul (namiyyat al-kubra), from which every lesser vegetative soul branches; the lesser vegetative soul is in reality the animal (hayawan).

The Greater Sensory Soul (hissiyyat al-kubra) extends from the encompassing sphere (muhit) to the sphere of the moon; the lesser sensory soul (hissiyyat al-sughra) is the rational obligated human soul; the greater rational souls are the Hudud, and the lesser rational soul is the respondent (mustajib).

These realities were never disclosed except by allusion (ramz) and from a tongue to an ear, but the author wrote them plainly without symbol or ta'wil at the questioner's request, in the language of haqa'iq.

When the newborn appears into the expanse of the earth a sensory power connects with it from the rays of the sun (heart of the sphere, center of the sensory), spreading through the body, sending movement, and uniting with the vegetative soul to become one thing nourished by the temperate breeze (nasim).

Ali defined the nafs al-hissiyya as a celestial power (quwwah falakiyyah) whose origin is the spheres, union at physical birth, seat the heart, action sensation/movement/assault/victory, separation by disharmony of materials, returning to the sun whence it began.

Sayyidna al-Mu'ayyad (Hibatullah ibn Musa al-Shirazi, Bab al-Abwab) in his Majalis admonished: 'I wish I knew why you were drawn out from the spheres and bodies and made to descend stage by stage into the narrow places of the loins and wombs and brought out into the expanse of this abode.'

The nutfah enfolds the vegetative soul drawn from terrestrial nourishment of the three kingdoms (mineral, plant, animal), which is drawn from the four mothers (fire, air, water, earth), and these four mothers are the powers of the celestial spheres.

Allah created only spiritual essences (zawat ruhaniyya / ashbah nuraniyya), granting them existence, knowledge, life, and choice (ikhtiyar); those who misused their choice fell stage by stage into nufus, then sensory and vegetative souls, then bodies, animals, plants, and minerals, all being fallen spiritual essences.

Salvation (najat) is the return of all things to being luminous specters (ashbah nuraniyya); the units of a person's various fallen parts are held by the Governor (Mudabbir) and gathered at the Qa'im, then at greater Qa'ims, ascending ultimately toward the Ashir and the Jannat al-Ma'wa, none reaching Sidrat al-Muntaha.

God created the essences in the human form (shukhusan ala shakli al-insan) before man existed; the one who arrived first occupies the station of the heart/head and the one who came last the station of the feet, and they ascend in that same human-form arrangement.

The human form has 28 parts corresponding to the 28 letters of 'La ilaha illa Allah': the head is 'illa Allah,' the body is 'La ilaha,' with three parts, four parts, seven parts, and twelve apertures (eyes, ears, nostrils, mouth, nipples, navel, chest openings, lower orifices).

Sayyidna al-Mu'ayyad in Taj al-Aqa'id refutes that God created out of need, to take work, or to be worshipped, concluding that the cause of creation is unknowable except that God by His grace (fadl) and kindness brought existence from non-existence.
The newborn learns speech from its parents through babbling (munaghat) until its speech matures, and learning the Book of Allah increases its speech and perfection.

When the person connects with the true teacher (mu'allim al-sadiq), is given longing to enter the circle of the people of truth, takes the noble covenant (ahd al-karim) through the Imam of the time, and enters the secure sanctuary of Allah, a point of light neighbors his soul and connects with the Pillar of Light flowing from the Imam of the time.

The more one benefits from the knowledge, gnosis, and love of the Imam and his hudud and walks in chastity, purity, and obedience to the Wali al-Amr, the more the point of light increases in vastness and light and the soul's illumination and substance increase.

The luminous point is a form (surah) which is the rational soul (nafs natiqah) imaged by the beneficiary from his benefactor; Ali defined it as an intellectual power (quwwah ilmiyyah), a transparent substance knowing in potentiality and actuality, living by nature.

Once the nafs natiqah is formed it cannot be destroyed, per the principle 'evil has no origin in the primary creation' (al-sharr la asla lahu fi'l-ibda'): evil, lying, darkness, and coarseness are not things but the absence/distance from good, truth, light, and subtlety.

Allah created only truth and sustenance; man himself created the body and turned sustenance into excretions and falsehood, so man is the cause of his own coarseness, which is removed by progressing on the path.

The spirit (ruh) is 'from the command of my Lord' (qul al-ruhu min amri rabbi); ruh is also used for the nafs natiqah, and when the nafs natiqah ascends high the command of the Lord (amr-i rabb) is at work.
The subtle nafs natiqah, by abiding with the coarse nafs hissiyya, gradually transforms it into itself, which is salvation, as a stone takes on fragrance from prolonged company with perfume.

Ali defined the nafs al-kulliyyah (Universal Soul) as a divine power (quwwah ilahiyyah), a widespread substance knowing in potentiality and actuality, whose origin is the (First) Intellect, from which it takes support and toward which it calls, its union being at the religious birth (ahd al-sharif) and its seat being knowledge and reality.

Each soul returns to its origin: the nafs namiyya to the moon, the nafs hissiyya to the sun, the nafs natiqah to the Pillar of Light / world of life, and the nafs al-kulliyyah to the Intellect / world of lights; the lower's origin is always the rank above it.

The nafs al-kulliyyah is the supreme Word of Allah (kalimatullah al-ulya), the tree of Tuba (shajarat al-tuba), and the Garden of Abode (Jannat al-Ma'wa) near the Sidrat al-Muntaha (the First Intellect); whoever knows it precedes and is saved, whoever is ignorant of it is misguided.

Every station in the world of religion corresponds to the First Intellect (named Sidrat al-Muntaha) and every Imam to it; the Bab corresponds to the First Emanated (muba'ath al-awwal, named Jannat al-Ma'wa), so Ali alluded to the Bab by the nafs al-kulliyyah and to Jannat al-Ma'wa by the muba'ath al-awwal.
The Pillar of Light flows from the Bab to the Hujjah, to the Da'i, to the Ma'dhun, to the believer (mu'min), and to the respondent (mustajib) who takes the noble covenant.

Ali ibn Abi Talib founded Arabic grammar by explaining to Abu'l-Aswad al-Du'ali that the 28 letters form meaningful words (kalimah) of three kinds, ism (noun), fi'l (verb), and harf (particle), corresponding to luminous essences, their intentions, and the relation between them.

The grammatical rules mirror the luminous world: every subject (fa'il) is raised (marfu') because it acts and advances foremost, every object (maf'ul) is established (mansub), and every preposition-governed noun (majrur) is broken (maksur).

Arabic is the original, still-existing language because the foundation of 'La ilaha illa Allah' rests on its 28 letters, which encode all the laws, and Allah revealed the Quran in 'a clear Arabic tongue.'

At the time of a respondent's departure, the Tenth Intellect (receiving the command, linked to the Imam) moves the Pillar of Light named 'the flowing' (al-jari), and the movement connects to the Imam of the time, who knows it signals the soul's purification and time of transfer.

The Imam moves the Pillar of Light and attracts the departing one toward himself; the luminous form (nafs natiqah) is drawn by the pillar's attraction, and the neighboring sensory soul (nafs hissiyya) is drawn along with it to the extent it obeyed the rational soul in the world, in the form of the universal body, leaving nothing small or great.

Souls cannot pass through the regions of heaven and earth except by an authority (sultan), which is the noble form (haykal) of the Imam where all forms gather, per 'you will not pass through except by an authority.'
The first chapter of Mabda' wa-Ma'ad contains five principles, with the sixth being a debate and the seventh expounding the reality of the fifth.
At the moment the sensory soul (nafs-e-hissiyah) is drawn out of its body, it mixes (tamtaziju) and merges with its spiritual form and becomes connected to the rational soul (natiqah).
After this merging the soul and its form become one single thing, one essence, and a radiant, angelic, Gabrielic light (nuran sha'sha'aniyan malakutiyan jibriliyan).
In life the soul and its form are merely adjacent (mujawir) while in death they become intermixed (mumazij) — a major difference.
The departing soul becomes a luminous substance (jawhar-e-nurani) that is living, powerful, knowing, speaking, hearing, seeing, smelling, and tasting — these being the qualities of the sensory soul.
The substance is called luminous because it has become one with the rational soul (nafs-e-natiqah), the qualities of the natiqah having entered it.
Once the soul separates, the body remains a corpse devoid of perception and feeling, because all its powers (life, light, power, knowledge, speech) were due to the soul.
Only the soul and form of one whose end was good (khatima bil-khayr, on the Sirat al-Mustaqim) become pure; the process described applies to such a purified, righteous soul.
The purified lower soul-and-form unite and then intermix with the higher luminous form of their Exalted Limit (hadde aali), becoming one essence with it while remaining adjacent to its sensory soul.
The Exalted Limit (hadde aali) does not die but remains alive, so the believer's purified soul attaches to a living higher being.

The Arabic poetic line about the sun (shams) being grammatically feminine and the moon (qamar) masculine illustrates that grammatical gender does not diminish the sun's superiority, since the sun's rays make the moon luminous.

The moon gathers little by little the aeolian souls (nufus-e-rihiyyah) carried in the sun's light, and the moon of the fourteenth night's brilliant fullness is the result of this accumulated light from those souls.
The aeolian souls (nufus-e-rihiyyah) initially carry impurities (kudurat); the moon's early dense light comes from these impure souls, and purification then progressively increases their luminosity.
Fasting on the white nights (ayyam al-biz: the 13th, 14th, and 15th) is recommended (mustahabb).
After the full moon the moon returns the subtle vapor (bukhar-e-latif / nufus-e-rihiyyah) to the sun bit by bit (shay'an ba'da shay'in) via the stations of Mercury ('utarid) and Venus (zuhra).
The celestial ordering from lowest to highest is moon, then Venus, then Mercury, then the sun.

The bodily corporeality (jismaniyyat) acquired by the aeolian souls during burial with the body is what is purified through the planetary stations, the heat removing accumulated denseness like cleaning trash from a house.
Instead of hellfire's heat, the souls being purified are given the sun's heat, though hell's heat is a thousand times greater.
The lunar cycle is mapped to ascent and descent: from the 1st to the 12th is ascending, the 15th is the zenith (intila'), and from the 16th the vapors are delivered down to the world.

When the aeolian souls reach the precinct (hayyiz) of the sun, the sun's light is the quintessence (khulasa) of the heat of the subtle instinctive bodies (ajsam-e-ghariziyyah), serving as vehicle and spouse of sensory life and center of the instinctive heat (hararat-e-ghariziyyah).
The sun refines the souls by making them sweat ('araq), breaking them down, and fermenting them until they are fit for the door of the totality of subtle, spiritual, noble forms.

The sun delivers the purified whole up to Jupiter (mushtari), the Greater Fortune (Sa'd al-Akbar), and to Venus (zuhra), the Lesser Fortune (Sa'd al-Asghar), Mercury being the scribe of the heavens (katib-e-falak), until it is a pure vessel prepared for the command of the Imam.

The rays of the two Fortunes deposit the purified spiritualities onto fruits eaten or waters drunk (like dew) that become the food of the Imam, the moon, and the sun, guarded by divine providence until it reaches the Near Station (maqam-e-qarib).

The Prophet's birth is said to have come from the apple of paradise or from a spring of water (dew) divinely indicated to be drunk, after which he was born from Sayyidatuna Amina as the Seal of the Messengers (khatim-ul-mursalin).
The Imam of the Time (Master of the Era and the 'asr) and his pure spouse take the descended subtle vapor as their food, and from it the wife's purified quintessence (sulalah) forms.
Sulalah denotes the purified parts placed in the father's loins and the mother's womb; when both combine a nutfah (sperm-drop) is formed, this being the stage of sulalah.
At the moment of conception the Imam (the Station) knows by Allah's decree the reality of the coming child and is filled with indescribable joy.
At that time the Imam gives good tidings of the coming successor to the deputy of the station who will succeed and return to him, alluding to the child's matter.
The deputies of deputies are gathered with the purified matter so it becomes a single whole ascending in ranks, from which the fetus's food is made and on which it feeds and grows in the womb.
The Imam's body in the womb is nourished not by menstrual blood but by the pure purified aeolian whole, making it free from the impurity (tams) that affects other fetuses.

The verse 'Indeed Allah desires to remove all impurity from you, O People of the House, and to purify you' (Innama yuridu-Llahu liyudhhiba 'ankumu-r-rijsa Ahl al-Bayt wa-yutahhirakum tathira) is cited as scriptural proof of the Ahl al-Bayt's freedom from impurity.
Membership in the Ahl al-Bayt requires being free from the impurity of tams (menstrual-blood nourishment) and not consuming the wealth of charity (sadaqah).

The hadith 'sadaqah is not permissible for the Ahl al-Bayt' (sadaqatun la tahillu li-Ahl al-Bayt) is anchored to the Prophet removing a date from young Imam Hasan's mouth, demonstrating the prohibition.
The Prophet's wives claimed Ahl al-Bayt status yet consumed sadaqah (and 'Aisha demanded treasury wealth), so by the sadaqah criterion they cannot be reconciled with true Ahl al-Bayt membership.

A believer's purified growth-soul (nafs-e-namiyyah) and sensory-soul (nafs-e-hissiyyah) go into the Imam and meet his rational, growth, and sensory souls; the believer's part becomes the spirit (ruh / nasut) from which the Imam's son's body is formed.

Upon the begetting of the Imam's son three streams — the believer's growth-soul, sensory-soul, and form (surah) — converge and gather in one ocean and connect with the nasut, having been separated only so they could reunite.

The order of ascent of the believer's faculties is: the rational soul (nafs-e-natiqah) first and most superior, then the sensory soul (nafs-e-hissiyyah), while the growth soul (nafs-e-namiyyah), having a defect, ascends later through perfection.

Whereas a human body's parts are fire, air, water, and earth, the Imam's son's body is formed from the growth-souls (nufus-e-namiyyah), and its growth-soul is the single most subtle part ascended from the entire universe.
On the fourth month the growth-soul (nafs-e-namiyyah) — the most subtle ascended part — is obtained from the sun and connects with the developing whole, becoming its nafs.

When the whole completes its term in the womb a complete, knowing, powerful, subtle, transparent man appears with the five senses, a noble disembodied (mujarrad) substance (jawhar-e-latif) whose faculties are pure.

The believer's parts are already fully processed and purified in the celestial spheres before entering the Imam's nasut; the purification process ends there, with only give-and-take continuing once in the world.
When the born one (mawlud) reaches the four years of upbringing (sini al-tarbiyah), the inner gate (baab-e-baatin) of his father transfers to him.
Grammatically, 'iza' before a past-tense verb conveys present-tense meaning, and sini (from sinin, original sanun) drops its final nun because it is in genitive construct (mudaf ilayh).

The baab is appointed by the Imam (the son's father); the father has two gates — an outer gate (baab-e-zaahir) connected to the inner gate (baab-e-baatin), and the inner gate connected to the Imam's son.

The son of the Imam has no baab-ul-abwaab of his own; instead his heart (qalb) becomes a temple (haykal), and the father's baab-ul-abwaab with its gathered forms (suwar) and souls (nufus) becomes connected to him.
It is a general rule (kulliyah) that the baab's transfer and the gathered forms and souls (al-mustakhrajah) connect to the soul of the born one, who is thereby the Imam.
From birth an Imam is an Imam, but the general rule is that designation (nass) — which may be manifest (jali) or hidden (khafi) — usually occurs upon the Imam's son at four years of age.

When the son becomes the Imam of the Time (Imam-e-Zamana) his father's rank is elevated, and the new Imam gradually takes charge with jadhb (attraction), fath (opening), khayal (imagination), and all ishraqat (illuminations).

The Prophet's saying 'Al-Hasan and Al-Husayn are two Imams whether they rise or sit' (Al-Hasanu wal-Husaynu imamaani qaama aw qa'ada) was said when they were around four years old, evidencing the four-year connection of their special forms and gates.
The gathered forms and souls become a thousandfold luminous human glorious structure (haykal al-alfi an-nurani al-insani), and the Imam's soul becomes the spirit (ruh) for this haykal.
The haykal of gathered forms is the lahut, which connects with the nasut (the mawlud descended from the moon); lahut is the forms-and-souls (suwarat wa nufus) and nasut is the born body.

In the haykal the luminous human form is constituted in the shape of a body (hay'at al-jism) with all limbs, nerves, veins, instruments, head, eye, ear, nose, mouth, hand, and foot — made of luminous apparitions (ashbah nurani).
Each form moving in the haykal and its attracting sensory soul (nafs-e-hissiyah) are one and the same thing and one kind upon the form of the body, leaving out nothing small or large.

Due to the gathering of the insights (basa'ir) of the brothers (ikhwan) in the noble luminous assembly, each soul's life, strength, power, knowledge, sharpness, intelligence, hearing, and sight become many times greater than in its singularity.

The one who makes that spirit flow through all of them is the soul of the designated Imam (al-mansus 'alayhi), and their reaching that high rank is the paradise (jannah) of this world attained in the haykal.

The divine light's connection with these souls is a total connection (ittisalan kulliyan), and the connection of the subtle entities with the soul of the Imam occurs after the completion of four years because religion is a support for the heart (ad-dini da'amatan lil-qalb).

A seeker of proof (mustadill) is only called a mustadill after knowing the Speaker (Naatiq), the Legatee (Wasi), the Imam of the Age (Imam al-'Asr), and the Proof (Hujjah) — the four things taught first in the religious sciences (haqaiq), also stated after four years.

Each of the four ranks (hudud al-arba'ah) is attributed to one year of the four, so the connection of the subtle entities cannot occur except after the completion of four years, named the age of upbringing (sinn al-tarbiyah).
The exotericists (Ahl al-Zahir) do not pronounce a ruling on a newborn's age until at least four years have passed, which they too name the years of upbringing.
The prophet who brought the science of the stars ('ilm an-nujum) was Idris, peace be upon him, and his establishing it was a miracle (mu'jizah) for the people of his time.
Idris devised the science of the stars because he lived in a time of precautionary dissimulation and concealment (taqiyyah wa sitr).

When the Imam of Idris's time died having willed the Imamate to Idris, the people did not accept it; Idris argued that Allah's justice cannot leave His earth empty of His Proof (Hujjah), and they agreed.

Idris taught the people astronomy and had them repeatedly divide the earth into quarters (arba'an), each time finding God's gaze upon the quarter they were in, until the division led to Idris himself, whom they then acknowledged as the Proof and witness of God.

A narration of Amir al-Mu'minin Ali in Kufa relates that, asked the whereabouts of Jibra'il, he searched all directions and the seven earths and finding him nowhere concluded the questioner himself was Jibra'il, who then ascended.

Praise is given to God who specified His friends (awliya) with the secrets of His vicegerency in the knowledge of the Imam, making them upholders (quwwam) of the gnosis of His oneness (ma'arif al-tawhid) and treasurers (khuzzan) of the depths of His wisdom.

The sciences of the Imams operate through symbols (rumuz) and indications (isharat), as in the recorded conversations of Dawud, Musa, and Sulayman, understood only by the speaker and the intended hearer.
Allah created numbers and placed the arrangement of everything in numbers, so that everything (e.g. derivations from 'La ilaha illa Allah') is related to numbers.
The sciences of concealment (sitr) are those that were manifest in the time of unveiling (kashf) but, since the time of Baqiyyat al-suwakh, have been expressed in a hidden (makhfi) manner.
The chapter closes with blessings upon Muhammad the Prophet and master of the legatees and upon their family, who are the pure and most noble Imams (a'immat at-tayyibin al-akramin).

At death the Nafse Namiyah of believers travels with the senses in the form of rihyat from the moon (qamar) toward the sun (shams), then through the kawakib and aflak, descending onto things fire does not touch.
The Imam and his household consume the descended rihyat, and from it the Imam's offspring are formed, their bodies taking shape from rihyat and their Nafse Namiyah from the sun's subtleties.

When the Imam's child reaches four years, the gathered forms and souls of the believers reach the Babul Abwab in order and connect with the nafs of the Imam's child, while the Imam's form becomes a ruh.
The human form at the Babul Abwab becomes the haykal, and the Babul Abwab becomes the qalbe haykal, with each rank retained at its proper station.
When the Qaimul Qiyam (Imam of the Imams) comes, a similar grand gathering occurs forming qawaim of qawaim and oceans of oceans, including all departed believers.
Every Imam is brought out (istikhraj) from the da'wat of his father, each establishing his da'wat until he extracts a successor, continuing forever in the Daur al-Kashf and Daur as-Satr.
In the Daur al-Kashf the esoteric/real sciences appear and are read in gatherings and from pulpits, with no enforcement of the apparent (zahir) ordinances.

Lahut cannot manifest without Nasut, and the Nasut-e-tabi'i (in which relationships exist but the five senses do not) is necessary for the manifestation of the relationships of the khuddam and the Imam.

Although Shari'ah injunctions are not enforced in the Daur al-Kashf, its people are so pious that their voluntary acts (tatawwu'at) of prayer, fasting, and charity exceed our obligatory duties (fara'id).
In the Daur as-Satr the da'wat is of two kinds: an esoteric hidden da'wat (batinah khafiyyah) and a manifest clear da'wat (zahirah jaliyyah).
The esoteric hidden da'wat is the division of the divine stations (maqamat ilahiyyah), luminous structures (hayakil nuraniyyah), and their abwab, hujaj, du'at, and ma'dhun.

In the era of Adam the people of the esoteric da'wat were in extreme concealment (istitar) out of fear of opponents, pharaohs, and adversaries due to scarcity of affinity, as the progeny of Qabil gained dominance and Habil's progeny went into concealment.

The manifest du'at openly call toward the Imam of the time because of the proximity of affinity between them and the rest of the world, and they extract those with sound guidance toward the esoteric da'wat of their masters.
The du'at act under the command of the Imams, take responsibility from them, speak by their word, recognize the loftiness of their stations, and continue thus through all eras.
Sayyidna Ali (cited as Ali bin al-Husayn al-Jamali) said in a khutbah, 'I am nothing but like a pen in the hand of the Imam,' as a pen in the hand of a scribe.
When Adam's era completed, Nuh rose as Natiq with his wasi Sam, then the Imams of his era and their du'at, until Ibrahim rose as Natiq.
Ibrahim was a confluence (majma') of the forms of the people of the two preceding eras (Adam and Nuh), unlike Adam and Nuh who were themselves da'i for that confluence.

When a Natiq abrogates his Shari'ah, the emergence of fudala' necessitates changing some Shari'ah laws (concerning halal/haram), while the worship and commands of Allah remain unchangeable, anchored in 'Innad-dina indallahil-Islam'.

Ibrahim is a luminous structure (haykal nurani) who attained all three ranks, with Adam standing in the station of tanzil, Nuh opposite ta'wil, and Ibrahim opposite the haqa'iq, anchored in the Quranic 'wa Ibrahimalladhi waffa'.
Ibrahim is the son of the preceding Imam Salih, the one who brought him into being and pointed toward him, and in him were gathered prophethood, messengership, successorship, and imamate.
The Daur al-Fitrah is the last 3,000 years of the 50,000-year Daur al-Kashf, in which two kinds of people emerged: bearers of the sciences of realities and bearers of the apparent sciences.
The total count is 57,000 years (50,000 Daur al-Kashf plus 7,000 Daur as-Satr) multiplied to reach 400,000 years, and the present is the last part of this first 400,000-year dawr.
Adam began the Daur as-Satr after the Daur al-Fitrah; in the Daur al-Fitrah there were prophets, and the era of priesthood, astrology, and sorcery was at its peak.
The Qaim of the Daur al-Kashf is Imam Hunaid, who became the Hijab-e-A'la (Highest Veil).

With the nutaqa' the people of their eras gather as a gathering of forms, but no haykal is formed; the term haykal applies only when all forms gather at the Babul Abwab to form the complete human form (form of alif).
The ten ranks ascend in order: Mustajib, Momin, Mukasir, Ma'dhun, Da'i, Hujjat, Bab, then Imam at the eighth rank, with Wasayat and divine speech (nutq-e-ilahi) above imamate.
The bearers of divine speech (nutq-e-ilahi) are the three Ha's: Hunaid, Ibrahim, and Hashim, with the Prophet in the second rank, distinguishing a Natiq from a divine Natiq.
Allah created from non-existence the intellects (uqul), luminous specters (ashbah nuraniyah), and essences (zawat), not forms, and the word nafs was not yet used for them.
Allah bestowed three things upon the created intellects: life/existence (hayat), knowledge (ilm), and free will (ikhtiyar) — gifts that no one can take away and present in every human.

The tenth intellect (ashir) delayed in using its free will due to corrupt imagination (wahm-e-fasid), descending from intellect into the form of a nafs, anchored in 'Ya ayyatuhan-nafsul-mutma'innah... irji'i'.

The word nafs (and nufus) originated only from the tenth intellect (ashir); when he later returned to the form of intellect he became the 'Aql-e-Kulli (Universal Intellect) and attained flawless perfection.

The Nafse Kulli is the ashir (also called Nafse Mutma'innah); the souls of the Imams are also called Nufuse Kulli because they immediately accepted the call of the ashir and gained a station in the realm of life.

The center of the Nafse Hissiyah is the sun, the center of the Nafse Namiyah is the moon, and the Nafse Kulli is in the dimensionless realm of life encompassing all, with effects flowing into the dimensional world.
Through further descent the nafs becomes a body (jism); the body was a nafs and the nafs was an intellect, showing the chain of descent.
The Nafse Natiqa is the spiritual form of knowledge and action created by one's own essence (which Allah created), making it the believer's real acquisition through free will.
A non-believer (ghair-e-momin) is a fallen physical form of a believer who has a soul but not a Nafse Natiqa, lacking the form of knowledge and action established through the 'Ahd-e-Sharif.
The essence is all intellect; soul and body are merely changed forms of intellect, and the return journey ascends in the reverse order of descent (body first, then soul).
At the 'Ahd-e-Sharif one receives the Nafse Natiqa as the khameer-e-nizamat performed by one's predecessor a thousand years earlier, who planted a seed now obtained by the successor.
When the four ranks gathered in Ibrahim, he established his da'wat until he brought forth his son Isma'il, though his son Ishaq had been born before Isma'il.
Ibrahim gathered both the eras of Adam and Nuh — all individuals who had entered the haykal of the Natiq — and the four ranks (Nubuwwah, Risalah, Wisayah, Imamah) gathered in him.
There are two Ibrahims: Ibrahim the Natiq 'alladhi waffa', and a man named Ibrahim who was a Nabi of his time, mentioned in the Quran as 'kana rajulun yuqalu lahu Ibrahim'.
The thalathaha (three) — Maulana Hashim, Maulana Hunayn, Maulana Ibrahim — hold a special khilafah and rank among the khilafats of the Qa'im.
The wazir of the Qa'im is 'Ayn 'Azim, whose khilafah is taken by Mim ('Abd al-Muttalib, then Abu Talib, then 'Abdullah), with two qiran and then Mim Jadd al-Qa'im, and Fatimah as khalifah of Mim.

The mutimmin of the Dawr-e-Muhammadi and every seventh Imam (Muhammad bin Isma'il, Ma'add al-Mu'izz, Imam al-Tayyib, the 28th Maulana Ma'add, 22nd Maulana Ahmad, 42nd Maulana Ali, 49th Abu al-Qa'im) hold a very high rank.
Hazrat Nasrullah Sahib taught that the atimmah of the Prophet's dawr reached so high a rank that a qiran (equality) occurred with the sevenths, making them sometimes equal in taking khilafah.

Among the atimmah, Maulana Muhammad bin Isma'il holds the highest rank (gathered with a personality like Imam Husayn), established in the dawr-e-kashf, and thus does not fall into the category of the seventh class.

Of the seven, four are greater (Muhammad bin Isma'il, Imam al-Tayyib, Maulana Ahmad, Abu al-Qa'im), three gathering two ranks each, while Muhammad bin Isma'il alone holds the special rank of sahib-e-dawr-e-kashf, anchored in Surat al-Ikhlas.
The Qa'im's name is 'Ali, and Sayyidna referred to him as Abu 'Ali in his poetic responses.
Because Anwar is a foundational book from which most Du'at take proofs, it places Wisayah before Imamah (unlike most books), and Wisayah is the higher rank.

Ibrahim established Isma'il as Wasi entrusting him Wisayah and Imamah by Allah's command because he is a maqam ilahi and haykal nurani, while entrusting Ishaq the ranks of Nubuwwah and Risalah and making him a khadim, hijab, and da'i to Isma'il.

Isma'il and his progeny are divine stations (maqamat ilahiyyah) and possessors of luminous temples (the people of permanence, ahl al-istiqrar), while Ishaq and his progeny are proofs and manifest summoners (hujaj and du'at zahirun) and veils upon them.

The chain of Du'at and hujub (manifest summoners) ran from Ishaq through Ya'qub, Yusuf, and the named prophets down to 'Isa, then Sham'un, 'Abd al-Masih, and Bahira al-Rahib — all the ahl al-istida' tracing their lineage back to Ishaq.
When the Prophet was manifested, the rank of Nabuwwah that had been with Bahira the monk was taken by Ubayy ibn Ka'b.

Hashim (Hasham al-sarid) gathered the four ranks and gave them completely to 'Abd al-Muttalib, who divided them: Nubuwwah, Risalah, Imamah, Wisayah to 'Abdullah, and a second part to Abu Talib; when 'Abdullah died all four gathered in Abu Talib.

Abu Talib gave Nubuwwah and Risalah to the Prophet and Imamah and Wisayah to 'Ali, but since they were young, all ranks gathered in the Prophet through the kafalat-e-'uzma (great guardianship), whose power overshadowed all the mustawda'in and mustaqarrin gathered with 'Ali.
The Qa'im of the progeny of Isma'il is 'Ali and the Qa'im of the progeny of Ishaq is the Prophet, but the succession occurred with the Prophet, who gathers them when joined with 'Ayn 'Azima.
The first of the A'immah (divine stations) after Ibrahim was Isma'il ibn Ibrahim, entrusting to Qaydar, with a long named chain of fathers-to-sons down to 'Udad bin 'Udad whose muqim was Musa.

When the time bound the manifestation of a Natiq, 'Udad established Musa from among his Du'at, and the chain continued through 'Adnan, Ma'add, Nizar, Mudar, Ilyas, Mudrikah, Khuzaymah, whose da'i was commanded to establish 'Isa.
The muqim of Adam is Maulana Hunayn, of Nuh is Maulana Hud, of Ibrahim is Maulana Salih, of Musa is 'Udad bin 'Udad, and of 'Isa is Khuzaymah.

The chain continued from Khuzaymah through Kinanah, Nadr, Malik, Fihr, Ghalib, Lu'ayy, Ka'b, Murrah, Kilab, Qusayy, 'Abd Manaf, Hashim, to 'Abd al-Muttalib, with whom the four ranks (Wisayah, Imamah, Nabuwwah, Risalah) gathered as they had with Ibrahim.

When the four ranks gathered with 'Abd al-Muttalib, two (Wisayah and Imamah) were reserved for the Qa'im of Isma'il's progeny and two (Nubuwwah and Risalah) for the Qa'im of Ishaq's progeny, and Imamah and Wisayah are never separated.

From Allah's justice and grace, Muhammad became a divine station (maqam ilahi) and luminous structure (haykal nurani), which is impossible unless one's father is likewise a haykal nurani; thus 'Abdullah being a haykal nurani is the precondition for Muhammad being one.

Because the Prophet received the great guardianship, despite bearing only Nubuwwah and Risalah he achieved superiority over all ranks gathered with 'Ali, becoming the deputy of 'Ayn, with no rank of the Qa'im remaining except the thalathah sukra (the three intoxicated ones).

After Maulana 'Abd al-Muttalib, the haykal-nurani condition requires that an Imam's father and grandfather be haykal nurani, but two sons of one father can both be Imams (one in the mustawda', one in the mustaqarr), as with 'Abd al-Muttalib's two sons.

'Ali said 'ana abdun min abid Muhammad' (I am one of the slaves of Muhammad), illustrating the loftiness of the awaited one's station and the three courses (salasa majari) of the relationship: adna (lower), masawat (equality), and a'la (higher).
Qaba qawsayn aw adna corresponds to the stations: 'Abd al-Muttalib and Abu Talib are 'qaba qawsayn' and 'Abdullah is 'adna'.

'Abd al-Muttalib set up two gates (babayn) to receive ascending forms from his da'wah, one higher than the other: the higher gathering the forms of accomplished believers and virtuous Hudud, the second gathering the forms of steadfast respondents.

Each Imam's bab al-abwab is his wife, who gathers the forms and then becomes the qalbe haykal of his son the next khalifah: Hashim's bab Salma submerged in 'Abd al-Muttalib; 'Abd al-Muttalib's bab Fatimah bint 'Amr in Abu Talib; Abu Talib's bab Fatimah bint Asad in 'Ali; 'Ali's bab Salman-e-Farsi in Imam Husayn.
The Prophet's bab al-abwab is Khadijah, submerged in Fatimah; 'Abdullah's bab al-abwab is Aminah, submerged in the Prophet — distinguishing being a bab al-abwab from becoming a qalbe haykal.

The four Ya Fateru sajdahs/recitations correspond to the four Fatimahs: first sajdah (100x) Fatimah al-Zahra, right cheek (100x) Fatimah bint Asad, third Fatimah bint 'Amr, fourth sajdah (110x) Zawjat al-Qa'im (also named Fatimah), with Fatimah al-Zahra superior to all.

In sajdah seven parts of the body must touch the ground (forehead/face, two hands, two knees, two feet), signifying that the complete order of the da'wah requires seven limbs/hudud; the cheek-only position signifies a lesser rank.

The fifth chapter restates that Qa'im min wuld Isma'il is 'Ayn-e-'Azimah and Qa'im min wuld Ishaq is the Prophet; the haykal-nurani requires receptive strength (quwwat) to gather all forms, formable only if the father is a haykal nurani.

The bab gathers all the world's forms and, when it is time to install them in the Imam's son (nasb), becomes the son's qalbe haykal; the Imam (and the Imam of Imams, 'Ayn-e-'Azimah) decides which form is ready for inclusion.

'Abd al-Muttalib made his son Abdullah's matter famous through the sacrifice (dhabh) — sacrificing 100 camels in place of Abdullah — to make known among the ahl al-haqa'iq Abdullah's virtue as one prepared for the station of Nubuwwah and Risalah.

The present Imam Maulana Muhammad bin Ali holds the lofty station of jadd-e-qa'im (grandfather of the Qa'im), who will have two sons by custom: one at Abu Talib's station (from whom the Qa'im comes) and one at Abdullah's station (Sayyidna Mahdi), whose daughter Fatimah will marry the Qa'im producing Hasan and Husayn.

'Abd al-Muttalib handed Wisayah and Imamah to Abu Talib (an imam-e-natiq, like Husayn) and Nubuwwah and Risalah to Abdullah (silent/samit, like al-Hasan); Abdullah fathered Muhammad and Abu Talib fathered 'Ali.

When Abdullah's transfer (nuqlatu) came, he entrusted Nubuwwah and Risalah to his father 'Abd al-Muttalib for his son Muhammad, and when 'Abd al-Muttalib transferred he entrusted them to Abu Talib because Muhammad was in childhood (tufuliyyah), Abu Talib becoming custodian (kafil) of all four ranks.

When Muhammad reached maturity Abu Talib handed over the entrusted Nubuwwah and Risalah, and Muhammad ascended through the ranks until reaching the rank of divine speech (nutq-e-ilahi), the final/highest rank above Nubuwwah, Imamah, and Wisayah.
The station of maqam-e-mahmud changes according to the 'ayn — a single-cycle 'ayn versus a seven-cycle 'ayn — and at the khutbat al-tasmeem the station of the 'ayn changes into the form of the Qa'im.

The completion of the religion ('I have perfected for you your religion') refers to the completion of the obligations of the din, with the command of wilayah announced last after Hajj, not to a change in station.

There are three courses (salasa majari) of the Prophet-'Ali relationship: 'Ali's 'ana abdun min abid Muhammad' (majra-e-adna), 'ana wa Aliyyun ka-hatayn' (equality), and the elevation of Hijab-e-'Ain at the conquest of Makkah (a'la).

Muhammad said 'I am the prayer (da'wat) of my father Ibrahim,' gathering all the lofty stations and luminous structures of all cycles from the first three thousand years (the higher suwarat of the dawr-e-kashf) within his haykal, which became 'Ali.

Successive du'at (e.g., Sayyidna Sulayman, then Sayyidna Ja'far) explained the du'as of the da'i but each kept some knowledge received from the Imam hidden, a series of concealment continuing from da'i to da'i.

When Amir al-Mu'minin was in the unmatched state no one else reached, the Tenth Intellect connected with him totally (ittisalan kulliyan), the creative intellects glanced at him eternally and cast their rays, and the divine substances connected with him above every other station except the Qa'im.

Amir al-Mu'minin's nuqta of the muhtajib has the highest station after Dhu al-Sa'y al-Ibda'iyah, manifested from Sarandip at the start of the Daur al-Kashf, until the inbi'ath of the Qa'im's nuqta which will be greater still.

Amir al-Mu'minin is a part (juz') in relation to the Qa'im who is whole (kull), and likewise the stations of the Imams are partial relative to 'Ayn al-'Azimah the Imam of Imams, who is in turn partial relative to the Qa'im, who is partial relative to Dhu al-Sa'y al-Ibda'iyah.

The Prophet alluded to this with 'al-Hasan wa al-Husayn imamani bi-haqqin qama aw qa'ada wa abuhuma khayrun minhuma' (Hasan and Husayn are two rightful Imams whether they rise or sit, and their father is better than them).

The Prophet placed qiyam (rising, Husayn) before qu'ud (sitting, Hasan) though Hasan is the earlier Imam, because to enact the imamate openly among the people is qiyam (as Husayn did) while Hasan remained silent.
From his state divine miracles and great signs appeared in Amir al-Mu'minin, all of nature became obedient to him, and some Shi'a out of deification (ilahiyat) called him God.

'Ali's saying 'ana al-awwal wa al-akhir' (I am the First and the Last) means he is the first of the forms of the preceding cycles and the last of them (the last being the Qa'im), being first and last of the adwar.
Surat al-Shams takes 14 oaths and demonstrates Arabic grammatical gender (shams feminine, qamar masculine, sama' and ard feminine by convention), with all pronouns 'ha' referring to the sun.

'Ali's saying 'ana al-batin' refers to the hidden knowledge from which the subtle hidden divine essences and substantial luminous souls (forming the haykal of 'Ayn al-'Azimah) came; 'ana al-zahir' is his appearance to sight through divine miracles.

The righteous manifest deeds are the first forms established for the awliya' from interpretive hearts and divine wisdoms in all cycles, all interpretive/real/divine wisdoms ultimately connecting through their Imams to the Imam of Imams Abu Talib.

All Imams gather through the bab/bab al-abwab process (da'i, then hujjat, then bab) and connect with 'Ayn al-'Azimah through the Prophet as the bab; capable forms join that haykal while the rest are given to the coming ones.

'Ali's saying 'ana nuqiltu Adam wa Nuh wa Ibrahim wa Musa wa Isa, wa ana naba'tu al-nabiyyin wa ana arsaltu al-mursalin' (I transported the prophets, I made the prophets prophets, I sent the messengers), the speaker of these forms from the end of the dawr al-kashf until his rising.

When the flowing light connected with 'Ali totally he knew what was and what will be, and all the world of nature became before him like a thrown ball with nothing hidden, anchored in 'inna li manzilah lam takhtur ala qalb bashar'.

Lordship (rububiyah) and Divinity (ilahiyah) do not occur to human hearts except for the Qa'im among them — interpreted not as a divinity claim but as the relation of the lord above and the one below.

All creation knows Allah with outward gnosis (zahir al-ma'rifah), the people of realities know Him with the reality of His gnosis, and no one knew 'Ali with the reality of his gnosis except the Messenger and the Imams of his progeny.

When people heard 'Ali's claims, groups variously said he is al-ghayb (the Unseen), the First Originated (al-mubda' al-awwal), or the First Emanation (al-inbi'ath al-awwal), and voices diverged; the subtle secret was hidden from all but the fewest of the awliya'.

'Ali's hijab was revealed (after Dhu al-Sa'y al-Ibda'iyah) so that he as the mustaqarr could settle the accounts owed to the mustaqarrin by the prophets who served them in earlier eras, while the Prophet, the qaim over prophets and messengers, gathers all the prophets.

Imam Husayn performed qiyam to settle the accounts of the transgressions in the wars of the Prophet's and 'Ali's times; without it the haykal of Imam Husayn (with the Master of the Universe) could not have developed.

The reward in the durud (salutation) upon the Prophet and his family exists to establish one's spiritual connection with them; it is a prayer whose acceptance is the reward, drawn from their vast unseen treasuries containing gathered forms of crores of years.

A qawr (also dawr) equals 400,000 years; 399 qawrs have passed since Dhu al-Sa'y al-Ibda'iyah manifested, and the world is in the last part of the first 400,000-year dawr whose forms are with 'Ayn al-'Azimah.

Ja'far ibn Mansur al-Yaman stated that Allah does not accept the prophethood of any prophet, the selection of any wasi, the imamate of any wali, nor any act of obedience — however exhaustive the worship — except through the wilayah of 'Ali ibn Abi Talib, and whoever comes without it has his prophethood, successorship, and deeds nullified.
'Ali is the confluence (majma') of all the Imams and successors (awsiya') from the beginning of the cycles until his advent, which is why nothing is accepted without his wilayah.

Maulana Abdan's saying (in Majmu' al-Tarbiyah) that 'the jum'ah is upon the service of the master for his slave' is proven, because the children of Ishaq (manifest da'wat) served the children of Isma'il (the lofty divine stations) throughout the past cycles.

When the forms gathered with 'Ali (Qa'im of Isma'il's progeny) and the children of Ishaq gathered with the Natiq (the Prophet, Qa'im of Ishaq's progeny), justice made it obligatory for 'Ali to serve the Prophet as requital (qadha') for the prior service of Ishaq's children to Isma'il's children.
The Arabic qadha' means to complete/fulfill (qadha'an ma fata) what was missed, not merely a missed-then-made-up prayer as commonly understood in Urdu.

This service of the master for his slave — 'Ali standing before, striving with, fighting the enemies of, and defending the Prophet — was requital for the service rendered by the prophets in the eras of Ibrahim, Musa, and 'Isa, measure for measure (hazwan bi-hazwin), with nothing small or great left unaccounted because the scale of justice is established.

The Tenth Intellect ('Aql al-'Ashir), the musta'id da'iya in the realm of life, is veiled by Muhammad, supports and looks upon him, and aids him through the mediation of jadd, fath, and khayal upon his reaching the rank of hijabiyyah.

Every natiq, wasi, and imam must receive instruction and progress rank by rank, anchored in 'wa Allahu akhrajakum min butuni ummahatikum la ta'lamuna shay'a' (Allah brought you from your mothers' wombs knowing nothing).

The Prophet acquired knowledge from Ubayy ibn Ka'b (alluded to as Jibra'il) at his beginning, then was elevated to Zayd ibn 'Amr the da'i of his island (alluded to as Mika'il), then to the one above (Israfil).
Ibrahim's progression through the ranks is shown by the Quranic account of seeing the star, moon, and sun and rejecting each that sets, anchored in 'fa-lamma janna alayhi al-laylu ra'a kawkaban'.

'Ali progressed similarly, learning at the side of the Prophet and of Khadijah bint Khuwaylid (the hujjah of Imam Abu Talib), and was alluded to as Ibn Maryam (analogized to 'Isa, Khadijah to Maryam), anchored in 'wa lamma dhuriba ibnu Maryama mathalan'.
'Ali said the Messenger taught him a thousand doors (chapters) of knowledge, and from every door a thousand more opened (one lakh / a thousand thousand).
Due to a hidden secret, Amir al-Mu'minin said 'Ana wa Muhammad min nurin wahid' (I and Muhammad are from one light), the light of God.

Allah commanded that one light to split into two halves, saying to the first 'Be Muhammad' and to the second 'Be Ali,' indicating the subtleties of the children of Ishaq and Isma'il and their da'wat of Nubuwwah/Risalah and Imamah/Wisayah.

'Ali said 'Muhammad is the yellow sapphire and I am the red ruby' (the most excellent), and the Prophet said 'Aliyyun minni wa ana minhu' and 'la yu'addi anni illa Ali' (none delivers on my behalf except Ali).
When Muhammad ascended to the rank of hijabiyyah and nutq al-haqiqi, the Imam of the Age Abu Talib transferred (passed away).

'Lawlaka lama khalaqtu-l-aflak' (Were it not for you I would not have created the celestial spheres) means without the Prophet bearing the forms of Nubuwwah and Risalah — upon whom retributions (qisasat) rested — the aflak and their cycle of accounts would not have been created, while 'Ali's people (Imamah/Wisayah) are not meant for the world's revolutions.

The Prophet's final station is rutbat al-hijabiyyah and the nutq al-haqiqi, anchored in 'an tab'athahu maqaman mahmudan alladhi wa'adtahu', and as the 'ayn is, so is the mim (manifestation) — rising together at corresponding ranks.

After Abu Talib's transfer he became in his station a veil (hijab) for the Tenth Intellect and a place for its rays to fall, aiding the Prophet through the mediation of jadd, fath, and khayal (the thalathat sufara', alluding to the 'ayn).

Jadd, fath, and khayal are the three spiritual emissaries in the world of veiling, corresponding to the three corporeal ones — 'Abd al-Muttalib (jadd), 'Abdullah (fath), and Abu Talib (khayal) — who became intellects divested of the senses, emissaries between the Prophet/'Ali and the Tenth Intellect.
The Tenth Intellect stands in the station of the First Intellect for the world of nature, and 'Ayn-e-'Azimah takes on the deputyship of the Tenth, in the spiritual world of life.

Jibra'il is a station (maqam), not a self-existing entity; whoever occupies the helper's station for the one being trained (at whatever rank) becomes Jibra'il, with the helper changing as the receiver's ranks increase.
In the tongue of the Shari'ah 'Abd al-Muttalib (jadd) is Israfil, 'Abdullah (fath) is Mika'il, and Abu Talib (khayal) is Jibra'il, the one who supports Muhammad in his beginning and end.
The complete light from the Tenth connected with Muhammad (making him natiq), while with 'Ali it was a ray (shu'a'), making him samit (silent) — the Prophet natiq and 'Ali the silent opposite.

The Prophet told 'Ali he was given five things the Prophet himself was not given, including a father-in-law (the Prophet), a wife (Fatimah), and sons (Hasan and Husayn), illustrating the third (highest) course of their relationship.
With the Prophet was the knowledge of what was and what will be (he made prophecies), while with 'Ali was the knowledge of what has been (what happened), due to the veil (hijab) of 'Ali.

When the Prophet fulfilled his service, appointed 'Ali (nass), and transferred to Allah's abode, 'Ali became in his place a veil for the Tenth Intellect and a place for its rays, with the Tenth manifesting through him via the mediation of jadd, fath, and khayal — now 'Abd al-Muttalib (jadd), Abu Talib (fath), and Muhammad (khayal) for Amir al-Mu'minin.

'Abd al-Muttalib, 'Abdullah, and Abu Talib did not enter the haykal of the Prophet or 'Ali but remained on the horizon of the Tenth as intermediaries between it and Muhammad and 'Ali, and will go into the haykal of the Qa'im.

By a general rule, every establisher (muqim) of a station after his transfer is the khayal for it, the one before him is the fath, and the one preceding them both is the jadd, each an agent within his extension (mandud).

The Prophet said 'Takhaffafu talhaqu' (Lighten yourselves and you will catch up) — reduce sins to join the angels — and 'the first of you only await the arrival of the last of you,' the departed awaiting those who come later.

When the sixth Natiq Muhammad rose with the command, announced the two testimonies (la ilaha illallah, Muhammadun Rasulullah), and established his exoteric (zahir) mission, people accepted Islam, performed jihad, established the seven pillars (da'a'im as-sab') and the sunnahs, and were true in love (mawalat) of him and his cousin outwardly.

When the believers' souls became jewel-like (tajawharat), their forms hidden, and their essences shone, those who passed away with outward (zahir) allegiance to 'Ali returned to the luminous haykal of Fatimah, the essence of the Islamic jewel (khulasat al-jawhar al-islami).

When the luminous forms were complete, Fatimah's father (the Prophet) married her to Amir al-Mu'minin by Allah's command and revelation, the forms of iman gathering with 'Ali and forms of islam with Fatimah, so the system was established and iman and islam were wed.

The exoteric mission continued with the esoteric mission within it, until Hasan was brought from the exoteric da'wat (the portion/qist of the Natiq) and Husayn from the esoteric da'wat (the portion of the Wasi).

The Prophet entrusted his son Hasan the rank of Nubuwwah and Risalah and his son Husayn the rank of Wisayah and Imamah, placing the entrusted (mustawda') ranks for Hasan with Amir al-Mu'minin since the children were seven or eight years old.

Amir al-Mu'minin stood in the Prophet's station with the four ranks, then entrusted Hasan Nubuwwah/Risalah and Husayn Wisayah/Imamah; in the imamate as in the human being there are ten degrees beginning with responsiveness (istijabat) then faith (iman).

In precedence (sabaqiyat) Hasan was first, but in sharpness of vision (hiddat-e-nazar) Husayn was superior; the four ranks became permanent (mustaqarr) in Husayn, not departing to his progeny, until handed to the Qa'im al-Qiyamah (per Da'wat-e-Ashir).
In the haykal of the Qa'im al-Qiyamah, the soul of the Qa'im is its spirit (ruh), Amir al-Mu'minin 'Ali is its heart (qalb), and the Natiq Muhammad is its head (ra's).

Every seventh Imam (Qa'im) appears every thousand years; over seven thousand years the Imams gather into the horizon of their father, and at forty-nine thousand years the seventh gathers his era plus the Imams of seven thousand and forty-nine thousand years.

Sayyidna Hamiduddin al-Kirmani said in Rahat al-'Aql that 'the sun of the Abode of Origination (dar al-ibda') and the moon of Emission (inbi'ath) shine upon them,' the sun pointing to the Natiq and the moon to the Wasi.

All the Imams from the children of ' Abd al-Muttalib, Abu Talib, 'Abdullah, and Fatimah become limbs (a'da') of the Qa'im's luminous haykal, but 'Abd al-Muttalib, Abu Talib, and 'Abdullah remain in the fold of the Tenth Intellect as ambassadors between it and Muhammad and 'Ali.

On the day of Badr the gathered angels (the stations that were with Amir al-Mu'minin) became personified, and Abu Talib was the master of Hayzum (Jibra'il's horse) commanding 'Ali to advance and attack in battle.

Maulana Husayn departed and the rest of the A'immah mutimmin (completers) continued until reaching Maulana Muhammad ibn Isma'il, the seventh, to whom the ultimate goal of the religious laws culminates and who is the Qa'im bil-quwwah (potential Qa'im), master of the first unveiling (sahib al-kashf al-ula).

The Qa'im bil-fi'l (kinetic Qa'im) who appears at the end of the dawr is the master of the later unveiling (kashf al-ukhra) and the great strike (batshat al-kubra), while Muhammad ibn Isma'il is master of the first unveiling.

The qiyamat are many: a qiyamah is a gathering (ijtima') of forms with hashr and nashr, and the ranks (ma'dhun makfuf, ma'dhun mutlaq, da'i muharram, da'i mutlaq, da'i al-balagh, hujjat, abwab) each represent a qiyamah for those connected to them.

These minor qiyamat are followed by the Qa'im of the great resurrection (qiyamat al-kubra), the master of the batshat al-kubra (great strike), with whom gather all the noble stations and all the Imams from the first 3,000 years (dawr al-fitrah) to the end of 7,000 years of the dawr al-satr.

Amir al-Mu'minin alluded with 'ala ra's kulli asharat alaf sanah yaqumu min al-suwarat' — at the head of every 10,000 years a form stands up — pointing to the Qa'im who gathers the dawr al-fitrah (3,000) and dawr al-satr (7,000), totaling 10,000 years.

Muhammad ibn Isma'il retains the name 'seventh Natiq' for his subtlety in the affair of God, yet he is unique in the rank of divine oneness (rutbat al-wahdat al-ilahiyyah), not arranged in the chain (silk) of the dawr al-satr but its terminator, having surpassed the seventh-Natiq rank to a higher one.

Counting any Natiq with his wasi and six mutimmin yields a seventh Natiq: Adam yields Nuh, Nuh yields Ibrahim, Ibrahim yields Musa, Musa yields 'Isa, 'Isa yields Muhammad, and Muhammad yields Muhammad ibn Isma'il.

The three concealed completers (mutimmu dawr al-satr) of Muhammad ibn Isma'il's dawr are the concealed Imams Maulana 'Abdullah, Maulana Ahmad, and Maulana Husayn, with their three abwab commanded to keep the Imam in taqiyyah and present themselves as Imam, the fourth being Imam 'Ali the Natiq to complete the count of seven.

The Ahl al-Haqq (People of Truth) are of two kinds: those of true gnosis and divine sciences, and those of pure devotion and righteous deeds; both perform righteous deeds and have loyalty to all the Imams.

Upon separating from their dense bodies (kasa'if), the Imams who possess gnosis become the chief members (a'za' ra'isah) of the luminous temple (haykal nurani) of the Imam, with the form (surat) pulling the sensory soul (nafs hissiyah) to reach the haykal.

The level of luminosity in the haykal is according to each one's measure in knowledge (ilm), gnosis (ma'rifat), and devotion (wilayat); those with pure devotion and righteous deeds but without true knowledge follow them at lesser ranks (lata'if below kasa'if).

The dense bodies (kasa'if) are preserved in the mightiest protection: returning to earth, then the tempered mixture, becoming rain, dissolving to vapor, ascending through the rays of the seven planets to the falak al-buruj (Saturn, Jupiter, Mars, Sun, Venus, Mercury, Moon below it).

The body parts ascend and take a place in the buruj as a successor (khalifa); from the buruj the prior occupant's portion (flesh, skin, marrow, nerves, veins) descends as a fine dust to earth and eventually becomes a human in the alam al-alfiyyah (thousand-year realm).

Allah created only essences (zawat/uqul); soul (nafs), body (jism), animals, plants, and minerals are progressively fallen forms of the intellect that delayed (ta'khir) in using its God-given powers, with the hardest fallen state being rock (sakhrah) — and we, not Allah, caused this fall.

When these descended human forms reach maturity (bulugh al-hulm) they are called, respond, and the noble covenant (al-'ahd al-karim) is taken from them, ascending in religious ranks and true knowledge without doubt because their first karra was on certainty.

A good deed once established (a created point) cannot be destroyed and its reward remains forever — its reward is tenfold while evil is onefold and can become non-existent — anchored in 'qad aflaha al-mu'minun' and the reward principle.

Sayyidna 'Ali ibn Husayn taught that all the points (nuqta) of those who will become believers in a given kawr are present with the Sayyid al-Ida'iyya, manifesting in the era appointed by his governance; likewise the mudabbir of the mawr holds the points of his whole mawr, and Adam al-Ibda'i holds the points of all who will progress.

Each rank returns to its same rank — bab as bab, hujja as hujja, da'i as da'i, mu'min as mu'min, mustajib as mustajib — and no one transgresses his first state even if he reaches higher knowledge; breaching ranks (kharq-e-maratib) like the hour-to-hour transition requires traversing all sixty minutes (degrees).

When a soul is purified and ascends to the Chosen One, another soul (a member of the body that became worthy of ascent) is sent forth in the remaining body by the governance of the governors, eventually becoming a single essence; for martyrs (shuhada') both heart and liver become soul, granting a degree or two of advance.

These successful believers are those alluded to in 'qad aflaha al-mu'minun' — humble in prayer, turning from vain speech, active in zakat, guarding chastity except with wives or right-hand possessions — these qualities being their distinguishing mark (sima) of mustaqim al-sayr in outward and inward.

Prayer is founded upon four pillars/shares (as-hum): wudu' (ablution), ruku' (bowing), sujud (prostration), and khushu' (humility), the first degree of khushu' being awareness of the meaning of what is recited.

The purification of a mustaqim al-sayr (one of upright conduct who committed no gravely forbidden sin) is completed over 360 karrat, in which his whole body becomes pure — the sole of the foot reaching the station of the heart.

The fifth chapter applies the statement on the ma'ad (return) to the righteous (sulaha') of the Ahl al-Zahir — those who hold to the outward, follow the Islamic rulings, believe in the Prophet, but in whom love and obedience to the Imam have not fully entered (sulh-e-kul), including the Ahl al-Tashayyu'.

The chaste, virtuous, pure man of the Ahl al-Zahir who establishes the pillars of Islam, holds no enmity, rancor, hypocrisy, injustice, falsehood, lying, or betrayal toward the Ahl al-Haqq, and adheres to the wilayah of the Natiq of the era and his Wasi and recognizes their pure progeny — though such people are very few.

Even a small good deed of anyone (believer, hypocrite, or disbeliever) is never wasted by Allah; good (khayr) can never become non-existent (kal-'adam) while evil (sharr) can — anchored in 'Inna al-hasanat yudhhibna al-sayyi'at'.
Without the wilayah of 'Ali one cannot have a good end (khatima bil-khayr) or cross the Pulsirat, yet a good deed still earns its reward and pulls the doer toward the wilayah of the Wali in the end.

When the righteous Ahl al-Zahir person nears death, the spiritualities of the sun and Venus move him, his soul (nafs) spreads in his body, his heat cools, and his blood freezes — the soul spreading into the body being a sign of inability to cross the Pulsirat.

The good concept (tasawwur) of such a righteous person — preservation of the Book of Allah, love of the Messenger and his Wasi, mercy, chastity, modesty, and fear of Allah — becomes a luminous form (surat-e-nurani) that ascends with the spiritualities to the moon, then is handed to the sun where it ferments and is purified until Allah permits its return.

The body of the righteous dissolves bit by bit, ascends as vapor, enters the tempered mixture, falls as rain, becomes pure foods and sweet drinks and fragrant smells, nourishes a human, appears as a sperm-drop, ascends through ranks, and at birth the purified form connects with it along with the sensory soul it deserves.
The vegetative soul (nafs namiyah) connects from the sphere of the moon when the sperm-drop forms, and the sensory soul (nafs hissiyah) connects from the sun at birth from the womb.

Because the scale of justice (mizan al-'adl) is established, the purified concept returns to the righteous person in a state greater, more glorious, and more noble than at death — like a traveler who leaves home, earns wealth in exile, and returns more abundant than before.

The concept of the disobedient and rebellious has no return ever to their body and soul at death — like a traveler who leaves family and home without intending to return — which is a type of punishment (per 'according to what his hands have put forth').

The fourth chapter gathers five sections; after clarifying the transition and progress of the awliya' to the gates of paradise and the fulfillment of the righteous Ahl al-Zahir, the discourse turns to the opposites (azdad) — the people of corruption and what torment they reach.

When death comes to one of the wicked opposites (azdad), the dark celestial jawzahar (placed beneath the sphere of the moon, comprising the two nodes ras and dhanab) moves him, being the magnet for the wicked (khabith) and the vile (khasis).

In opposition to the 'amud al-nur (pillar of light, descending from the First Intellect and connected through the kalima la ilaha illallah to every person on the 'ahd-e-sharif), Allah established the dark celestial jawzahar; one is either connected to the 'amud al-nur or pulled to the jawzahar with no space between.

The jawzahar-e-zulmani is made from the parts (ajza) of people who were elevated but ended in wickedness, placed beneath the moon's sphere (not reaching the rock) as justice from Allah, from where they carry out their ploys (tadabir); the dhanab (tail) is more wicked than the ras (head).

True progress (taraqqi) is the body becoming soul, while the soul becoming body is decline (tanazzul); at the wicked one's death his soul and body become a single thing and one part transforms into another.

The wicked one separates from his dark destructive sciences, his disbelief about the Ahl al-Haqq, his concealed enmity and hatred, his wicked deeds, and his corrupt beliefs — all of which build a subtle dark wicked form (surat zulmaniyyah khabithah) mirroring the noble luminous form built from interpretive sciences and divine gnoses.

That dark soul is called the dark, Iblisi, satanic soul (nafs zulmani iblisiya shaytaniyya) and becomes a fiery incinerating form, just as the luminous form is an angelic speaking soul (nafs malakutiyya natiqa).

Evil has no root in the primordial creation (al-sharru la asla lahu fi al-ibda'); evil is distance from good as darkness (zulmat) is distance from light (nur), and corporeality/density (kasafat) was created because of us, not by Allah.
A created thing cannot become non-existent (fana); its form (shakl) can change but its existence cannot be annulled — no one but the Originator has the power to turn existence into non-existence.

The wicked dark soul-form is buried with the body and becomes an incinerating, tormenting fire for a period of days, so that grave is seen aflame at night, though one who approaches perceives nothing; its owner is the most wicked, most criminal, most hostile to the Ahl al-Haqq, and most oppressive of creation.

Sayyidna Ikramali Sahib narrated (1255 Hijri) an incident on the journey from Bharuch to Baroda where lightning-fire descended and burned only the clothes in one room while he and his students (Sheikh Ibrahim, Fardali) were safe in another.

Sayyidna Sheikh Adam Sahib verified that light (nur, distinct from fire nar) descends from the sky onto the grave of Muhammad Arif Sahib in Mumin-bagh, Baroda — his reward for endowing (waqf) his land for the jamatkhana and masjid.

Sheikh Adam Sahib ruled by nass that whichever portion is designated as a masjid is a masjid (tahiyyatul masjid may be prayed in it) regardless of a residence below it, and the portion not so designated is not.

When a person passes away, the soul's/form's attention is directed first to the body's parts, then to the shroud (kafan), then to the grave's soil (which is why his own grave-soil should be used), then to his house and dwelling.

Once separated from the dense body (which was like a prison/sijn), the wicked dark form takes whatever shape it wishes and does what it wills, since the body's density no longer restrains it, having become the extremity of evil as the luminous form is the extremity of good.

By Allah's justice the wicked soul is not prevented from what it deserves of torment, because the scale of justice (mizan al-'adl) is established; from the moment it separates from its body it is in torment in all it does, by its will and without its will.

When the wicked soul leaves its body it seeks ascent to pierce the veils (kharq al-hujub) but the rays of the celestial spheres reflect it back to earth — anchored in 'la tanfudhuna illa bi-sultan' — and it seeks its old body but does not find it, remaining terrified and regretful, roaming the place of the body and grave (called mun'if by the common people).

The wicked soul roams between earth and sky, anchored in the Prophet's saying 'al-hawa' la khala'un wa la mala' (the air is neither empty nor full), and takes refuge in dark places, foul urinals, desolate wildernesses, and filthy slaughterhouses — hence the prayer 'a'udhu billahi min al-rijs al-najis...' upon entering the lavatory.
key_terms: al-hawa' la khala'un wa la mala'

teaching: The wicked soul appears in the dreams of like-minded evil people (ahl al-nufus al-khabithah), affirming their corrupt beliefs and increasing their enmity to the Ahl al-Haqq and inclination to their opposites, anchored in 'shayatin al-ins wa al-jinn yuhi ba'duhum ila ba'din zukhruf al-qawl ghurura'.

The wicked form mingles with an ignorant man, woman, or boy and speaks through his tongue, sometimes uttering unseen matters or events (not necessarily true, used to deceive); the common people call this the ruh or ruhiyyah, and it can only affect things through using another body.

The wicked soul disparages the Ahl al-Haqq before its present helpers, affirming their opposition and corrupt beliefs and inclining their hearts to obey it — all from inspiration, whispering, and beguiling (anchored in 'yuwasswisu fi sudur al-nas min al-jinnati wa al-nas') increasing them in devilry and Iblis-like behavior.

When that wicked man or woman dies, the wicked form leaves and the dark celestial node (the abominable jawzahar/node of the sphere, Rahu and Ketu) pulls it after it completes its reckoning, being the dark isthmus (barzakh) and magnet that pulls the evil souls into its horizon, where it becomes a Satan and gathers with its kind for as long as the Governor wills.
The shayatin (devils) are devilish forms that reside in the 'uqdatain (two knots), which constitute the dark isthmus (barzakh al-zulmani).
These devilish forms descend to the earth by the will of the Mudabbir (Director) and enter into edibles and drinkables (ma'kulat wa mashrubat).
The respite (postponement of punishment) is given so that the one from whom qisas (retribution) is due can have his manifestation (zuhur), enabling the full retribution to be exacted.
Nourishment (ghiza) from the poisoned foods can be taken by either a wali (friend) or a zidd (opposite/adversary).
The poisoned food becomes a passageway (ma'bar) through which an evil form manifests, e.g. as Qabil manifested from Adam, and from various Imams enemy-sons were born.
The evil form appears from a man at the time of intimacy with his wife, producing a son who progresses in ranks until born and matured.
Such a matured son becomes the zidd (opposite) of the natiq, his wasi (legatee), or the Imam of the Age.
The zidd transitions from being a shaytan bi-l-quwwah (devil in potentiality) to a shaytan bi-l-fi'l (devil in actuality).
The zidd claims the rank of the high station (maqam al-'ali), conceals the true holder's status (manzilah), and denies (jahada) his station.
Concealing a hadd's station is a spiritual killing (batini qatl), exemplified by al-Harith ibn Murrah who concealed the station of Adam.
Qabil concealed the station of Habil, claimed his maqam, and killed him.
Rasib was the zidd (opposite) of Nuh, though he was not necessarily his son.
Ham was the zidd of his brother Sam (Shem) and killed him.
Nimrud ibn Kan'an was the zidd of Ibrahim.
Al-Walid ibn Mus'ab was the zidd of Musa.
Sahbuta killed 'Isa (Jesus).
Abu Lahab and Abu Jahl were the two opposites (zidds) of the Prophet Muhammad.
Abu Bakr and 'Umar were the two opposites (zidds) of Ali ibn Abi Talib, with the curse of God upon them.
Ibn Muljam was the one who killed Ali ibn Abi Talib lastly (akhiran).
Mu'awiyah was the zidd of al-Hasan and then poisoned him.
Yazid was the zidd of al-Husayn, and Shimr killed him.
Mawlana al-Mustansir Billah and Mawlana al-Amir were each killed by poisoners/killers who were zidds.
The woman of Khaybar (al-Imra'at al-Khaybariyya) poisoned the Prophet in his food, and the poison remained until it became the cause of his passing.
It is a sign of the Prophet's greatness that even a cooked, severed goat's leg testified to him that it was poisoned (masmum) after he had eaten.
The hadith 'li-kulli nabiyyin shaytanun wa liya shaytanan' (for every prophet there is one devil, and for me there are two) identifies the Prophet's two devils as Abu Lahab and Abu Jahl.
