The vices (qaba'is), which are forms gathered in the two knots (the dark isthmus), can flow upon vegetation and become a deadly poison destroying the noble stations, as with the poison that destroyed the Natiq.
The poison from the two knots destroyed al-Hasan, and likewise Mawlana Muslim and Mawlana al-Shams.
When the vices fall upon minerals (ma'adin), they become swords, knives, and arrowheads with which the noble stations are killed.
Every poisoned/weaponized thing is preserved (mahfuz) for its owner (sahib), and its preserver is the dark atmosphere (al-jaww al-zulmani).
This preservation operates by the will of the Mudabbir, the requirement of wisdom (hikmah), and the scale of God's justice (mizan al-'adl).
If the Imam's era is one of the sword, killing, and dominance, the forms of the slain opposites ascend to the two knots to take revenge from that noble station, returning swiftly as devils to attack.

If the Imam's era is one of commands, prohibitions, establishing punishments (hudud), flogging, imprisonment, and exile, the forms of the opposites executed upon them descend from the isthmus as poisons.

Retributions (qisasat) must be completed so that the wronged opposites' transgressions are settled and the further promotion (taraqqi) of the gathering of Imam Husayn can occur; this is a purification.
A person who delivers the poison to the noble station is himself a collection of curses gathered in the two knots, like Ja'dah the wife of Imam Hasan.
Curses (la'anat) from the stations and punishments gather with the conceptions of the opposites in the two knots, producing extreme oppressors most confirmed in enmity and devilry.
Amir al-Mu'minin Ali cursed the people of Kufa/Iraq who betrayed him, foretelling a severe tyrant would be imposed upon them; these curses gathered and manifested as al-Hajjaj ibn Yusuf al-Thaqafi.
Ibn Mahdi was likewise from the curses of the punishments and the conception of the opposites, poured upon the people of Tihamah.
A curse (la'ana) means seeking that Allah distance someone from His mercy; in prayer, seeking mercy (tarahhum) for opposites is impermissible while cursing is permissible.
For the bodies and souls of the opposites (azdad), at death the single soul spreads throughout its body and both become one thing, transforming into dust, ascending as vapor, and descending as rain.
In the believer the bodily parts become soul, whereas in the opposite the soul becomes body (the process is reversed); the soul, being a divine creation, cannot be destroyed.
From the opposites' rain are produced destructive lightnings, annihilating thunderbolts, ruinous floods, and harmful hail, which is the action of the opposites in all times.
The opposites' substance pours onto earth becoming vegetation and animals, by which the nearer torment (al-'azab al-adna) is unleashed upon them.
The first level (dark) of torment is named al-rijs, which is the human tunic (qamis al-bashar).

The consumer of the poisoned substance becomes a nutfah, ascends to a womb, and emerges as a fetus in a tunic from peoples like the Zanj, Zabab, Barbar, Turk, for whom addressing the people of truth is unsuitable.
He transfers from one tunic to another, completing seventy tunics (qamis) in each type.
The second level (dark al-thani), khums al-'aks, is the level similar to human composition: the ape, bear, nasnas, ghoul, and lizard, each with seventy tunics.
In these temporal tunics, the existence of torment is confirmed for him because he opposed the lords of truth, and he becomes one who knows the people of truth and falsehood.
The third level (dark al-thalith), khums al-'ars, is the predators of land and sea (lions, tigers, wolves), every creature with a canine (nab) and a claw (mikhlab), each with seventy tunics.
God grants the punished soul enough cognitive power to understand it is in this animal state because of its prior opposition; this awareness was not granted in the first (human) tunic.
The fourth level (dark al-rabi'), khums al-khars, is the crawling creatures of land and sea (vipers, snakes, scorpions); in this level he is mute (khars), each type with seventy tunics.
The fifth level (dark al-khums), named al-najis, is the predatory birds of land and sea, each type with seventy tunics.
Were it not for the soul's knowledge of its punishment, there would be no pain in punishment nor comfort in reward — knowledge is the precondition of both 'azab and thawab.

Lawful (ascending) animals are not in these torment levels; when a lawful animal is slaughtered its part becomes the human body and to that extent its salvation occurs, returning by the lawful (ascending) path.
After completing the five khums levels, the soul passes into the sixth level (dark al-sadis) named al-naqs (deficiency).
In the sixth level (naks), no knowledge of his state remains because he has departed from the world of sense ('alam al-hiss).

Quran 16:70 ('and among you is he who is returned to the most decrepit of age, so that he knows nothing after having known') is cited as the proof of the matter being obscured and knowledge snatched away from the descending soul.
When he reaches this limit, nothing remains except the faculty of growth ('alat al-nama'), entering the plant state where the growing soul remains but the sensing soul is removed.
This sixth-level form is the forbidden plant (al-nabat al-mahzur) that is a killer and destroyer of the living being (hayawan).
While descending, souls descend from bad bodies; while ascending, they ascend from good bodies — the same vegetative state operates in both directions.
The seventh level (dark al-sabi'), named al-daks, is the hard sanj mineral and the filthy, wicked stone, each type with seventy tunics; good stones like those of the mosque or Ka'bah are excluded.
For each of these seven levels (adrak) there are seventy types (naw') and seventy tunics (qamis), yielding 4900 manifestations per level.

Fallen souls reach the mineral state by two paths: either their intentions at descent were so bad they became stones directly, or they ascended and then fell back; not everyone completes all levels — many return after one to seven levels.
In the shari'ah, animals whose meat is forbidden are forbidden because they are in the descending levels (in punishment), while ascending animals are permissible to eat.

After completing the seven levels, the most stubborn enemies (mutakallifin) are immersed with the opposites of the divine stations, messengers, and prophets, and exiled to the four uninhabited corners of the earth outside the boundary of moderation.

The northern region (place of the star Jady), frozen and dark with the sun absent six months, receives the freezing cold of zamharir; there the opposites of the Imams' stations exist as terrifying frozen-mountain animals.
Zamharir is the mist/wind of intense cold, while asir is the mist of intense heat (the sphere of fire).

The southern region (orbit of Suhayl/Canopus), day for six months, receives the heat of asir; there the opposites of the messengers and prophets are punished as huge ugly mountain-like animals with no apparent senses but feeling great punishment.
The eastern region (sunrise), with lofty mountains nearly reaching the sphere of fire, holds the punishment of the assistants (a'wan) of the opposites of the messengers and prophets.

The western region (sunset) holds a vast dark turbulent sea called the Sea of the Jinn (the Pacific) with mountainous waves, holding the punishment of the assistants of the opposites of the Imams' stations, who return as misshapen sea-animals devouring one another.
Souls are rotated through all four regions in turn (north, south, east, west) so the periphery-punishment ('azab al-atraf) is undergone in all directions.

This is the reality of Sayyidna al-Mu'ayyad's saying (in the 70th of his first hundred Majalis al-Hikmah) that whoever proceeds upon other than the right proportion slips from the luminous center (al-markaz al-nurani) and is cut off from the wilayah of the friends of Allah.

Quran 77:30-31 ('a shadow with three branches, neither cooling nor availing against the flame') refers to the three-branched periphery punishment, identified as the three dimensions (length, breadth, depth).

All the foregoing (seven levels plus four-periphery punishment) is the nearer punishment (al-'azab al-adna); afterward souls are returned to the inhabited quarter (rub' al-maskun) until the Resurrection.

When returned to the inhabited quarter, that quarter is for them like a garden/paradise by comparison to the peripheries, until they manifest with the signs of the millennium (alfiyyah), are brought for the accounting, and then meet the greater punishment (al-'azab al-akbar).

As for the followers (atba') from the pillars ('umud) and subjects (ra'aya), some return after the perception-levels and some complete them; their attainment of punishment is according to their earnestness for the people of truth and their actions.
On the ascending return, the soul begins in minerals beneficial to mankind, then non-forbidden plants, then lawful animals — the good path, as opposed to the bad bodies entered while descending.
The lawful animal is used by whoever must use it (a wali or a zidd) and becomes a passage (ma'bar) for the person to emerge in the fifth millennium, where tribulations (balaya) are presented to him.
Those undergoing punishment are not subject to shari'ah rulings, since shari'ah obligations apply to persons of intellect, not to animals or those in the qisas period.

The returning soul is presented with the wilayah of the hadd it had denied; if it accepts, it is saved (naja) and enters the company of the people of truth — a clean-slate state like the first perfection (kamal-e-awwal).
If it refuses and is arrogant, it returns falling (saqitan) into the classes of punishment; this continues until the rising of the Qaim.

When the Qaim's appearance draws near, all of creation from the time of Adam to the era of his cycle manifests with his appearance; no one remains, obedient or sinner, except he appears, journeying to earth then to temperament and compounding, then into foods and seminal drops, ascending in ranks to appear as a person upon his first invited state.
Each soul is restored upon the very state (old age, youth, smallness, bigness, acceptance, denial, even skin color) in which it was first invited to the truth.
Every prophet, wasi, imam, and hadd is personified (yashkhasu) for the people of his era as a witness over them.

Quran 39:69 ('the prophets and the witnesses will be brought, and it will be judged between them with truth') means each maqam is appointed a witness (shahid) over the deeds of the people of its time; shahid here means a saint of higher rank, not a literal witness.
Quran 56:49-50 ('Say, indeed the former and the latter will surely be gathered for the appointed time of a known day') narrates the gathering of all creation at the appointed time.

Each maqam/hadd disputes (yunafishu) with the people of his era — the Qaim among them and the one sent to them — confronting them about their belying, stubbornness, hostility, and all their actions and sayings, small and great.

The gathering of resurrection occurs in the plains of qiyamah, identified as the western line of the equator (khatt al-istiwa al-gharbi), the land of Ma'rib, because the rising of the Qaim will be there.
Only those creatures (khala'iq, including animals) whose time for qiyamah has come will gather at Ma'rib, rushing from all islands; not the entire world, since the place would become constricted.

Quran 21:96-97 ('Until, when Ya'juj and Ma'juj are released, and they from every elevation descend... and the true promise has drawn near, the eyes of those who disbelieved will stare') is interpreted: Ya'juj and Ma'juj are the opposites (azdad), their followers are the disbelievers, and their objects of worship are their chiefs who stood in the station of the true Imams.

When the creatures gather before the Qaim and every hadd, imam, wasi, and natiq is individualized for the people of his era and made to face all their deeds, the necks of the opposites (azdad) are struck and a fire is sent that burns them all, transforming them into vapor at that moment.
The vapor of the destroyed opposites ascends to the two knots because the two knots attract it through the foul affinity (al-munasabah al-khabithah) between them.
From the two knots beneath the earth, the Sakhrah (the rock in the lowest part of the earth) absorbs that vapor through affinity, drawing it into its parts and pores until it reaches its center.

By the will of the Mudabbir, a reaction occurs in the Sakhrah's center that re-forms each individual upon the state (the millennial stature, qamat al-alfiyyah) in which he opposed the Master of the Age (Sahib al-Zaman).

The Sakhrah is shaped like a brass pot (qidr al-sufr): hard smooth bottom, hollow middle of sulfuric (kibritiyyah) stones, a hard rock roof — closed (mulamlamah) on all sides with pores only in its lower part to vent the vapor.
The Sakhrah is what the Noble Book names Sijjin, and the wise ones (hukama') modeled the bathhouse (bayt al-hammam) upon its pattern.
The fuel (waqid) beneath the Sakhrah is the heat of the sun, which heats it from below as the sun passes beneath the earth.
Upon reaching the center, the individuals observe (mu'ayanah) those who preceded them, recognize they deserve the punishment they are in, and confess their negligence and wrongdoing.
Quran 21:97-98 ('woe to us, we were in negligence... you and what you worship besides Allah are the fuel of Hell') is applied to the punished opposites and their false objects of worship.
Quran 21:99 ('Had these been gods they would not have entered it') means: had the chiefs they followed been true Imams of truth, they would not have entered the Sakhrah.

The Quran's 'khalidina fiha' without 'abadan' for the disbelievers/People of the Book indicates the abiding in Hell is temporary (khulud 'aridi) for purification, whereas 'khalidina fiha abadan' for the righteous indicates eternal abiding (khulud abad) in Paradise.

When the sun's path goes beneath the earth each night, it heats the Sakhrah like the bottom of a hot pot, igniting the sulfuric, calcareous, and glassy stones so the accursed ones tumble in the boiling middle, crying for help unanswered.

This Sakhrah/Sijjin punishment is specific to the opposites (azdad) of the nutaqa', awsiya', a'immah and all their hudud — and their hostile claimants, fanatical helpers, doubt-whisperers, and mockers of the people of truth.

The foolish rabble (huhud and ru'a') who merely followed are turned back from the last perception-level and are not put into the periphery or Sakhrah punishment, because they acted without knowing intent.
The pores of the Sakhrah are located beneath the Ka'bah, since by 'ard' (earth) the Ka'bah is always meant; entry into the Sakhrah occurs from beneath the Ka'bah.

The earth is both elliptical (baydwi) and flat (musattah): a flat platform for humans (the land of da'wat) whose center on one surface is the Ka'bah and on whose opposite surface is the Sakhrah/Sijjin (the Great Hell), the abode of the Ahl al-Tabut.

The earth has four corners (atraf al-zamin) adjacent to the Sakhrah where the periphery-punishment befalls the opponents, and on which the Sakhrah's vents (manafiz) are located, with cold so severe no bird can fly past.

Besides the periphery vents, there are many vents in the inhabited quarter, the largest being Durdur, located in the sea between China and India, toward which all rivers flow and from which various sounds emanate.

The Ahl al-Sakhrah experience reversed day/night relative to earth's people, with intense heat in their day and intense cold in their night, the punishment increasing a hundredfold during the sun's revolution.
God created the Sakhrah before the earth, and in the Quran earth, Sakhrah, and sky are mentioned as three separate individualities in a single ayah.
Around the earth and Sakhrah revolve nine celestial spheres (aflak) with imaginary lines revolving on a plane, and seven planets (kawakib) that are circular and revolve both around and on their axes.

Beneath the Ka'bah, Maqam Ibrahim, Ghadir, and the Rawda places there is no Sakhrah but a void containing the luminous and good souls (arwah nuraniyyah, arwah hasanah), while at amyal, Wadi al-Shaytan, and the Jamarat al-Thalathah there is a great multitude of filthy souls (arwah khabithah).
Sayyidna al-Malik states the pores' locations are not in the aflak but are free of physical limits — all spiritual and imaginary, not physical.

Quran 19:71 ('And there is none of you except he will come to it; this is upon your Lord an inevitability decreed') means everyone must arrive in human form on the earth (Sakhrah included), after which progress occurs.

The order of creation: from the remorseful (nadimin) the aflak were made; the ummahat (fire, air, water, earth-ball) were made; from the insistent (musirrin) the Sakhrah was made; and after 51,000 years of revolution the earth on which we pray was created.

The 'alam al-'uqul (World of Intellects) was made in the luminous world; the delayed tenth became the contented soul (nafs al-mutma'innah, per Quran 89:27) which ascends to take the place of the final intellect.

Upon the command 'ihbitu' (descend), some immediately repented (forming the World of Life), and the increasingly delayed ones formed the falak al-muhit (imaginary, no materiality, state of nafs), then the falak al-buruj where materiality and near-material light first appear with the fixed stars (thawabit).
Thawabit (fixed stars) revolve on their own fixed center, while planets (sayyare/kawakib) revolve around a larger star.

The spheres of Saturn, Jupiter, Mars, and Sun derive from the nadimin and ta'ibin (repentant), while Venus, Mercury, and Moon are all from the nadimin, the more delayed but repentant elements whose effects can carry residual badness.
The Sakhrah was made from the most insistent and arrogant (musirrin, mustakbirin), and the most arrogant of all became the station of Sijjin, which contains the Tabut.
The Prophet said 'Mu'awiyah min al-Tabut' (Mu'awiyah is from the Tabut), placing him in the lowest station (asfal).
The opposites remain in the belly of the Sakhrah until the end of the Great Cycle (al-kawr al-a'zam), which is 360,000 years multiplied by its like, equaling 129,600 million years.

Within that cycle the opposites perpetually curse and kill one another in eternal enmity and warfare, and whoever is killed is transformed into an uglier deformed person (two/three heads, faces turned backward or sideways) burning in the fires.
Upon completion of the Great Cycle, the opposites kill one another, are transformed into vapor, ascend, and exit from four vents (manafiz) at the top of the Sakhrah to the earth's surface.

The four vents are: a well called Barhut (and Shafahu) in a valley of Hadramawt (east); a well in Khurasan; a well in Arabia; and a fourth in an unnamed land — named in the four directions as Barhut/Shafahu (east), Buqa/Han/Har (west), Saydum/Jub/Kharqa (north), Sabr/Sahiq (south).

After exiting as vapor, the souls re-enter the world through temperament and compounding (mizaj wal-muntazij), then praiseworthy minerals, plants, and lawful animals, until appearing in the millennial form (qamat al-alifiyyah) as individuals invited again to the truth — a clean-slate choice like the first perfection.

Three things created by God can never be destroyed but only temporarily hidden: existence (wujud), knowledge/intellect, and free choice (ikhtiyar/freedom); intentions made in the eternal pre-existence ('alam al-azal) are matters of this choice.

The current Qaim (qaim al-muntadhar) is cyclical and is the first cycle of the 400th cycle; 399 cyclical resurrections (qiyamahs) have already passed and we are at the start of the 400th, in its seventh satr cycle.

The true universal resurrection (qiyamat-e-kubra) is the resurrection of the cycle (qiyamah of the dawr), when 'the earth will be changed to another earth' (Quran 14:48), distinct from the partial cyclical resurrection.
Earthly life cannot be older than four lakh (400,000) years because at each cycle's end everything is destroyed and the earth begins anew; the first jussa of the current cycle manifested at Sarandip.

The 400th jussa will manifest in the Ka'bah (Khana-e Ka'bah) and will gather the 399 prior cycles (jami'-e-arba'); cyclical jussas of the past manifested at holy places like Ghadir Khumm, Rawda, Bayt al-Muqaddas, Najaf, Karbala, Maqam Ibrahim, and Hijr Aswad, which are visited, whereas Sarandip is not counted among the holy places.

The greatest jussa is the initial jussa (jussa-e-ibtida'iyyah) at the beginning of a mawr; no other jussa in the whole mawr can reach it, and the final jussa at the world's end may equal it; the true successor of a mawri jussa is the next mawr's jussa (kulli successor), not a cyclical jussa.
Returning to the discourse of the Qaim's state: when he appears, the reckoning (hisab) occurs, the people of punishment meet their torment, and the reward of the people of reward is multiplied.

The Qaim establishes the da'wah to extract a successor whose station is in establishing the da'wah, and he transfers with those in his fold to the rank of the Tenth Intellect (al-'aql al-'ashir), a perfect luminous intellect, one of the Primordial Intellects.

The principle 'la yukhlifu ahadun illa mithluhu' (no one succeeds except one like him): no one can be promoted until a universal (kulli) successor like himself is born; a partial (juzwi) successor does not enable promotion.
Sayyidna Sadiq told Sayyidna Jumali that where 'juzwi' is said the meaning is 'kulli' and vice versa — each term implies the other.

The Tenth Intellect ascends to the rank of the Ninth, and this Qaim, in the rank of the Tenth Intellect, becomes administrator (mudabbir) of the entire world of nature, celestial and terrestrial, perpetually transferring upward as each successor is appointed.

The chain of intellects ascends: ninth takes eighth's place, and so on, but the second (Munba'ith al-awwal, the First Emanation) remains in its sphere and is exalted in its second perfection (kamal-e-thani); the sphere of the First Intellect (the circle of unity, wahdat) can be reached by no one.
Every station transfers to the horizon (ufuq) of the Tenth by the customary habit until the completion of the term, which is 7,000 years (in the period of concealment, satr).

In the dawr-e kashf the period is 10,000 years; after each 10,000 years a Qaim manifests, reaches the horizon of the primordial jussa, and the jussa places the Imams' forms under his authority; the Qaim manifesting after 50,000 years gathers all five qawa'im and becomes a universal Qaim.

After seven dawr-e kashf and seven dawr-e satr, a universal-of-universal Qaim gathers the qawa'im of the seven satr cycles (under which sit the kashf-cycle Qaims); when a qawr ends a new primordial jussa comes, is promoted, and the prior one is exalted, with each succession resting under the jussa-i ibda'iyyah's horizon (ufuq).
At the start of the dawr-e kashf the resurrection (ba'th) of the bodies of the people of the dawr-e satr occurs; 'innal-ba'tha haqq' (indeed resurrection is true).

The first bodies taken/resurrected are those of the people of the Muhammadan dawr, due to their nearness to the Qaim's dawr, their nobility, and their being last in the dawr-e satr; then the bodies of the awliya' whose souls ascended to the world of purity ('alam al-safa') and whose noble bodies fermented bit by bit.
Then the bodies of all the sects (firaq) and the opposites whose souls transformed in their bodies are resurrected and made to taste the lesser punishment (al-'azab al-adna), not the greater.

Each dawr is established for 7,000 years, after which its Qaim rises and faces the resurrection (ba'th) of the people of the preceding nabi's dawr, in sequence: 'Isa, then Musa, then Ibrahim, then Nuh, then Adam — completing the dawr-e kashf.

After the dawr-e kashf comes the dawr-e satr of 10,000 years, of which 3,000 years is the dawr of the people of astronomy, philosophy, and mathematics (nujum, falsafah, riyadiyyah) and 7,000 years is of Shari'ah.

The dawr of kashf and satr, the Imam and Imamate, continue in unbroken chain (one to another, child after parent, no interruption or deviation from lineage) until the passing of the qawr of Adam, which is 360,000 years multiplied by its like.
A small cycle (qawr asghar / dawr) is 400,000 years; the great cycle (qawr a'zam) is 360,000 years multiplied by itself.

At the universal resurrection, the tethers of the celestial spheres (rubatat al-aflak / pegs/gravity) loosen, everything on earth perishes (plants, animals, humans), the affair becomes as at first, and administration (tadbir) passes to Zuhal (Saturn).

Mountains and stones are pulverized, extreme cold and piled snow, clouds, fog, atmospheric darkness arise, vapor rises, rains and rivers burst until the entire earth becomes like a turbulent sea covered in darkness, the sun's light unable to penetrate the dense clouds due to Saturn's influence.

When the time comes for the Qaim of the millennium to appear from the caves (mugharat) as at first, a pure light/substance ascends from the subtle parts (lata'if) and purest of the earth to become a successor (khalifah) to the sun and the rest of the stars and constellations.

Things from the Ka'bah ascend to take the place of the sun; the sun, the six (other) stars, and the twelve constellations descend to earth and become fine dust, from which the new primordial jussa is nurtured after the earth settles.

From the earth arise twenty-eight noble, excellent persons (fudala al-kurama) of the primordial corporeality (jussa al-ibda'iyyah); the sun becomes their Imam and chief, and the remaining stars and constellations are the twenty-seven who appear with his appearance.
The Hudud, peace be upon them, are servants (khuddam) in the world of the body ('alam al-jirm) and the world of religion ('alam al-din).

When a Hudud's subtle essences transfer to the spiritual world at death, his body remains in the earth; for three days whatever remained of the sensory soul (nafs al-hissiyyah), also called the airy soul (nafs al-rihiyyah), ascends to the sphere of the sun.
How much of the vegetative soul (nafs al-namiyyah) ascends or remains in the grave for punishment depends on each Hudud's rank and degree of respect for the shari'ah during life.

Upon the body's dissolution it becomes pulverized dust; the flesh, blood, nerves, veins, and bodily excesses (except the bones) become subtle vapor, ascend to the sphere of the constellations (falak al-buruj), take the place of a constellation, then descend to earth as dust, then to temperament and the blended, returning to edibles that do not enter fire.

The nourishment becomes a nutfah, then a person who is invited and answers, joining the awliya', ascending in the gnostic sciences (ma'arif) to become one of the serving Hudud in the Da'wat of Truth, with his final rank matching his initial rank.
A believer crosses one rank per cycle (there are ten ranks for a believer); only a martyr (shahid) crosses one or two ranks at once ('darajatan aw darajatayn').

The seventeen-fold du'a of light (Nuran fi...) names ten internal locations (heart, hearing, sight, tongue, hair, skin, blood, flesh, bones, nerves) and seven directions (front, behind, right, left, above, below, in the grave).

The bones, due to their hardness (salabah), remain in the earth a long period as the Disposer (mudabbir) wills; they are then ground to dust, ascend as vapor to the temperament and blended, return to earth, and solidify in mines as rubies, pearls, and precious stored jewels.

A human comprises an essence/soul (the divine creation), a sensory soul, and a vegetative soul; the luminous form (rational soul), developed through knowledge and action and free will granted by God, becomes greater than the soul itself.

The vegetative soul is purified by ascending to the moon via the sun's rays, refined with the sun, passing through Mercury and Venus, then descending until the physical form (nasut) of the Imam's progeny is formed, after which the connection of Lahut (divinity) is established — this nasut-Lahut union is the meaning of 'La ilaha illallah'.

The full return cycle is 1,000 years: 360 years residing in twelve constellations (30 years each) ascending and 360 returning, plus 280 years for ascending/descending to manifest as a human, so that a believer manifests again as a believer with consolidated point.

In each cycle one soul is consumed/transformed (the crimson heart-blood taking the form of soul); over 360 cycles (360,000 years) a person of straight path who avoided major sins reaches the station of the heart, and a respondent attains the rank of a natiq.

At the time of return, all the dispersed elements (vegetative soul, sensory soul, form, body, points) are assembled at the Qaim (the universal-intellect court), where individuality both merges and remains distinct, ultimately forming a single whole that seeks to become the Universal Intellect.

The primordial jussa (jussa-i ibda'iyyah) that gathers the great cycle holds all the points (nuqat) from a single respondent up to a Qaim, each point's intensity (hiddat) established according to the intensity of faith in the prior cycle.

The bones progress and solidify in mines as jewels, preserved long because they must manifest with the primordial jussa; old bones preserved from past cycles come to take the place of the body that has gone.

When the Great Cycle's fulfillment arrives, the jewels (transformed bones) are ground, ascend, and become planets succeeding the seven planets and twelve constellations, preserving their places arranged by rank until the supports of the heavens loosen at the next cycle.

From the descending planets/constellations becoming dust, the physical form (nasut) of the primordial jussa is formed; the sun becomes the unique individual of the rank of oneness (the Qaim in the station of the First Originator), and the moon becomes its gate (bab) receiving the ascending forms.

All the Hudud follow in service upon this pattern until all their bodies are purified, and nothing of them remains in the world of generation and corruption ('alam al-kawn wal-fasad) except returning to the abode of purity and eternity — honored, gifted, rich, forgiven, living, eternal, happy.
Quran 37:61 ('and for the like of this let the workers work') is cited as an exhortation to strive for this eternal return.

The paradise for the soul is Jannat al-Ma'wa (Sidrat al-Muntaha); the paradise for the body is the paradise of the presences (jannat al-hadarat) — worldly peace and comfort free of social strife — distinct from the realm of kashf.
In the lofty paradises (jannat al-'aliyat) fasting is not obligatory and there is no hunger or hardship, since obligations of hardship are removed in the state of free choice.
The seven planets and twelve constellations total nineteen, equal to the numerical value of Bismillah al-Rahman al-Rahim.

Of the 354-day (lunar) year, 100 days are the highest, marked by a tasbih; within these, 18 special days include 1st and 10th Muharram, 1st/15th/27th Rajab, 15th Sha'ban, the odd nights of Ramadan, Eid al-Fitr, Yawm Nuzulika, 'Arafah, Eid al-Adha, the three Ayyam al-Tashriq, and 18th Dhu'l-Hijjah.
The 18th of Dhu'l-Hijjah, Yawm al-Ghadir, is the most excellent day of the year; Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq affirmed three times by oath ('No, by God') that no day is better than it.

In the common speech of the exoteric people, at the time of death there must come a mubashshir and bashir (bearers of glad tidings) for the people of good, and Munkar and Nakir for the people of evil, and these are two angels present with the dying person.
This saying about the two angels at death is a true saying heard from the people of truth (ahl al-haqq), though its inner reality became hidden from the world.
Every Natiq of a cycle (dawr) and his Wasi are themselves the two angels referred to in their era: mubashshir and bashir for their friends (awliya') and Munkar and Nakir for their opponents (addad).
The two angels are a single personality that appears as Munkar and Nakir to opponents and as mubashshir and bashir to the friends, depending on whether the person's end is with good and love or not.
Likewise every Imam of the Time and his Hujjat is mubashshir and bashir for his friends and Munkar and Nakir for their opponents, so this reality persists in every age.
Amir al-Mu'minin Ali said in verse to Harith Hamdan: whoever dies, believer or hypocrite, will see me soon; he recognizes me with his eye and I recognize him by his name and kunya and what he did.

The reality is that the form/imagination (khayal) of every station (Natiq, Wasi, Imam) at the time of each one's death moves the Pillar of Light ('umud al-nur), which flows from the world of holiness ('alam al-quds) and is connected to the form of every wali, the Master of the Time.
Between the Originator (mubdi') and the originated (mubda') is a Word (kalimah), which is the kalimah 'La ilaha illa Allah,' and from it the Pillar of Light is connected.

All luminous forms up to the First Intellect ('aql al-awwal) are connected to the kalimah 'La ilaha'; above the First Intellect is the kalimah, which connects to the Originator, and no one can pass beyond the Originator.
The detailed explanation of the Pillar of Light ('umud al-nur) has come in Akhbar al-Latifa.

The Pillar of Light has different centers, the largest being the First Intellect, then the 'ashir, then the Imam of the time, like graded centers of electricity, and all good forms are connected to it like a beehive.

At the last minute of his divine life and righteous deed, the one transitioning imagines a luminous person, rejoices and is delighted at seeing it, and knows by its pleasure that he is headed toward good as he departs the moment.
That luminous form is the form the believer acquired from the walayah (friendship/allegiance) of the people of truth, their divine knowledges, and their righteous deeds with the friends of God.

Mawlana al-Sadiq alluded to this, transmitted by Sayyidna al-Nu'man in Da'a'im al-Islam: when God raises the believer from his grave, a beautiful image (mithal hasan) emerges with him and says through the hardships 'Do not fear, there is no harm upon you.'
That luminous image is the believer's real master/guardian, acting as a supervisory angel over his body, keeping watch over every part of it.
The image continually reassures and gives glad tidings to the believer until it brings him to God, who calls him to an easy reckoning (hisab yasir).
When the believer asks the image who it is, it answers: 'I am a creation from the creation of my Lord, created from the joy (surur) you used to bring upon the believers, so today I make you happy.'
By God's decree, no particle can go astray; like a magnet each particle draws its connected particles, so the believer's parts cannot be scattered and progress to their station.
This is the reality of mubashshir and bashir for the friend (wali).

For the opponent, the evil dark magnet — the two knots (al-'uqdatan) — by the movement of the station moves the satanic dissolver (al-muhill al-iblisi) and the evil deeds, knowledge, enmity, and hatred he harbored against the people of truth.
One center (the Pillar of Light) was made for the good; two (the two knots) were made for the evil — only one is mentioned for the Pillar of Light but the knots are two.

The two knots were formed at the head of the snake when God made the celestial spheres (aflak); high beings of the world of light who took precedence into satanic nature (iblisiyyat) yet repented were placed there, kept high beneath the sphere of the moon rather than with the hellfire (saqar), by a specific intention of the 'ashir within divine providence.
Through the movement of the Imam's station, the decree (tadbir) of the Imam is in effect on the two knots, so the Imam also grants the requital of his opponents' evil deeds.

The opponent's dark disfigured form is what he acquired bit by bit from his evil; at his last minute he imagines a dark, disfigured, most-ugly person which he rejects, fears, and is horrified by, then it is cut off and he knows he is of the people of evil — this is the reality of Munkar and Nakir.
The Messenger of God alluded to this in his sermon to Qays ibn 'Asim: you have a companion who is buried with you alive while you are buried dead, and he will not be resurrected except with you.

If the companion is noble he honors you, and if base he abandons you; you are raised and questioned only about him, so make him only righteous — for he is your deed ('amal): your luminous form built by knowledge and deed is your provision for the hereafter, higher than your self (zat).
If the companion is righteous you find comfort only in him, and if obscene you feel terror only from him, for he is your deed.

Sayyidna Hamiduddin alluded to this in the third mashrab of the fourth tasawwur of Rahat al-'Aql where the opposite is mentioned: the interpretation of one's evil deeds is a harmful animal that harms and terrifies him.

Rahat al-'Aql by Sayyidna Hamiduddin is profoundly difficult (mughlaq); a learned Arabic scholar (the Nawab of Rampur) could not understand it, and Mawlana called it 'Kulfat al-'Aql' (agony of the intellect) for the uninitiated.

The dark form (surat zulmaniyyah) is formed from knowledge and deeds done contrary to God's commands, knowledge acquired from people from whom it should not be taken, and enmity held against the people of truth.

The dark form separates from the souls of bodies; the form's station is the two knots (uqdatayn), while the soul, instead of progressing with the form, expands within the body and acquires materiality — the opposite of believers' souls which progress with the form.
The dark form roams (ja'ilah) in the air and in vile places — latrines, places where blood flows, where wine and filthy forbidden things are made — because it is inclined toward what is forbidden.

The dark forms reach toward the barzakh which is dark and vile, namely the two knots (uqdatan); barzakh is the path between paradise and hell, and the uqdatayn is the quarantine/short-stay station before reaching their final hell.

For the punished (mu'adhdhabin) the uqdatayn (beneath the sphere of the moon) is the barzakh; their final destination is the sakhrah, where they remain until the Great Cycle (kawr-e-a'zam) of four hundred thousand cycles, each cycle being four hundred thousand years.

The dark forms pass in turn through the air, vile places, empty habitations, and terrifying wells (bir muhawwishah) before reaching the uqdatayn, and they are the blameworthy jinn given the subtle lower punishment each according to his measure.

It is necessary that every Imam in his time calls the punished jinn to Islam, for the Imam knows them by their names and places — as Sayyidna Ali did, calling each by name with nothing of their affair hidden from him.

Whoever among the punished completes his lower punishment ('adhab al-adna) and is permitted deliverance submits to the one who calls him, repents, and becomes one of the praiseworthy jinn (jinn al-mahmudin).
Upon becoming a praiseworthy jinn, he ascends from the side of the moon to the sphere of the sun, serving there as a servant (khadim) among the mustaqdimin in a glorious station.

The jinn-e-mustaqdimin respond to the call to prayer (adhan); Sayyidna Ali bin Sulayman recounts a crow that came at the adhan guiding lost travelers to a village, an instance illustrating the mustaqdimin.

The adhan recited by the saints (e.g. Hazrat Fathullah, Hazrat Ishaq, Hazrat Nasrullah, and the narrator at Arafat during Hajj) brought about miraculous reversals — receding floodwaters, redirected fires and winds.
There are one hundred and forty thousand mustaqdimin (suwarat-e-mustaqdimin) centered in the sun, who are entrusted ministering angels (mala'ikah).

Among the mustaqdimin are attractors (jadhibah) who draw up the praiseworthy forms, repellers (dafi'ah) who send forms down to the world, and restrainers (masikah) for what travels within; when one ascends another descends in his place to be born a believer, perpetually.
The one hundred and forty thousand mustaqdimin and the one hundred and twenty-four thousand prophets (anbiya') are separate counts and must not be confused.
The second chapter (al-bab al-thani) of the fourth path contains five sections (fusul).

Whoever among the mustakhdamin (those made to serve) completes his service is brought down to earth and travels into a thing from the edibles (ma'kulat) and drinkables (mashrubat), taking sustenance suited to him.

He then appears at the union (mulaqah) between the seed (nutfah) of the da'i and his wife as a trustee, progresses through the stages of the fetus (janin) until born a complete person, and is raised until puberty (bulugh).
At puberty he is called and responds, entering the circle of the people of truth (ahl al-haqq); he can be born to anyone but will come to the people of truth.

Because his purification is done and his service accepted, he progresses through the religious ranks (maratib al-diniyyah) in the swiftest and nearest manner, reaching the high ranks and lofty stations with no need ever to return.

He never returns because he fulfilled what was upon him of sins, repented, and accepted the caller of God (da'i Allah) in the beginning and in the end — in the beginning he accepted the covenant (qawl) in the world of light, and again here.
His swift progress is because he rendered his service, stood by his obligation, entered the sacred sanctuary (haram-e-amin), and obeyed the Lord of the worlds.

On the platform of this world gather various kinds of people — those destined for punishment by their prior states, and those who arrive with a clean slate now in the realm of free choice to accept or not.
As animals are halal or haram, so among arrivals some will progress (halal) and some descend (haram), and within halal some become food for a believer and some food for a disbeliever (kafir).
In the realm of free choice no one can pull a person from his choice between the straight and crooked path; the call is presented and he chooses.

Dark forms (suwarat-e-zulmah) can only progress by becoming mustakhdam: held in the uqdatayn, they complete the lower punishment, serve, are presented with the call, and if accepting become mustakhdam.

The station of the cursed forms (surat-e-la'inah) whose end was not good is the sakhrah; their barzakh is the uqdatayn, their bodies undergo the lower punishment in the world, and bodily purification occurs through halal animals.

The mustakhdamin remain in service until the rising of the Qa'im (qiyam-e-qa'im), after which accounting occurs, fire descends from the sky to burn the enemies' bodies, and they enter the sakhrah through its mouth, remaining there for one kawr — the greater punishment.

The lower punishment ('adhab-e-adna) has two forms: the punishment of the seven levels of hell (adrak) and the punishment of the peripheries (atraf); the great punishment ('adhab-e-akbar) is the punishment of the sakhrah.

Whoever refuses, is arrogant, and persists in disobedience and disbelief is made to tread the bridges (qanatir) of the lower bodily punishment until the Qa'im stands, then is made to tread the greater punishment.

Sayyidna Zu'ayb alluded in his Risalat al-Nafs: at every transition there is a halt (tawqif); if they repent they return to a higher rank, and if they insist they descend to the lowest rank, to the Great Cycle, the product of three hundred and sixty thousand multiplied by its like.

God said He will make them taste the lower punishment short of the greater punishment so that perhaps they may return — evidence that the lower punishment offers repeated chances to return, a mercy of God.

Amir al-Mu'minin indicated this in his saying 'wa yathanuhum al-dawru fi madarij al-kawr' — the cycle grinds them in the stages of the cycle; in every cycle they are presented the call, and if they reach the sakhrah, lava comes out of it.
The white days (ayyam-e-bid) are the thirteenth, fourteenth, and fifteenth, the best of days; of the 354 days in a year about one hundred fifty are distinguished days.
Changing the vowels (zabar, zer, pesh) or dropping/consuming words alters Allah's speech in the Qur'an by the time it reaches the servant, and this alteration becomes a cause of sin.

The completion (khatm) prayer affirms 'Sadaqa Allah' — Allah has spoken the truth, there is no god but Him, the Most Gracious and Merciful, nothing is like unto Him, and He is All-Hearing All-Knowing; His messengers delivered His messages and we are witnesses, in defiance of the deniers (irghaman lil-jahidin).

The one completing the Qur'an prays that God benefit him with it, make it the spring of hearts, healing of chests, remover of worries, atonement for sins, purification, and a guide and proof toward Him and toward the gardens of bliss in the company of prophets, truthful, martyrs, and righteous.

The completion prayer asks God to overlook errors in recitation — mistakes, forgetfulness, altering words from their places, changing a letter, transposition, addition, omission, wrong interpretation, doubt, haste, slips of the tongue, wrong stopping, wrong merging, wrong clarity, errors in extension, emphasis, hamza, jazm, or vocalization other than as written.
One must be extremely careful in saying, writing, or speaking the Qur'an because scribes often write something else and changes occur in Allah's word.
Adding words such as a virtue-saying within Yasin is an addition (ziyadah) and a sin; the letters of the Qur'an must not be changed, though words of separate prayers differ.
Madd (elongation) occurs when a vowel letter (alif, waw, ya) is followed by an alif or hamza, in order to clarify both letters distinctly (e.g. ula'ika, yasha'u, qa'idina).
There are six guttural letters (huruf halqi) — ha, kha, 'ayn, ghayn, and others — that must be pronounced properly from the throat; the science of recitation (ilm al-tajwid) details this.
Tashdid doubles a letter for two durations and must be pronounced clearly (e.g. iyya, sabbar); the final letter (e.g. the dal) must not be dropped.

The prayer continues: awaken us before death from the sleep of heedlessness, secure us from the punishment of the grave and the questioning of Munkar and Nakir and from being eaten by worms (didan), make our faces white on the Day of Resurrection, free our necks from the Fires, and protect from the evil of the reckoning and loss.
The vocalizations (i'rab) — zabar, zer, pesh — are placed upon the 28 letters of the alphabet.

The 28 letters correspond to the 28 of the Qisa-i Ibda'iyah; the Juz'-i Ibda'i manifested them materially in the world, having received them from the First Intellect via the kalimah 'La ilaha illa Allah,' which contains 28.

The vowels (i'rab) were placed on the 28 letters in the World of Intentions ('alam al-niyyat); the First Emanation (Munba'ith al-Awwal) also has 28, and every circle formed in every intellect, including the Imam's, reduces to 28 — a uniquely special number.

Each emanated being was given three things — life/existence, knowledge, and free will; those who used free will to come foremost (pesh-pesh) received a pesh, those who delayed remained with zabar, and those lower with zer, so the ranks of movement are pesh (highest), then zabar, then zer.

Jazm is a bent/crooked zabar (movement not straight); madd combines two movements; the doubled forms (maddo, madda, maddi) join a jazm with pesh, zabar, or zer respectively, signifying a joining of crooked and straight.

Madd commands elongation wherever two entities of the same nature meet whose distinction in rank must be clarified, because God created two same-rank entities that must differ — two individuals cannot hold the identical status.

These letters that came from the realm of spirits and the kalimah 'La ilaha illa Allah' constitute the original Arabic; the Qur'an names no language but Arabic ('bi-lisanin 'arabiyyin mubin'), the language God chose for His expression.

While reading the Qur'an the entire letter must be pronounced completely and clearly; turning a zabar into a zer or otherwise mispronouncing changes the meaning entirely (illustrated by the Arabic vs. Hindi 'ha' distinction).
It is good for all to read aloud in the gathering so mistakes can be known and corrected, or to read privately for correction, removing the barrier of reading.
The Maqamat (the Imams, peace be upon them) issue a call (du'a) both to humans, who are mortals, and to the jinn, who appear as 'these forms' (suwar).
The purpose of the Imams' call (tawqif, to make aware) is so that whoever is destined to turn back may turn back and whoever will insist on disbelief may insist.
Faith is established through three things: by word, by bringing truth into the heart, and by action.
Jinn who accept the call are assigned services within the rank of Shams and are then called jinn-e-mahmud (praised jinn) and mustaqdimin (the forerunners).
There is a permanent congregation of one hundred and forty thousand in the Shams; when one departs or falls, another becomes his successor (khalifa), keeping the number constant.

The call to these wretched forms and the response of those who answer is a manifestation of the miracle the Maqam reveals to those around him from among the ally (wali), the opponent (zidd), and the hypocrite (munafiq).

The miracle serves to make the establishment of proof (iqamat al-hujjah) greater and to reveal the clear path (mahajjah) more swiftly, so that the People of the Book gain certainty and believers increase in faith.
The miracle's purpose is so that he who is to perish perishes by a clear proof and he who is to live lives by a clear proof.
The Messenger of Allah sent companions of Amir al-Mumineen to Yemen with the command to call the jinn dwelling in the valley of Zahr and Musayyab.
The Prophet informed the companions of the jinn's names so they could call those jinn by name in the desolate well.
The Prophet declared that whoever the jinn answer would be the wasi (successor) of the Prophet — an incident narrated in detail in Sayyidna Hatim's work (Saluni).
The Prophet ordered that Abu Bakr call the jinn first; if they did not respond then Umar, then Uthman, and finally Ali ibn Abi Talib.
The Prophet declared that whoever among them the jinn answer is his wasi among them and his khalifa over them.
The Prophet declared that whoever obeys his answered successor has obeyed the Prophet and Allah, and whoever disobeys him has disobeyed the Prophet and Allah.
The Prophet's arrangement was meant to urge the companions toward obedience to and recognition (ma'rifah) of Amir al-Mumineen.

In Arabic grammar, the particle 'ila' is the last of the seventeen letters that govern the genitive (zer/kasra), yet the noun 'haythu' remains indeclinable (mabni) and is always read 'haythu' even after 'ila'.
Abu Bakr went forward alone and called out loudly to the named jinn, but no one answered, so he returned to his companions disappointed.
Umar likewise went forward and called the jinn loudly, but no one answered, and he returned disappointed.
Uthman did as his two companions had done, calling the jinn, and no one answered, so he too returned disappointed.
Ali ibn Abi Talib then went forward, his companions secretly following to observe; when he called out loudly the jinn answered one after another and responded to him.
Ali greeted the jinn with peace and they returned the greeting, addressing him as Amir al-Mumineen with 'wa alaykum al-salam wa rahmatullahi wa barakatuh'.
Ali then called the jinn to the two testimonies (shahadatayn): 'There is no god but Allah, Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah'.
Those jinn who testified affirmed Allah's Oneness (wahdaniyyah) and Muhammad's Messengership and servitude (abduhu wa rasuluh), and Ali's wilayah as Amir al-Mumineen.
Two of the jinn took bodily form and accompanied Ali; they were named Abdullah Mard-shah and Abdullah Ard-shah.
The two jinn reached the Messenger of Allah, renewed their Islam before him, and their Islam became excellent, then they returned to their companions at the Well of Alam.
This affair was among the greatest miracles for the Natiq and the Wasi, yet it increased the hypocrites (the first and second who went) only in distance and disbelief.

Amir al-Mumineen descended into the Well of Dhat al-Alam twice to commune with the jinn there, killing those of them he killed and accepting the Islam of those who submitted — a separate incident from the San'a (Wadi Zahr/Musayyab) episode.
Ham bin al-Him came to the Prophet while he sat in his mosque among the Muslims and greeted him with a voice that was heard though his person was not seen.
Ham identified himself as Ham son of Him, son of Laqis, son of Iblis, and stated he had accepted Islam for the Prophets Nuh, then Ibrahim, then Musa, then Isa.
Ham bore witness that there is no god but Allah and that Muhammad is His servant and Messenger, which was among the greatest miracles, yet it increased the disbelievers only in aversion.
After his Islam for Nuh, Ham ascended to the rank of Shams through the intermediary of the Qamar (moon).
At the appearance of each successive Natiq (Ibrahim, then Musa and Isa, then Muhammad) Ham descended from his rank to accept Islam anew for that Natiq, then returned to his place.
In Arabic, the names Ibrahim, Ishaq, and Yaqub are non-Arab (Hebrew) and indeclinable, taking a zabar (fatha) rather than zer (kasra) even in the genitive case (li Ibrahima).
When Muhammad appeared Ham descended to accept Islam for him, was then made to die (tuwuffiya), and returned in the swiftest time to the lofty stature (qamah saniyah).
It is necessary for everyone among the jinn who accepted Islam in past eras to accept Islam for Muhammad, who is the sixth Natiq.
By the completion of Muhammad (the sixth Natiq) the creation of the religious body (jism al-dini) is completed.
Such a believing jinn ascends through the ranks until reaching the rank of the Bab (Gate), which is the limit of infallibility (hadd al-ismah).
The rapid ascent of ranks up to the Bab applies to the mustaqdimin (forerunners), who because of their long service can attain a rank higher than ordinary believers.
Both the Imam and the Bab al-Abwab (Gate of Gates) possess ismah (infallibility).
Amir al-Mumineen declared from the pulpit 'Saluni qabla an tafqiduni' (Ask me before you lose me), an incident recorded in Saluni and in Tawil al-Da'a'im.

When asked 'Where is Jibril?' Ali looked in every direction, could not find Jibril, and concluded that the questioner himself was Jibril (Ana azunnu anta Jibril), naming his lineage — a sign of Ali's knowledge.
The evil form (surat al-khabitha) separated from souls is the utmost evil for wickedness, standing in opposition to the noble end which is the utmost good.
Even evil forms sometimes speak true things and give accurate news because, while truthful in the era of the natiq, they rendered service and the truth they earned is rewarded and never lost.
Evil has no root in creation (al-sharr la asla lahu fil-ibda'), so a person's earlier truth and good service survive even after corruption and are rewarded.
Allah's justice does not let any deed, small or large, of good or evil be wasted, as proven by the verse 'whoever does an atom's weight of good/evil will see it'.
The apparent desert ghouls (al-ghilan al-zahira) mentioned by the Messenger affect mainly bedouins and children, and amulets and incantations work only out of fear of their evil.

Recitation and seeking refuge (ta'awwudh) at sleep — including Qul a'udhu, and the supplication against Allah's plan/forgetting His remembrance/heedlessness — was commanded specifically as protection from these ghouls.
Seeking refuge (saying A'udhu billahi min al-rijs al-najis) is prescribed in dark, filthy places like urinals out of fear of the evil forms there.
Jinn who submit (aslama) from the high-station forms are the praiseworthy jinn (al-jinn al-mahmudun); those who persist in disobedience are the blameworthy jinn (al-jinn al-madhmumun).
Many in the Rightly-Guiding Mission (Da'wat al-Hadiya) deny the jinn's existence due to scarcity of knowledge, self-sufficiency, and abandoning allegiance to the appointed hudud.

The jinn are the people of inward knowledge (ahl 'ilm al-batin) and humans the people of outward knowledge (ahl 'ilm al-zahir), and both the interpretive sense and a real physical existence are simultaneously true.
The people of the inward are called jinn because of their concealment (ijnan/satr), and they divide into praiseworthy and blameworthy types.

The praiseworthy inward folk are those ordered in the thread of truth and its ranks, holding fast to the laws of tawhid, knowing the stations — and they are the divine philosophers (falasifat al-ilahiyyun).

The blameworthy second type are the negating philosophers (falasifat al-mu'attilun) who deny the intermediaries — the nuqaba', awsiyya', a'imma and their hudud — and are more astray than all sects, being the devils and Satans.
Among humans, the praiseworthy uphold the unaltered statutes of the shari'a with chastity, purity and soundness of soul, free of hatred for the people of truth, and they are few.
The blameworthy humans outwardly uphold the shari'a and display piety but conceal falsehood and hostility to the people of the Da'wat al-Hadiya, and they alter the law.
Allah commanded wiping (mash) the head and feet in ablution; one who washes the feet believing washing is the obligation (rather than wiping) invalidates his prayer.

The virtuous, knowledgeable, active person persists until he becomes prepared to establish the shari'a and receive revelation, and on leaving the world becomes an angel in actuality (malak bil-fi'l), entering the company of angels.

The Author of the Epistles' statement alludes to the People of Truth who uphold the truth in the two worships — outward worship being action ('amal) and inward worship being knowledge ('ilm) — connected to the divine stations.
The assembly of angels (zumrat al-mala'ikah) the virtuous soul enters is the noble temple (al-haykal al-sharif).
Through ignorance of his Originator and His friends the opposite becomes an enemy of his Lord, claims what he does not deserve, and becomes the Imam of error and chief of ignorance.

When the opposite departs the world with his body he becomes the shaitan of his own soul; his soul does not leave the body but descends to the lowest of the low, whispering and inspiring his likes with specious words just as angels inspire prophets.

Ruh and Nafs are often synonymous, but the rational soul (nafs al-natiqah) is distinct from the vegetative (namiyah) and sensory (hissiyah) souls; the Ruh is the command of the Lord (Qul al-ruhu min amri Rabbi), the divine support (ta'idat) descending as the first perfection.
Death is the departure of the nafs (soul) from the body, not the departure of the Ruh (the command).

By 'his ignorance of his Originator' the speaker means the opposite is no gnostic of Allah nor of His hudud who clarify the sciences of tawhid, tanzih and tajrid and make Him known in the beginning, the return, and its end.

Tawhid means each hadd is created unique in essence so the hierarchy holds; tanzih is declaring Allah transcendent of all attributes; tajrid is that the creation of beings (ijad al-zawat) belongs to none but the First Originator (Mubdi' al-Awwal).

By 'his Lord' in 'he became an enemy to his Lord' is meant the Imam of the Time; the false claim is partnership (shirk) in the Imam's station and claim to his rank, fulfilling 'We made them leaders inviting to the Fire'.

By 'satanic soul' is meant the evil conception (tasawwur) the opposite formed from enmity to the Imam and the hudud; it alone departs and is called a satanic soul, just as the People of Truth's conception is called an angelic soul.
The sensory soul does not depart the body but transforms with the body's transformation toward the noble rank.
The vegetative soul descends from the sphere of the moon, the sensory soul from the sun, and the rational soul from Mujrima; their three centers are moon, sun, and Mujrima respectively.

At death the luminous form (surat nuraniyyah) separates and ascends to the person's higher rank (hadd-e 'ali) and merges with its form, so that if that hadd later strays the good form can be detached and preserved since Allah does not waste good.

The departing evil form roams between the celestial sphere and earth, presenting itself to people in human or satanic form, appearing in dreams to evil souls, and uniting with dark bodies to speak blasphemies, abominations, and predictions through their tongues.

Hearers of the evil form's speech regard it as truthful in all it predicts, because in the era of the natiq it had rendered service and spoken truth, for which it is compensated by accurate prediction.
Evil spirits have freedom because they lack physical constraints, so they can descend on people in sleep and utter truths mixed with disbelief; their words must not be verified or treated as karamat.
Following such spirits' mixed truth and falsehood causes destruction (halak) for the hearer; the straight path is obedience to Allah, the Messenger, and those in authority (Uli'l-amr).
key_terms: ati'ullaha wa ati'u al-rasula wa uli al-amr

teaching: Both humans and jinn act as the whispering enemy behind the scenes; refuge is sought from both in the Mu'awwidhatayn (Qul a'udhu).

After leaving a possessed body the evil form ascends to the two knots ('uqdatan), the dark celestial barzakh that magnetically attracts it, where its satanism and enmity become firmly rooted before descending again to earth.
Evil spirits' station is at the markers (amyal) around the Ka'bah and at Safa, Marwah and the place of pelting, but not inside the Ka'bah or in the sacred presences (hadarat) where angels descend.

Gathered at the two knots, the evil forms increase in satanism, disbelief, distance and denial, then descend to earth and reach the thousand-year stature (al-qamat al-alfiyyah), becoming devils in actuality (shayatin bil-fi'l).

Evil forms attach to whoever opposes the People of Truth, inciting and aiding them, until their time to take retributions (qisasat) comes; they cannot act against everyone, only those with whom dues (baqiyat) are pending.

The lowest of the low (asfal al-safilin) is the rank these devils occupy because there is no rank beneath it nor anything viler than it; refuge is sought from their evil breaths (nufus) and suggestions (hamazat).

When the disobedient souls reach the final link of the chain prepared for their punishment, the angels of punishment plunge them in and the wrathful angel (malik al-ghadban) drives them to the form of pure darkness.

In the rock (sakhrah) the punished soul perceives in its own essence the figures of the chain it traversed and the waves of Hell, raised to the heat of the ether and dropped to the cold of zamharir, with devils mingling and angels stoning it with meteors.

The lesser punishment ('adhab al-adna) comprises the seven stages (adrak) of the chain and the punishment of the four peripheries (atraf); the greater punishment ('adhab al-akbar) is the rock, which comes after the Qa'im appears.

After completing peripheral punishments the evil souls and bodies are present before the Qa'im, who judges them; fire descends from their forms, burns body and soul, and they enter the rock through its gates.

The dark form (surat zulmaniyyah) has no permanence (baqa) because it was created by a wrong method, while the luminous form (surat nuraniyyah), light and truth have permanence — though not eternity — for evil/darkness is merely distance from truth/light.

When a person passes through punishments, his evil conception (tasawwur) is finished, and after the punishments end the residual evil in his essence is also finished; the soul then re-enters the world of choice with a fresh series and is given free choice.
The lesser punishment is the seven stages God mentioned: 'Seize him and shackle him, then cast him into Hell, then insert him into a chain whose length is seventy cubits'.
After judgment by the Qa'im, the rays of Saturn (Zuhal) and Mars (Mirrikh) and the two knots hand the evil forms over to the middle of the rock, where the Sun, Moon, Venus and Mercury have no access.
The punishment in the middle of the rock lasts as long as the heavens and earth endure — the Greatest Cycle (qawl-e a'zam) of 360,000 solar years (400,000 lunar) multiplied by itself.

'And the wrathful angel drives it' refers to the Tenth Intellect ('aql al-'ashir), the administrator (mudabbir) and owner of the entire world of nature who arranges everything in its rank and is wrathful against every sinner.
The Tenth Intellect is the gate of the world of sanctity ('alam al-quds) just as the sun is the gate of the world of nature and the hujjah is the religious gate (bab dini) of each Imam.

Ridwan, treasurer of paradise (khazin al-jinan), is the name for the gate serving righteous souls, while malik al-ghazban serves sinners; both are servants of the Tenth Intellect, the end of every soul.
The sun is named after Ridwan because it is a magnet for every praiseworthy thing and the destination of pleased spiritual and righteous outward souls; bad things are drawn to Saturn and Mars.
Auspicious times are determined by planetary hours; on Friday the first hour is Venus (Zuhra), then Mercury, Moon, Saturn, Jupiter, Mars, with the time stated after reciting Bismillah.
The name malik al-ghazban also falls upon Saturn (Zuhal), who is in charge of causing sinners' souls to fall beneath the rock by its rays and the rays of the two knots.

In the rock the punished souls retain full memory of every stage of the lesser and greater torment they traversed through their disobedience to the lofty stations and their hudud — and this remembering is itself a torment.
The northern direction is the center of zamharir (cold) and the southern direction the center of ether (heat); the punished journey there after fully receiving the torment of the cycles.
The 'devils falling with it' refers to the punished souls' misleading scholars and chiefs who are entrusted alongside them in these loathsome torments.

The angels stoning them with meteors of torment is what flows to them from the curses of the disembodied intellects ('uqul mujarradah) and from the hudud and believers cursing them, spreading their vices and praying against them, since the hudud are angels in potentiality.

Being driven off from every side refers to bringing the evil forms to the filthy plains (biqa' khabithah) prepared for their torment and removing them from the inhabited land, which is a decorated paradise by comparison.

Amir al-Mu'minin recited Surat al-A'la for a month at Fajr, explaining its closing verses ('this is in the former scriptures of Abraham and Moses') as the inheritance of the prophets' scriptures received from the Prophet.

The scale of justice (mizan al-'adl) is established by Allah upon all His servants — wali, exoteric person, or opponent (didd) — leaving out neither small nor large deed but enumerating it, and recompensing good with good and evil with evil.
key_terms: la yughadiru saghiratan wa-la kabiratan illa ahsaha

teaching: The natiq passed away poisoned and his wasi (Amir al-Mu'minin) killed; likewise Hasan, Husayn, al-Mustansir and al-'Amir passed by poison or being killed — and this befell them by the requirement of wisdom and the demand of justice as retribution (qisas).
Even the Friends of Allah, the chosen and trustees over His revelation, are subject to qisas with no escape; had pardon (musamaha) been permissible for anyone they would be most deserving of it.
A person's deeds extend to and are accounted against the people of his era, so retribution due from one era can be exacted in another — as Imam Husayn bore recompense for battles of Mawla Ali.

There is no escape from the scale of justice for any creature — noble or base, mighty or humble — and Allah shows no favoritism (muhabat) in any act of good or evil, as in 'whoever does an atom's weight of good/evil will see it'.

Everything a person does of good or evil returns to him as recompense except what the shari'a makes lawful and is delivered by mutual consent and submission — like marriage on Allah's Book and the Prophet's sunna, in which there is no qisas.
Good deeds earn a tenfold reward and evil deeds a single recompense; evil (sharr) and sin (gunah) differ, with sin born from evil.

Sins against Allah are forgiven by Allah through repentance, but rights/retributions owed to His servants are not forgiven until the servant forgives or Allah arranges means for the dues to reach the wronged party, else qisas occurs.
Acts done lawfully by the shari'a's command — such as killing on a valid order — do not obligate retribution.
Stoning for adultery (zina) is commanded collectively by Allah's order to remove the collective harms that such acts breed in the community, and it was the command in earlier religions too.

The Prophet said no scratch of a twig, throbbing of a vein, or stumbling of a foot afflicts anyone except by a sin (dhanb), and what Allah forgives is much more — meaning such afflictions are pending retributions.

Unaccepted supplications in the world are stored and rewarded on the Day of Judgment, and a sacrifice (intended for a sick person who still dies) yields its benefit, multiplied in the next cycle if not reached in this one.

A man's delivering the present gift, dower, possession and mutual consent with shari'a's permission nullifies any right of qisas; but intercourse without shari'a's permission or without delivering dower obligates qisas.

Qisas became obligatory on the Imams (maqamat) for their lawful actions because there was no mutual consent from the killed party, and it may be exacted in the same cycle or a previous one — illustrated by 'the master served his slave' (khadam al-mawla 'abdahu): prophets served the hidden Imams, repaid by the Prophet through Mawla Ali.

The kalima La ilaha illallah relates to numerical structures (negative/positive, dotted/undotted letters) such as 'ayn-lam-ya being three letters and the letters yielding totals of 40, 70, and 12 through their compositions.

In Ali were combined seventy special characteristics (khususiyat), each testified to by Allah and His Messenger, that could not be gathered in any other person (in whom more than ten could not combine).
Ali delivered extempore (murtajjal/fil-badih) sermons demonstrating his mastery — a roughly three-page khutba containing no alif, and a thirteen-page khutba containing no dotted letters.
Umar said 'Lawla Ali lahalaka Umar' (Were it not for Ali, Umar would have perished) — recorded as said seventy times.

The deeds of the Imams and their friends — jihad against opposites, killing, applying hadd, stoning by command of Allah and the Imam — earn a reward that returns to their luminous structures (hayakil nuraniyya) and souls even while the qisas remains in place.

Killing in self-defense (dafa'-i hifazat), by the command of Allah, the Messenger, or those in authority, is rewarded though its qisas also remains; such deeds seeking Allah's reward are not lost (their reward not wasted) but the fullest requital still applies.

The qisas of the opposites falls upon their dense bodies (katha'if) by Allah's command, due to the aversion (karahiya) of the opposites' souls to what was done to them and their lack of pleasure in it — distinguishing defense from those who initiate bloodshed.
Inheritance law arises at death (not lifetime gifts/hiba), and a gift in terminal illness (marad al-mawt) has no consideration; valid hiba requires giving possession.

In inheritance the parents each receive one-sixth, the husband a fourth (or eighth with children), the wife an eighth (or fourth without children); the order of death between mother and child decides who inherits.
The scale of justice is established by Allah even in the date-stone's membrane (qitmir) and groove (naqir) — i.e., in the most minute matters.

The Imams' actions against their opposites in their cycles are taking qisas from them for deeds committed in previous cycles and ages, which divine providence ('inaya ilahiyya) necessitated by gathering them in the Imams' time as justice and requital for their sins.

Mawla Ali composed the grammatical maxim that every doer is nominative (kullu fa'ilin marfu'un), every object accusative (kullu maf'ulin mansubun), every genitive broken (kullu majrurin maksurun) — esoterically: the one who acts is elevated, the imitator supported, the one needing to be drawn is broken.

Passing the hand over the face at Bismillah symbolizes the connection (ittisal) between the five upper and five lower limbs of the body, mirroring the connection of the five luminous essences ('aql, nafs, jadd, fatah, khayal) with the five worldly essences (Imam, Bab, Hujjat, Da'i, Ma'dhun).

Bismillah al-Rahman al-Rahim is the highest summary, but La ilaha illallah is higher; its 28 letters split into 15 dotted and 13 undotted, while Bismillah shows five repeated letters facing five non-repeated (khamsatun bi-iza'i khamsah).

The five non-repeated letters of Bismillah correspond to the five Luminous-Realm individuals who need not manifest, the five repeated to those who manifest in the world repeatedly, their connection forming one kalima — paralleling the body and the spiritual realm.

La ilaha illallah is the light of the word (nur-e kalima) from God; Bismillah and all Quranic verses descended from the Circle of the First Intellect / Circle of Origination, but their entire source is La ilaha illallah.

Acts a person does that the shari'a has not made lawful and the Imam has not commanded — killing one's own kind, looting, usurping, taking by oppression or treachery — quickly darken the soul's essence and become a barrier between it and the path of guidance.

Whether a sin is erased after the Imam applies a hadd depends on the qisas of the Mudabbir across the cycles and returns (karrat), of which each Imam has 360; the Prophet said one who seeks forgiveness (istighfar), even seventy times, is not among the persistent sinners.

Sins against Allah are forgiven through seeking forgiveness, but rights of His servants are not forgiven until that servant forgives or Allah arranges means (like the Bitaq method) to bring the recompense to the wronged.

The darkened soul is driven into the paths of error, ensnared in sins, made to hate the hudud and the people of truth, and cast into the fire of Hell — but the Quran says the disbelievers abide (khalidina) without 'forever' (abada), unlike the believers' eternal gardens, a mercy from Allah.
Vile acts like adultery (zina) inescapably require qisas (la budda min al-qisas), with the soul's essence darkening, eclipsing and descending.
The qisas for human major sins is exacted quickly in the descending garments (qumus): human form (Riss), then monkey-like (Waqs), 'Aks, Khars, then mineral, passing through the seven stages.

Remaining qisas for adultery passes into the Qamis al-Waqs, the human-like composition (monkey, nasnas, etc.), because copulation among monkeys exceeds that of other animals; the nasnas is a northern species said to have faces on their chests and to stand on one leg.

When many men sin with one woman, the qisas is distributed across the descending garments — some in Riss, most in Waqs and 'Aks and Khars and other descended animals — proportional to the abundance or scarcity of the act.

The descending forms (qumus) are temporary; only the thousand-year stature (Qamat-e Alfiyyah) has a (contingent) permanence, being the form on which the luminous essences and the world were created, with density and atoms stripped away stage by stage.

Qisas and punishment apply in the descending animal stages despite the acts there occurring with consent and payment, because the original human act was done without the shari'a's permission, though the form of punishment differs.
The descending garments (darakat) apply to adultery and its likes (theft, robbery, usurpation), whereas the opponents of the Imam descend into the lower levels (adrak) rather than the darakat.
The 27th of Rajab unites three events: Ali's birth (30 years before), the Prophet's mission (Mab'ath, when Ali was 10 and the Prophet 40), and Laylat al-Isra'.

On the Night of Ascension Allah raised the Prophet to the knowledge of His Kingdom (malakut), informed him of the limits of the heavens, taught him the unseen, favored him over all prophets and brought him near the celestial limits.
Fifty prayers were made obligatory and reduced to five at Moses' counsel during the Ascension; the lecturer holds the Prophet was more correct to accept five, given prayer's great blessings.

The verse 'Glory to Him who took His servant by night from al-Masjid al-Haram to al-Masjid al-Aqsa' declares the Creator's transcendence; God showed His signs (ayat), not Himself, and the inability to grasp comprehension is itself comprehension (al-'ajzu 'an dark al-idrak idrakun) — a saying of Ali.
God took 'His servant' ('abd), not 'the prophet' or 'the messenger', because servitude precedes messengership, as in the testimony 'Muhammad is His servant and His messenger' ('abduhu wa rasuluhu).

In ta'wil 'night' (layl) is an example of the veil and concealment (sitr/kitman) of the inner dimension; God concealed the Prophet and made him travel in the inner world between himself and the Completer (mutimm) of his era, who is the sixth Imam (Abu Talib).

The Prophet's elevation by 40 years signifies completing 40 stages of prophethood then becoming messenger, surpassing all prophets; reaching qaba qawsayni aw adna (Abd al-Muttalib and Abu Talib as the two bows, Abdullah as adna), attaining the rank of the veil (hijabiyya) below 'Ayn Hazira (the Originator).

The verse 'they feed the indigent, orphan, and captive' is interpreted: miskin = the Da'i from whom hearts find peace, yatim = a high-ranking one whose supporters were finished, asir = one imprisoned where evil scholars controlled — each freed by the call of the five companions (Ali, Fatima, Hasan, Husayn, Fidda).

On the Ascension the Prophet saw the greatest signs of his Lord with the sight of the pure soul that did not swerve (ma zagha al-basar), narrated by A'isha that he never left her, indicating the vision was of the soul, not bodily absence.

The Buraq in ta'wil is the flashing, illuminating knowledge (al-'ilm al-mubriq) — the bayan, above the knowledge of the successor (lahiq) and below the Imam's knowledge; riding it is mastery over it, and ascension to heaven is being informed of its kingdom.

God showed Abraham the kingdom of the heavens and earth (malakut), meaning the spiritual world after the loftiness of his rank, and the earthly kingdom means the physical hudud (star, moon, sun) from whom he learned in the beginning.

The Prophet led all the prophets in prayer (esoterically his call to all nations), with Abraham as the muezzin at Safa and Marwah; he was sent to all nations whereas other prophets were sent only to their specific peoples.

The Prophet conveyed the knowledge he received to his foundation (asas) and instructed transmission one to one to each successor; al-Masjid al-Aqsa is the mutimm upon whom initiation is forbidden, and the blessing (baraka) is the support and initiation.
