When the fallen insisted on their claim of equality, their essences darkened (azlamat dhawatuhum) after being luminous, they became estranged from the darkness and entangled with one another, becoming the First Matter (al-hayula al-ula).

Three successive movements of the fallen essences produced first length (al-tul al-awwal), then first width (al-'ard al-awwal), then first depth (al-'umq al-awwal), until they became one body (jism wahid) intermingled together.

The reversal of the movements was from the wisdom of the 'Ashir, who was the mutawalli (manager) responsible for governing the disobedient group and arranged for them an abode (dar), instruments (alat), and a call to salvation.

The disobedient varied in their inner intentions and fell into three categories: the repentant seekers of forgiveness (nadim mustaghfir), the doubting bewildered (shakk mutahayyir), and the insistent arrogant (musirr mustakbir).
Sayyidna Isma'il ibn Hibatullah al-Makrami (Da'i al-Shumukh) in his book al-Kawakib al-Durriyyah explained that the hayula divided into 70 parts: 15 repentant, 20 doubters, and 35 insistent.

The recurrence of 70 in tasbihat (e.g. reciting 'Ya Karimu ya Rahimu ya 'Azim, ya ghiyath al-mustaghithin' seventy times) corresponds to the 70 sections of the hayula, and the ghiyath al-mustaghithin invoked is the 'Ashir al-Mudabbir.

The repentant group was noble and did not blame the 'Ashir; they praised and glorified him as they descended, ending with 'al-hamdu lillahi rabb al-'alamin' — where the Lord of the worlds refers to the 'Ashir al-Mudabbir — so their return (raj'at) happened quickly.
The Prophet's ummah dividing into 73 sects corresponds to the 70 sections plus three (the most severe insistent, the most severe doubter, and the purest repentant).

The post-fard tasbih (Allahu Akbar, Alhamdulillah, Subhanallah 33 times each, ending with La ilaha illa Allah) symbolizes the namiya, hissiyya, and natiqa faculties with the noble form, or the Imam's nasut tabi'i, nasut dhilli, nasut khass with his sura sharif.

The tasbih of the sunnat al-fajr ('Subhana rabbi al-'azim wa-bi-hamdihi, astaghfirullah al-'azim wa-atubu ilayh') is the very tasbih the repentant seekers of forgiveness (nadimin mustaghfirin) recited as they fell.
The munajat of the istiftah ('ya rabbi zalamtu nafsi fa-ghfir li... la yaghfiru al-dhanb al-'azim illa anta ya 'Aliyyu ya 'Azim') is from Imam Husayn ibn 'Ali.

Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq narrated that the Lord asks the angels what His servants say in their prostration, and upon hearing they confess wronging their souls and seek His forgiveness, He makes the angels witnesses that He has forgiven and pardoned them.
Allah forgives all sins ('Inna Allah yaghfiru al-dhunub jami'an', 'La taqnatu min rahmat Allah') except shirk, which the Quran calls al-zulm al-'azim.

The 'illa anta' that alone forgives the great sin refers to the Imam of the time, ultimately the 'ayn al-akhirah — the Qa'im 'ala dhikrihi al-salam — who holds the jami'iyyat of 400,000 years (seven satr and seven kashf) and is the qasim al-nar wa-l-jannah (divider of Fire and Garden).
Mawlana 'Ali is also called qasim al-nar wa-l-jannah in a partial sense.
At the gate of paradise people will be stopped and questioned about the walayat of 'Ali — a question on which the great Sunni scholars and all Shia agree.
The forms (suwar) of a believer across successive cycles unite and merge with the later forms, so souls progress across cycles toward settlement.

Yunus, sahib al-hut, said 'la ilaha illa anta, subhanaka inni kuntu min al-zalimin' — combining tawhid, tasbih, and istighfar — and 'la ilaha illa anta' appears only once in the Quran, of greater status than all other forms, directed toward the 'ayn al-'azimah.
Yunus did his tasbih for 40 days, and had he not done it he would have remained in the fish until the Day of Resurrection (yawm yub'athun).
The number 40 carries a power of maturity: a person reaches maturity at 40, the Prophet was made a messenger at age 40, and if 40 people gather and pray for someone their prayer is accepted.

'Umar ibn al-Khattab was the 40th person to accept Islam, upon which the Messenger said Islam had gained strength — likened (per Qutb al-Din) to a house declared built once its final part is completed.

From the 'Ashir's (the Mover's) first motion of the hayula were created the awtad al-falak (pegs of the spheres), four non-visible constellations: tali' (ascendant, east), gharib (descendant, west), 'ashir (mid-sky), and rabi' (under the earth).

When the density overflowed, the four awtad and the two poles (qutba al-falak from north and south) pulled it and held it in the middle of the sphere, the falak encompassing it from all sides like the white and shell encompass an egg's yolk.
The atmosphere split and the spheres were arranged into nine, each sphere contained within the one after it like the layers of an onion.
The falak al-muhit (encompassing sphere) surrounds all spheres and moves them every day and night with one total divine motion by the governing power of the mudabbir, from east to west.

There are seven spheres from Zuhal (Saturn) down to the moon, and all stars reside in the eighth sphere, named the falak al-buruj (sphere of constellations) — just as all believers ultimately gather at the Bab al-Abwab.
The falak al-buruj is divided into twelve constellations (buruj), each with 30 houses, totaling 360 degrees.
The spiritual essences (fudala) ascend through all 360 degrees of the zodiac for purification, traversing them in roughly 720 years of going and coming plus 280 years.

The Quran's 'wa lakum fi al-qisasi hayatun ya uli al-albab' means our very life runs within the vast circle of qisas (retribution), spread across many cycles, not merely that retribution occurs within our life.
The ninth sphere (falak al-muhit) is empty of constellations and planets due to its subtlety and nobility — just as no form gathers with the 'Aql al-Awwal / Mubda' al-Awwal in the spiritual realm.

Two du'at gave two counts of the intellects collected at the Mubda' al-Awwal: Sayyidna 'Ali bin Sulayman said 28 (seeing the 'uqul in totality), Sayyidna Hasan bin Nuh said 12 (the letters of 'La ilaha illa Allah') — both are correct, differing only in perspective.
The Imam takes the forms (suwarat) but the Mubda' al-Awwal does not take them; the governing decisions are made by the 'Aql al-Awwal even though the forms gather at the Mubda' al-Awwal.
When the Imam hands the gathered collection of forms (the imamat) to his farzand, the farzand — previously an Imam in potential made of riya' — goes from potential to actual.

Upon the Imam's passing the Bab al-Abwab also passes away and becomes the heart (qalb) of the Imam's farzand; this is illustrated by the death of Mawlana Abu Talib (the Imam) followed three days later by Khadija (his hujjat) in the Prophet's Year of Grief.
Mawlatuna Khadija is the Bab al-Abwab of Bibi Fatimah al-Zahra.

When the spheres cast their rays toward the earth, something of their nature returned to their essences and shells (asdaf) formed upon the non-visible spheres, rendering the stars visible but introducing negativity (nahusat) — so Zuhal, pure in essence, acquired inauspiciousness through its sadaf.

The stars in their original state were notional (wahmiyya) and invisible like the spheres; the Mudabbir made the asdaf by His wisdom so they would be perceptible and illuminate the dark physical world.

At the 'Ashir's call the fallen disobeyed saying 'la nasma'u wa la nuti'', accepting only the Mabda' Ta'ala and claiming equality (sawa'an bi-sawa'), thereby acknowledging only the first perfection while denying the second perfection attained by the intellects and the Mubda' al-Awwal.
Isbagh al-wudu' is performing ablution thoroughly three times; there is no established virtue (la fadila lahu) in doing it beyond the third, though one praying alone is not forbidden from more.
One leading prayer must not prolong tasbihat or recite long surahs, as weak or weary followers cannot bear it.
Density (kathafa) brings a being down while subtlety (latafa) raises it; spiritual progress is attained through subtlety, and the hayula fell from the realm of purity due to density.

The 'Ashir arranged the physical world by rank of purity: the seven spheres and planets from the purest (the repentant nadimin), the four mothers (fire, air, water, earth) from the middling (the doubters and bewildered), and the sakhra (core of the earth) from the densest (the insistent and arrogant).

The falak al-muhit, encompassing the entire realm, is called the gate of the spiritual world ('alam al-quds); beyond it lies first the world of life ('alam al-hayat), not directly the spiritual world.

Of those who repented with the 'Ashir's repentance, the group 'Ta'ibu bi-Tawbatihi' ascended as intellects with his group, while another group ('Labbu Nida'ahu', who answered his call) had a separate world of life created for them, containing the tamur (repository) and the spiritual Ka'ba connected to the physical Ka'ba.

The 'alam al-niyyat (world of intention) is the upper realm of our intentions at origination; after origination we remained passive, not joining the intellects who affirmed God's oneness, until we fell into the 'Ashir's illusory equality, and there our world of intention was established by our differing consciences.
The tamur, above the falak al-muhit in the world of life, holds the original essences of the mohtajibin (the veiled ones of the Imams) who did not enter the spiritual world.
The Prophet's mi'raj (ascension) reached only the falak al-muhit and then returned, because beyond it one cannot return without becoming an intellect.

The twelve constellations of the falak al-buruj are: Hamal (Aries), al-Thawr (Taurus), al-Jawza' (Gemini), al-Sartan (Cancer), al-Asad (Leo), al-Sunbula (Virgo), al-Mizan (Libra), al-'Aqrab (Scorpio), al-Qaws (Sagittarius), al-Jady (Capricorn), al-Dalw (Aquarius), and al-Hut (Pisces).

The seven planetary spheres in order are Zuhal (Saturn), Mushtari (Jupiter), Mirrikh (Mars), Shams (Sun), Zuhra (Venus), 'Utarid (Mercury), and Qamar (Moon); from their revolutions arose the spheres of ether and air (kurra-e-asir, kurra-e-nasim) and the four mothers.

The governing being assigned the planets to administer the physical world in sequence under Zuhal's overall governance (Mushtari, Mirrikh, Shams, Zuhra, 'Utarid as helpers), and in the seventh thousand-year period the first human came into being under Qamar's partnership.
The spheres revolve around the earth (with the Ka'ba as center point), not around the sun; modern science has changed its position on this three times.

The Mudabbir Ta'ala made the opposites (azdad) of the celestial bodies by His wisdom to illuminate the dark physical world, and the senses perceiving them confirms the power of the Planner and the soundness of the celestial world.
When the falak al-muhit moved, the atmosphere below the moon's sphere reached extreme heat and dryness — the nature of fire — and was named asir (ether), the first of the four mothers.

Every sphere has its own kawkab except the falak al-muhit and the falak al-buruj; the falak al-muhit is invisible (ghair-mar'i) and its single 24-hour total motion, called the divine motion, drives all the spheres and planets below it.

After death a person is divided into three: the surat-e-sharif goes instantly to its hadd-e-'ali on earth; the middle part (riyat), released after three days, goes to the spheres (mainly the moon's, also Jupiter and the Sun) to be refined; and the body's purification proceeds to the falak al-buruj over 360 years.
The body's purification journey through the zodiac takes 720 years ascending and descending plus 280 years, returning after 1000 years minus its namiya, hissiya, and natiqa faculties.
In one kaur (cycle) a believer's fuzlah repeats 360 times, and Sayyidna 'Ali wrote that a believer's body contains 360 nufus, each of which progresses each cycle by becoming a nafs.

If a believer's hadd-e-'ali has passed away with a good end, his form merges (muwazajat) with it; if the hadd-e-'ali is still alive, his form remains in the vicinity (jiwar) — guarding against loss should the hadd-e-'ali go astray.
If a hadd-e-'ali goes astray, the ascending one's form is removed and he is given another hadd-e-'ali.

When one who served the da'wat goes astray, his luminous form (surat-e-nayyirah) earned by his good deeds is separated from his bad form — as Da'ud ibn Qutb's noble form passed to Sayyidna Muhammad ibn Fu'ad, and Abu Bakr's luminous form (from his service to the Prophet) passed to his son Muhammad bin Abi Bakr.
One's hadd-e-'ali must be from the current Imam's hudud, never from the ranks of a previous Imam whose cycle (haikal) is over.

Promotion cannot be held back; a lower one (adna) cannot restrain his higher one, and if a hadd-e-'ali is promoted into the gathering assembly the lower one is simply assigned a replacement hadd-e-'ali.
In the daur-e-kashf returns occur every thousand years, but the people of the daur-e-qa'im (the final era, like us) return first and are not bound by the thousand-year rule.
A believer has only one hadd-e-'ali, but a hadd-e-'ali may have a whole congregation (majma') of believers.
The Prophet said that when a believer prays, two rows pray behind him — his unseen (ghair-mar'i) congregation of his hadd-e-'ali.
When a questioner asks a question he is often a medium through whom a form from his congregation, or his hadd-e-'ali, asks for its own satisfaction of knowledge.

The Quran's 'Innal-hasanati yudhhibnas-sayyi'at' means the believer's hasanat — his lower ranks (hudud-e-daniya), still engaged in tasbih and pursuit of knowledge — eliminate his evil deeds, namely the doubts and misgivings (shukuk wa shubhat) in his hadd-e-'ali.
Doubt is necessary for a believer because the plant of certainty (yaqin) always grows in the soil of doubt (shakk).

Ibrahim's request to see how the dead are revived ('li-yatma'inna qalbi') shows that certainty is above faith ('al-yaqinu fawqa al-iman'); his belief was iman, but the satisfaction of the heart he sought was yaqin.

A hadd-e-'ali is appointed only after one takes the 'ahd-e-sharif, which is the spiritual birth (wiladat-e-batini) as distinct from the physical birth (wiladat-e-zahiri); before it one cannot have a hadd-e-'ali or become a hadd (zimmah) for others, lacking the magnet to attract the iron.

The four mothers form in sequence by the spheres' diminishing motion: asir (ether, center of fire, invisible, its light concealed by divine wisdom), hawa (air, moderate), ma' (water, cold and flowing), and earth (extreme cold and dryness).
The Mudabbir willed the earth to be the place for the appearance of the mawalid (creations): mineral (ma'dan), vegetable (nabat), animal (hayawan), and human (the rational animal, hayawan-e-natiq).

The celestial rays struck the hard rock (sakhra), recoiled from its hardness, returned reflected and heated the earth's surface and air, producing nasim (the breeze, center of water) and zamharir (intense cold, the highest part of the nasim sphere).

The sun's opposite (sadaf/azdad), like all the celestial bodies', was formed from the rock mixture; the kawakib are noble in essence (made of the highest parts of the nadimin) but their azdad acquired inauspiciousness from the rock, which is the basis of planetary effects on people.
The markaz al-ma' (center of water) is not water itself; if one travels there, water is not present — it is only the center from which water is balanced.
The Quran's 'Wa-llahu anbatakum min al-ardi nabata' establishes two kinds of human creation: from the earth (more excellent and higher) and from spiritual parents (lower).

Resurrection is true ('innal-ba'tha haqqun') and is of two kinds: the believer's resurrection (raised in faith after dying in faith) and the Prophet's resurrection at the praised station (maqam mahmud), appearing from Quds, into which Salman al-Farsi entered first and then the Prophet.
A qutb is born at the beginning of every cycle; the qutb of this cycle was born in Sarandib, and the qutb of the very first cycle of the du'at was born in the Ka'ba — the place where 'Ali was born.
The Quran's 'wa anzalna al-hadid fihi ba'sun shadid' states iron was sent down from the sky, and reciting this verse on Tuesday has great virtue.

The two nodes (head and tail, ra's wa dhanab) lie beyond the moon's sphere, the tail more severe than the head; the evil concepts (tasawwur-e-qabih) of the opposites of the du'at, prophets, and nuqata' went to the head, and those of the Imams, hujjats, and awsiya went to the tail.
The Mudabbir ('Ashir al-Mudabbir) delegated the administration of the world to Zuhal (Saturn) by his own substance, and Zuhal administers for a thousand years.

From the intermingled natures arose vapors, dense clouds, and continuous non-beneficial rains (matar al-su', the evil rain mentioned in the Quran), which carry impurities down, whereas good rains bring down the purified luminous essences (fudulat-e-nayyirah) from the falak al-buruj.

The essence's purification journey runs from the first degree of the first zodiac to the last and back, 720 years total; the book being read (Sayyidna Mu'ayyad al-Shirazi's) supplies the Tahajjud du'a 'la tuksiranna ya Rabbi fi hadha al-safarana' (do not prolong our journey).

Spiritual progress moves from the physical world to the psychic world: the body becomes a nafs (namiya, hissiya, natiqa), reaches the station of the sura, then the station of the 'aql (intellect) on some distant day (yawman ma); once the form enters the Imam's haykal it is like a fixed deposit that progresses with the Imam.
The mizaj-e-muntazij of essences is ascending through vapors (bukharat) and descending through rainwater after purification.

Even unbelievers, infidels, and hypocrites return after 1000 years; after purification they reach the station of affirmations (ta'yidat) with a thousand-year lifespan, becoming in actuality the angels they were in potentiality.
Per Sayyidna 'Ali, of five times one is when prayers are accepted, namely 'inda nuzul al-ghayth (at the time of rainfall), because at that time the purified essences are descending and ascending.

When the people asked the Messenger to pray for rain and then for it to stop, he recited 'khuliqa al-insanu min 'ajal' (man was created of haste); a parallel rain miracle occurred in the time of Sayyidna Ghulam Husain at Gandipet, traced back through Sayyidna 'Ali bin Qutbuddin (author of Bahrat al-'Adillah) and Sayyidna Isma'il bin Hibatullah.

At his death Sayyidna Mu'ayyad al-Shirazi wept, saying 'mata yalhaku al-baytu ila rabbihi' (when will the house join its Lord) — the body (house) longing to join its noble form (Lord) — before his four student-du'at including Lamak bin Malik.

The principle 'al-mu'minu yanzuru bi-nurillah' (the believer sees with the light of God) was invoked by Sayyidna Ja'far regarding the 12-year-old Sayyidna Hasan Khan, foreseeing 'yakunu lahu sha'nun min sha'n' (he will have a great station); Hasan Khan later wrote 70 books in haqa'iq.

In Zuhal's first thousand years the earth became a surging sea ('Wa sarat al-ardu bahran muwwajan') and fermented essences (khama'ir) resembling Saturn's nature — iron, stone, copper, and the Sudanese, farmers (zarra'a), the wretched (ahl al-shaqa), and the harsh — were formed.

Mushtari (Jupiter) is the Sa'd-e-Akbar; Jupiter and Venus are the two auspicious planets (sa'dayn), and 'al-Mushtari bayna al-nahsayn' (Jupiter between the two inauspicious) is illustrated by the Prophet's grave lying between Abu Bakr and 'Umar.

The 14-rak'at prayer at the Prophet's Mosque is offered at the pillars (ras, maqam al-Tawbah, Hannanah, 'Ali, etc.), of which the eight rak'at at the pillars are most meritorious, alluding to the bearers of the Throne; the maqam al-Tawbah is the spot the Prophet said people would draw lots for if they knew its virtue.

The successive thousand-year planetary governances each fermented essences of matching nature: Mushtari (pious religious people, vegetation, crawling creatures), Mirrikh (commanders, soldiers, minerals), Shams (kings, ruby, gold), Zuhra (Arabs, women, singers, fruits, birds), and 'Utarid (scribes, ministers, accountants), preparing for the human's appearance in the seventh millennium.

The human person appeared in the seventh thousand years 'nabatan min al-ardi' (as a plant from the earth), per 'wa-Allahu anbatakum min al-ardi nabata'; dinosaurs and similar claims of science have no mention in this tradition and are fiction.

A hadd is a fixed limit or measurement, per the Quran's 'la ta'tadu hudud Allah... man yata'adda hudud Allahi faqad zalama nafsahu' (do not transgress Allah's limits; whoever does has wronged himself).

When a believer dies his namiya, hissiya, and natiqa souls instantly unite into the surah sharifah, which goes to its hadd-e-'ali — one superior to it in rank by only a nineteen-to-twenty difference, not a da'i or hujjat of the time.

The Tahiyyat al-Masjid's mamsulat (referents) include one's hadd-e-'ali and its hadd-e-'ali; as a gift to the mosque it requires reciting the descending surahs (Falaq then Nas), a practice otherwise reserved for obligatory prayers and the sunnah of fajr, giving it special status.
A living hadd-e-'ali does not stop the lower one's wrong deeds, but a knowledge-loving hadd-dani can incite his hadd-e-'ali toward the world of knowledge if the latter is disinclined to it.

The 'ahd-e-sharif is the greatest act of worship, surpassing obligatory prayers, Hajj, Zakat, and fasting; without it the surah sharif is never formed and no hadd-e-'ali can be appointed, so it is renewed yearly on Yawm al-Ghadir per 'wa-dhakkir fa-inna al-dhikra tanfa'u al-mu'minin'.

Through the 'ahd-e-sharif one receives a nuqta-e-nur (point of light) from one's own hadd in the spiritual world, from its inabat and tawbah, per the Quran's 'la tansa nasibaka min al-dunya' — meaning do not die without the 'ahd-e-sharif.

A minimal 'ahd-e-sharif can be completed in one's last moments by taking the name of the Imam of the time and sending blessings upon him; even loving and obeying the infallible Imam of the time (khalifat Allah fi al-ard) without a formal covenant is tremendously beneficial.

Children who die young (ahl-e-istighar) do not have a surah formed, but have a majma'-e-sighar that progresses; this assembly was first given to Bibi Fatimah al-Zahra then to Mawlana Baqir, and the children of the A'imma who die young form the majma'-e-mufritin, also under Bibi Fatimah's care.

The believer's journey after death proceeds from higher hudud to the Bab al-Abwab; when the haykal gathered there is complete, the Imam acquires it and hands it to his farzand, who thereby goes from Imam in potential to Imam in actuality.

The Imam hands the gathered majma' to his farzand in four days or four years; rarely Mawlana 'Abd al-Muttalib received the majma' before birth, so his mother said 'wulidtu shaybah' (I gave birth to an old man) because his hair was white.
The spiritual majma' of nasut and lahut runs completely parallel (mumathil) to the nasut: a rank attained in nasut corresponds exactly to the form's place in lahut, never higher or lower.

Animals that die their own death in the 6000 years died a halal death, like the pigeons of the Ka'ba and Madinah, which cannot be hunted yet die halal because they are formed from the fudlat of the mukasirin.

A mukasir is the da'wat teacher who breaks (kasr) his students' false beliefs and establishes correct belief through his hujjat; he carries the entire load of the da'wat from the Imam down to the lowest rank, like the feet bearing the body's weight.

As reward for their lifelong labor, jewels (jawahir), rubies (yawaqit), and salt form from the fudlat and bones of the mukasirin; the Prophet said 'al-milh qabl al-ta'am wa ba'd al-ta'am yaqta'u sab'ina da'an, awwaluha al-junun wa al-juzam' (salt before and after food wards off seventy diseases, the least being madness and leprosy).

The Quran's 'fas'alu ahl al-dhikr in kuntum la ta'lamun', per Imam Husayn, means the Ahl al-Bayt are the ahl al-dhikr; God divided the world into ahl al-dhikr and la ta'lamun, obliging the latter to ask, but not obliging the Ahl al-Bayt to answer.

In the seventh millennium the higher governor moved the sphere and vapors ascended from the dregs of minerals, plants, and animals, became clouds (ghuyum), and poured down as a pure rain ('amtaran safiyatan') that made shallow furrows (khudad) in the earth.

A second, nobler vapor rose from the furrows and poured down as rain 'shabihatun bi-maniy al-rajul' (like a man's semen) into the furrows 'shabihatun bi-arham al-nisa'' (like women's wombs), mixed with the woman-like water, and took form through the stages of creation over nine months by the Mudabbir's arrangement and the celestial bodies' influence.

After nine months the first human opened his eyes, inhaled the nasim, rolled in and absorbed the remaining oily water through his pores, was nourished first from his navel then sucked his thumb (from which his Creator caused pure milk to flow), explaining infants' thumb-sucking habit.
The first human spent nine months plus one full year in the pit, then stood up the size of a four-year-old child due to the greatness of his parents, who are the heaven and the earth.

The Imam has four things: his nasut, his lahut, his nafs, and his surah; in the obligatory four-rak'at prayer the higher first two rak'at allude to the Imam's nafs and surah sharif, the latter two to his nasut and lahut.

The Imam's nasut is made from the riya' of the believers and the hudud of the da'wat, and his lahut from their surat; both are borrowed, only the Imam's nafs and surah being his own, which is why celestial bodies and poison can affect his borrowed body.

The Imam's nafs-e-hissiyah is so exalted it bears all the nawasit, lawahiq, lahut, and nasut of the entire era; Amir al-Mu'minin 'Ali ibn Abi Talib's nafs-e-hissiyah carried the hayakil of all the A'imma from Hunays to Abu al-Qayyim.

The Imam is infallible, so 'Ali uprooting the gate of Khaybar 'la bi-quwwatin jismaniyyatin bal bi-quwwatin ruhaniyyah/rabbaniyyah' was an allusion to the strength granted by his muhtajib (veiled one), not physical strength.
The Imam, being infallible, fulfills our qisasat; any difficulty falls upon the riya' and the believers, not upon him, his original essence remaining far removed.
'Ali's words at the blow ('fuztu bi-Rabb al-Ka'bah') related to the qisasat; 'Ali was the bearer of the surat of 10,000 years (plus 3,000 years of fatrat).

The present Amir holds the jami'iyyat of 400,000 surat (seven daur-e-kashf and six daur-e-satr) in his seventh manifestation; he is the khalifah of the Qayyim, the Qayyim the khalifah of the 'Ashir, and while the Amir is the 'ayn-e-awwalah the Qayyim is the 'ayn-e-akhirah.

In each pit (khudad) males were created first and females afterward from the remaining water; multiple pits were created at Sarandib and across the 12 islands, including evil pits from which enemies and adversaries arose.
There is a city in Sarandib named Nur Eliya, said to be the manifestation (tajalli) of Mawlana 'Ali.
The Exalted Planner (al-mudabbir ta'ala) separated and distinguished the purest, noblest, most excellent, and most subtle part of the rainwater descending from the sky.
The purest portion of the rain was carried to the noblest of places (ashraf al-biqa'), which in the first epoch was Sarandib because it was the locus of earthly equilibrium (mawda' i'tidal al-ard).
Twenty-eight individuals were formed in the depressions (al-qudad) of Sarandib, who in honor, purity, and excellence surpassed all other humans, with the rank of the red ruby over ordinary stone.
Amir al-Mu'minin ('Ali) declared 'I am the red ruby' (anal-yaqut al-ahmar) and that the Messenger of Allah is the yellow ruby (al-yaqut al-asfar).

Among the twenty-eight, one individual (the jussa ibda'iyah) is superior to all in nobility and excellence, like the red ruby over a stone, and he is the essence (zubdah), choicest part (safwa), and extract (khulasa) of the world.
The one individual attained superiority over the other twenty-seven because of his purity of intention (safa' an-niyyah) and his great remorse (kathrat an-nadam) for his fault at the call of 'Ashir.
When the noble individual emerged from the depressions, he looked at his own essence by his own essence, without any teacher (mu'allim) or inspirer (mulhim), and contemplated the world.

Contemplating the constructed sky, the spread-out earth, and the varied creatures, the noble individual reasoned that he, his species, and the whole world have a single Creator (mubdi') who is different from them.
The noble individual negated divinity (ilahiyyah) from himself and all creatures and affirmed it for his Creator, bearing witness to Him.
The power to bring from non-existence (nist) into existence (hast) is not in any creature; this is a skill belonging only to the rank of the first intellect.
The noble individual stood in the lower world (al-'alam ad-dani) at the station of the First Precedent (maqam as-sabiq al-awwal), mirroring the station of 'aql al-awwal in the spiritual world.

Once his intellect became pure, his portion of substance (maddah) and support (ta'id) connected with him, establishing the principle that anyone with a pure intellect and clean thought necessarily receives divine support.

Even though the ibda'iyah were born knowing their own status, the Imams, like other creatures, must still acquire knowledge and study, as the Quran states they were brought forth from their mothers' wombs knowing nothing, while remaining infallible (ma'sum) from the beginning.
The jussa ibda'iyah gathered the twenty-seven individuals, from whom his physical form (haykal) was prepared, and from this the purification of the world (takhlis al-'alam) occurred.

The son of the jussa ibda'iyah was the first Imam; the imamat began with him and will continue in his lineage until the Day of Resurrection through every epoch (dawr al-kashf, dawr al-sitr, dawr al-fatrah).
The twenty-seven individuals are not ordinary; they are the essence (zubdah) and cream of creation, superior to those born naturally.

The jussa ibda'iyah received substance and support not directly but at the hands of the First Precedent (sabiq al-awwal) through the intermediary of all the creative intellects (al-'uqul al-ibda'iyah).

Through that substance the jussa ibda'iyah was ennobled and came to know what was and what will be (ma kana wa ma sayakun), as had been granted to 'aql al-awwal, muba'ath as-sabil, and the creative intellects.

The noble individual then called the twenty-seven who were with him to affirm Allah and His Oneness (wahdaniyyah), acknowledge His divinity, and negate divinity from themselves, and all of them responded with 'labbayk'.
Unlike the spiritual world where some denied 'Ashir, in the lower world all twenty-seven affirmed and brought faith, denying divinity for themselves and acknowledging Allah as Creator.
The Quranic verse 'shahidallahu annahu la ilaha illa huwa' is interpreted such that the name Allah is applied to 'aql al-awwal and 'huwa' (He) refers to the mubdi' ta'ala.

'Aql al-awwal could not name the mubdi' ta'ala and so gestured and said 'huwa' (He); Sayyidna al-Mu'ayyad said even saying 'huwa' is a sin accompanied by seeking forgiveness (dhambun mashfu'un bil-istighfar).

The angels (al-mala'ikah) who bore witness in the verse are the incorporeal intellects (al-'uqul al-mujarradah), the nine intellects from the second to the tenth, who hastened to the call made through muba'ath as-sabil.
'Aql al-awwal did not himself make a call; the call happened through muba'ath as-sabil, otherwise a circle of gathered intellects would have formed around 'aql al-awwal.
The people of knowledge (ulul-'ilm) in the verse are the noble individual (sahib jussa ibda'iyah) together with his twenty-seven hudud who respond to and bear witness to his call.
They are alluded to as 'people of knowledge' because they are the repository (mahill) of substances and supports, which is intellectual knowledge ('ilm al-'aqli) given to support them.
Among the twenty-seven, ranks are established according to each one's purity (safa) and response (ijabah); they are not of one rank but hold distinct ranks in repentance, gnosis, and testimony.
Just as the companions held different ranks, with the Imam the hujjatul layl and hujjatul nahar have different ranks, and the Imam chooses among them.
The hujjatul layl, who are always in the Imam's presence, are superior to the hujjatul nahar.
The bab al-zahir and bab al-batin are from among the twelve.
In the Imam's presence are the bab al-imbi'as; the bab al-batin is superior, and the bab al-imbi'as is even superior to the bab al-batin.

The verse 'shahidallahu annahu la ilaha illa huwa wal-mala'ikatu wa ulul-'ilmi qa'iman bil-qist, la ilaha illa huwa al-'aziz al-hakim' is a very special verse in which the kalimah shahadah appears twice.
The kalimah la ilaha illallah appears in the Quran in five intonations: la ilaha illallah, la ilaha illa huwa, la ilaha illa ana, la ilaha illalladhi, and la ilaha illa anta.

There are thirty-seven such kalimat of testimony in the Quran appearing across thirty-six verses, since one verse (shahidallah) contains it twice, giving that verse great importance and a tasbih of great power.
The Da'i 'Abd al-'Ali (al-Wazir) wrote that whoever recites these thirty-six verses has his prayer accepted immediately, as mentioned in Majmu' al-Ad'iyah.

A tradition of Qadi Shurayh states that whoever recites these verses will attain ten states; Qadi Shurayh lost his eyesight and regained it by reciting the kalimah shahadah intonations in order on the Prophet's instruction.
This entire verse is included in the kalimat at-tahlil (verses of tahlil) recited in the community's prayer.

The moon, the last intellect of the kawr, assisted Jupiter (Zuhal) in administration for a thousand years, which was a thousand years of felicity and the establishment of the Noble Mission (da'wah sharifah).
The da'wah sharif is not the name of a room or chamber but, in the spiritual world, the name of the intellects, and in the physical world, the name of the assembly formed by these hudud.

The noble individual (jussa ibda'iyah) separated the twenty-seven and sent them to the twelve islands (ithna 'ashar jazirah) of the earth to call people to the worship and obedience of Allah and to teach them.
Those called were the jussas born in the islands, of whom many were born in different places.
They taught the people the knowledge of worldly life ('ilm al-ma'ash) and the knowledge of the Hereafter ('ilm al-ma'ad).

The noble individual taught each da'i the language of the people to whom he was sent, since every island had its own language, fulfilling the verse 'We have not sent any messenger except in the language of his people'.
key_terms: wa ma arsalna min rasulin illa bi-lisani qawmihi

teaching: Without revelation (wahy) and connected support (ta'id), the noble individual could not have taught the properties, benefits, harms, beneficial medicines, and deadly poisons of minerals, plants, and animals from himself.

This teaching of properties verifies the Quranic statement 'And He taught Adam all the names' (wa 'allama Adama al-asma'a kullaha), because the noble individual is the First Adam (al-Adam al-awwal) and the Father of Humanity (Abu al-Bashar).
'Ashir is the spiritual Adam, while the jussa ibda'iyah is the First Adam of the physical world and the father (teacher) of his species in worldly and otherworldly matters.
Had Allah's grace not supported the noble individual, by which he was made deserving through his glorification (tasbih) and administration (tadbir) for his Lord, all the people would have perished.

The punishment of the accursed ones lasts for one kawr, but some are taken out earlier due to their just deserts (mujibat-i-'adliyah), emerging through volcanic lava and then returning in human form via the plants that grow.
Umar bin 'Abd al-'Aziz was taken out of punishment before his time as reward for stopping the cursing of 'Ali from seventy thousand pulpits and returning the garden of Fadak to the Ahl al-Bayt.
Souls return in human form even where only infidels eat the plants grown from volcanic lava; after repentance is accepted (tawba 'alayh) they gradually move into other cycles.
The human form is a common platform from which souls both fall and climb.

Each da'i in his island taught the people how to make clothes from trees, obtain food from minerals and animals, and the way of salvation through the worship and obedience of Allah and obedience to His chosen wali (the Imam of the time) on earth.

The noble individual established in his presence at Sarandib twelve individuals who are the Hujjatul Layl (Proofs of the Night), the most excellent, associated with the Night Prayer (Salat al-Layl), in which twelve rak'at are prayed at once.

The hujjatul layl are kept together in the Imam's presence, while the hujjatun nahar are stationed in separate islands, paired such that two hujjatun nahar of a da'i are tied to another da'i, one higher and one lower, reflected in praying two rak'at at a time.
The Tahajjud is for the hujjatun nahar, and the concluding du'a is for the Da'wat — a call to the twelve hujjatul layl to join Qa'im Al-i-Islam or the Imam of the time.
Among the twelve hujjatul layl, four are called the Khurum and are more excellent than the other eight; the twelve themselves are more excellent than the twenty-seven born with the jussa.
Among the four Khurum, one is superior and is the Bab (gate) of that noble station (the Imam or the jussa ibda'iyah himself).
The term station (maqam) applies to three persons: the Imam, the Wasi, and the Nabi.
The noble individual appointed before each da'i in his island three persons: a Mukasir, a Ma'dhun Mutlaq, and a Da'i Mahsur.
These ranks (Mukasir, Ma'dhun, Da'i) are preserved (mahfuzah) and are never cut off with any Natiq, Wasi, or Imam in his epoch.

Every da'i commanded the people of his island that each should marry a woman formed in a cavern other than his own, and not marry the woman who emerged from his own cavern from the remnant of his water, who is like his sister.

From one cavern, males were born first and then females from the remaining water, fulfilling 'Men are the protectors and maintainers of women' (ar-rijalu qawwamuna 'ala an-nisa'); these women were the sisters of those men and unlawful to marry.
This exogamous practice is the pure, unblemished way of the People of Truth (tariq ahl al-haqq).

The exoteric belief (held by the ignorant ahl az-zahir) that Adam married the children of his first wife's womb to those of the second womb is rejected, because it would make all human progeny born of incest/fornication (sifah).
The Du'at affirm the correct account against the ignorant, praising Allah with 'praise be to Allah who guided us to this, and we would not have been guided had Allah not guided us'.
The birth from the earth happened in a single event (daf'ah wahidah) in the first epoch and never recurred, mirroring how the mubdi' ta'ala brought all creations (mubda'at) into existence at once.
After the single earth-birth, all subsequent human births until today occur through procreation (tanasul) between man and woman.
Believing women who are very pure and worship purely for Allah are gradually made men in the coming cycles (karr) due to their worship; such risen women are very few (illa ma sha' Allah).
When a woman rises to a higher state, another is brought to the pit in her place, because women remain a necessity of the world and the ratio is preserved.
Sulayman bin Hasan said of his wife Khadijah bint Nuh, 'kanat hiya dhukur' (she was male), meaning she outwardly wore a woman's dress but was inwardly a man.
Knowledge and proof come in two types: naqli (transmitted evidence found in lectures, books, and physical things) and aqli (rational evidence weighed on the scales of the intellect).
The doctrine of zahir-batin (exoteric-esoteric) is unique to the Ismaili tradition and is not possessed by Hinduism, Christianity, or Judaism.
In the present age it is more necessary to strengthen the conviction of one's own community than to bring outsiders into the faith.

We consider 'Isa, Musa, Ibrahim and all earlier prophets to be true prophets great for their respective times, whereas the followers of those faiths do not accept our Prophet as a prophet, which is the biggest difference between us.
Allah's revealed books are the Tawrat, the Zabur, the Injil, and then the Quran, with the Quran being the final one.
The Bible is a corrupted, late version of the Injil with conflicting recensions (Matthew, Barnabas, John), and the Tawrat and Zabur are likewise unreliable; none preserves the original text.
Not a single letter or even a diacritical mark (zabr, zayr) of the Quran can be changed until Qiyamah, and any such variation is rejected.
The Quran's incorruptibility is guaranteed by Allah's words 'Inna nahnu nazzalnahu wa inna lahu lahafizun' (Indeed We sent down the Reminder and We are its guardian).
Reformers who claimed certain Quranic rulings (e.g. on pardah) no longer apply in the modern age are wrong; the shari'ah remains in force until Qiyamah.
The Quranic phrases 'Asatir al-awwalin' and 'Zubur al-awwalin' refer to ancient scriptures, including the Hindu scriptures (Bhagavad Gita, Upanishads, Rigved, Atharvaved).
Zubur al-awwalin denotes the eras of Nuh and Hud, when Hinduism was the prevalent tradition.
Adam's era is roughly 6,900-7,000 years ago, and Nuh's era begins about 1,000 years after Adam.
Nuh's reported lifespan of 900 years refers to the duration of his period/era, not his personal age, which was about 120 years.
Across the 7,000-year period, seven great Natiq prophets are born: Adam, Nuh, Ibrahim, Musa, 'Isa, and Rasulullah (six so far), and the seventh, who establishes Qiyamah.
A great prophet is normally born approximately every 1,000 years, though sometimes after 1,500 or 2,000 years.
'Isa's era lasted only 600 years, so the Prophet Muhammad came after 600 rather than the usual 1,000 years.
Everything that exists is recorded in the Quran, per 'wala ratbin wala yabisin illa fi kitabin mubin' (no moist or dry thing but is in a clear Book); one need only extract it.
By the principle 'li-kulli qawmin had' (for every people there is a guide), every nation received a prophet, so figures such as Krishna and Ram were the guides of Hinduism's ancient era.
Meat slaughtered by the hand of the Jews (People of the Book) is permissible for us to eat.
The religion (din) began with Adam, the first prophet, and has continued unbroken to the present.
Human beings existed before Adam, as shown by fossils found in Java, Sumatra, and Heidelberg through anthropology, dating back hundreds of thousands of years.
'Adam' is not a personal name but a title (mansab) for the one who begins a period, and 'Qayem/Qa'im' is the title for the one who ends it; the two have a special relationship.
When asked who came before Adam, Hadrat 'Ali repeatedly answered 'Adam,' teaching that countless Adams have passed and countless will come.
Din (the one system of Allah) never changes, but shari'ah (the rules of prayer, fasting, zakat, etc.) changes from one prophet's era to another.
The salawat 'Allahumma salli 'ala Muhammad... kama sallayta 'ala Ibrahim' shows that the same din existed in Ibrahim's time.
The names of Adam's father, grandfather, tribe, marketplace, district and province, as well as the name of Shaitan of that era, are all recorded in the complete books.
The seventh and final great prophet, yet to come, is the greatest, being simultaneously the Imam, the Nabi, and the Qa'im who brings the Resurrection.
The Imam is interpreted as the sun (aftab) and the Da'i as the moon.
Every Nabi is paired with a Wasi (successor): Musa with Harun, 'Isa with Yusha', and the Prophet with 'Ali.
After the Nabi and Wasi pass away, Imamat takes over the task of spreading the deen, and every Imam is the controller of his time.
The Da'i cannot give knowledge until he receives it from the Imam above; the real control over the shari'at-e-Muhammadi rests with the Imam.
As the moon has no light of its own but takes it from the sun, the Da'i takes knowledge from the Imam, while the Imam has his own light and takes from no one.
The method of da'wah descends in rank from Imam to Da'i to Ma'dhun to Mukasir to Hudud and finally to the believers (mu'minin).
Knowledge ('ilm) always descends from above to below, like water that Allah sends down from the heavens to the earth ('Nahnu nazzalna al-maa'), never the reverse.
Water is the standing metaphor for 'ilm (knowledge): wherever water is mentioned, its batin (inner reality) is knowledge.
Zahir is the apparent, visible thing (like the body or a seed) and batin is the hidden inner reality (like the soul or what is inside the belly).
Democracy and election are rejected; rank is conferred from above, the one higher lifting the one below, as illustrated by the lifting of the rosary bead in tasbih.
The Prophet's knowledge is like the vast salty ocean, available to all mankind, for he came 'kaffatan lil-nas' (for all people) and as 'Rahmatan lil 'Alamin' (a mercy to the worlds).
The ocean's salty water represents 'ilm-e-zahir (exoteric knowledge such as biology, science, philosophy and logic), which must be separated out to obtain sweet (esoteric) water.
The Prophet wrote no book except Hadith, which are short, plain narrated sentences; the formal aqa'id were derived from them later.
The Prophet said 'I am the city of knowledge and Ali is its gate,' so all knowledge sprouted from Ali.
Tanzil (revelation) descended the Quran upon the Prophet's heart, while ta'wil (interpretation) is the task of Ali; the Prophet did not perform tafsir of the Quran.
Since Ali is no longer present, the Imam of every age stands in his place as his descendant; the Imam being in ghaybat (occultation), one asks the Da'i.
Knowledge reaches the believer filtered down through the ranks rather than directly from the original source.

In the village-well analogy of Mabda' wa Ma'ad, the pure Imam holds the rank of the great bucket (dol) into which water (knowledge) is drawn, then poured into successively smaller vessels representing the Hujjat, Da'i and lesser ranks.
The two hands used in wudu and ghusl symbolize the Mukasir and the Ma'dhun: the Ma'dhun (the sanctioned one) is the right hand, and the Mukasir is the left hand and the lower rank.
Mukasir means one who can refute or break an opponent's argument; the Ma'dhun is greater than him and grants permission to speak.
The Mir Alam Talab episode of Hazrat Abdullah Sahab teaches that one must drink water (receive knowledge) through one's own channel of dawat, not directly from the dawat-e-zaahir.

Blood is the metaphor for doubt (shakk); just as prayer is invalid while blood flows until wudu is performed, one must pray in a state of certainty (yaqeen), for nothing is permissible in a state of doubt.
A total of 124,000 prophets have passed in the world.
The ranks Nabi, Rasul, Natiq, Ulul 'Azm messenger, A'immah, and Awsiya' are all distinct categories that must not be conflated.
Nabi means one who gives news (from naba' = news) and is the lowest of the high ranks.
The roughly 26-27 prophets named in the Quran (27 if Luqman is counted a prophet) are the greatest among the 124,000, since inclusion in the Quran is itself a supreme honor.
Among the 27 named prophets, seven bear a message (paigham) from Adam to the Qa'im, of whom six Natiq have already come.
A Rasul ranks higher than a Nabi; not every Nabi is a Rasul, and a prophet is first a Nabi before becoming a Rasul.
Natiq means one who speaks; six Natiq have passed (Adam, Nuh, Ibrahim, Musa, 'Isa, Muhammad), and in Adam's time all others were samit (mute), lacking the intellect Allah gave Adam.
The Ulul 'Azm (possessors of firm resolve) are five: Nuh, Ibrahim, Musa, 'Isa and Muhammad, Adam being excluded because the era of Ulul 'Azmiyyat had not yet begun.
The five Ulul 'Azm prophets are the esoteric basis (mansul) of the five daily prayers (Fajr, Zuhr-Asr, Maghrib-Isha), supplying what makes namaz into namaz.
The two greatest prophets of all are Ibrahim, the Khalilullah (Friend of Allah), and Muhammad, the Habibullah (Beloved of Allah), with Muhammad standing one degree above Ibrahim.
The prophetic hierarchy narrows from 124,000 to 27, to six or seven, to five, to two, to the single greatest, the Prophet Muhammad.
Sayyidna Sulayman is the concluder of the Muhammadi dawr (mukhtatim-i dawr-i Muhammadi), at which point the qaimi dawr begins.
We belong to the Muhammadi ummah and follow the shari'at-i Muhammadi, but we live not in the Muhammadi dawr but in the higher, permanent era that follows it.

About 400 years have passed in this permanent era since the time of Imam Du'al, and this 400-year excess over the standard 1,000-year prophetic period is compensation for the fact that 'Isa's era was only 600 years long.
The Prophet said 'ulama ummati ka-anbiya'i Bani Isra'il' (the scholars of my community are like the prophets of the Children of Israel), equal to them in rank.
After the Prophet, with no more prophets or wasis and the Imam concealed, the du'at who pass through history are the 'ulama who stand equal to the prophets of Bani Isra'il.

Da'i means 'one who calls toward Allah'; the master of one jazeera, two jazeeras, or three jazeeras holds graded rank, the master of three jazeeras being the Da'i, while 'amils and mullas who call people are of lower rank without certain authority (ijazah).
The Quranic verse 'fa-faddalna ba'dahum 'ala ba'd' (We preferred some of them over others) shows that no one stands at a single equal rank; excellence (fazilat) is graded everywhere.
The world existed before Adam; the 7,000-year span is one specified period within which seven great Natiq prophets appear.
Allah's order alternates calamity and relief so that no community weeps forever; the era before this 7,000 years was a very good era.
History runs through two alternating periods: kashf (manifestation/openness) and satr (concealment/veiling).
When the Imam (the sun) is manifest it is kashf, likened to day; when he is concealed it is satr, likened to night, during which the Da'i (the moon) gives light.
Kashf always comes first and satr follows, just as day precedes night.
Seven cycles of kashf and satr (day and night) form one 'week,' from which months, years and centuries are built up by the same mathematical pattern.
The kashf period lasts 50,000 years while the satr period of the current cycle is 7,000 years.
Adding kashf (50,000) and satr (7,000) gives 57,000 years; multiplied through the seven-fold cycle this yields about 399,000-400,000 years, which constitutes one dawr.
A dawr multiplied by a dawr (about 4 lakh x 4 lakh) yields roughly 16,000 crore years, which is called a kawr (qaur).
A kawr multiplied by a kawr produces a number requiring 25 zeros, called a mor (mawr), the largest duration in existence.
The ascending hierarchy of time units is: dass/day, dawr (week-equivalent), tawr, kawr/qaur, and mawr/mor.
The soul (ruh) is the real power and 'generator' that makes a person act; the body (jism) does nothing of itself, so the ruh is superior (bartar) and the jism inferior (kamtar).
Just as a person has a physical realm there is a jismani 'alam (physical world) and a ruhani 'alam (spiritual world), and the ruhani 'alam is the most superior and was created first.

The single question whose answer cannot be written or told is why Allah, the mudabbir-e-ka'inat, created the ruhani 'alam at all; one must 'believe and then go forward' as a child accepts alif before be.
Duniya (this world) and ka'inat (universe) differ: the ka'inat is the whole universe and contains the ruhani 'alam and the other realms ('awalim).
The realms descend in order: 'alam al-'aql (intellect), 'alam al-khalq (creation), 'alam al-jismani (body), and then this world in which we exist.
The opening 'Alhamdulillah Rabbil 'Alamin' uses the plural ''alamin' to prove that there are many worlds (spiritual, bodily, physical), the spiritual created before the physical.
The skies are arranged in layers (tibaqan), plate upon plate; the visible sky where sight stops is the sama' al-dunya (heaven of the world), with further skies above it.
The creator of the spiritual realm is named Mubdi' (not Mubda'), the one whom people call Allah, who brought things from non-being into being.
A khaliq (artisan/creator) only reshapes existing material, but the Mubdi' brought existence out of nothingness by the command 'Kun fa-yakun' (Be, and it is).
In the ruhani 'alam Allah created innumerable individuals in a single stroke (dafat'an wahidah) as ashbah, luminous human-form figures (nurani paikar) without substance or blood.
Humans were created in the qamat-e alifiyyah (stature of an alif), because the alif came first before the ba, marking humans as distinct from animals.
The countless hosts (junud) created in the spiritual realm number only known to Allah.
All were created simultaneously in one stroke so that Allah's justice ('adl) is established; had some been created earlier and others later, His justice would not hold.
Each individual was given three things equally: 'ilm (knowledge), hayat (life), and qudrat (power/authority, ikhtiyar).
The knowledge given there was complete, the 'ilm ma kana wa sa yakun (knowledge of what was and what will be), together with qudrat-e-tammah (complete power).
The life given was the most excellent state (afdal); Hazrat Zain Saab illustrated it by the wedding day being every person's most excellent, memorable day.
Allah, having given everything, willed that the created beings recognize Him (ma'rifah), and it was from this demand for ma'rifah that the test and troubles began.
Although all were created equal with the same gifts, there is an inherent mental difference between them, as in a class where only one student comes first.
One individual reasoned that neither could the others create him nor he them, so his creator must be someone else; this recognition is Tawhid (belief in Allah's oneness).
When that individual reasoned correctly, the nur (light) within him began to increase visibly, which the others observed.
Only two beings perceived the increasing light, which is why the rank of 'two' arose; Arabic uniquely has a dual (tathniyah) between the singular and the plural, the plural beginning at three.
Of the two who rose, one looked at the cause (illat, the batin) and one at the effect (ma'lul, the zahir).

'Aql-e-Awwal (the First Intellect) was the first being Allah created, the first of the entire universe; the word 'aql means tying or binding, signifying limitation, as a tethered she-camel can graze only within its rope.
The two rising beings are called Mabda'-e Awwal (First Originator) and Mabda'-e Thani (Second Originator), mabda' meaning those who rise.
The one who perceived the inner cause became the assistant and took the second position, while the one fixed on the external appearance remained stagnant and was left behind.
Seven Intellects ('aqls) came into being one after another, each with a large group, all professing Tawhid that Allah neither created them nor they Him but a separate Creator made them.
The First and Second Intellects plus the further seven make nine 'aqls in all.
The being who stayed fixed on appearances and on his own 'I' realized too late that the others had advanced, and his chance was gone, like one who loses his cinema seat by leaving for tea.
The fundamental error of the being left behind was the delusion of equality (masawat), thinking himself equal to the one who had risen.
The remedy for his error was to seek forgiveness and feel remorse (nadamat/repentance), and his plea ascended through the chain of connections (itisalaat) to the top.
Upon being forgiven (taba wa anaba, he repented and turned back) he became the tenth ('Ashir; 'ashara = ten); these ten describe the 'alam-i asl (world of origin).

Of his large following, one group repented along with him (tabu bi-tawbatihim), another accepted on hearing his call (labbaw al-nida'), and the rest refused, saying 'la nasma' wa la nuti'' (we will neither listen nor obey).
Allah, the ruh-i mudabbir-i wahid who created the spiritual world once and then governs through delegation, appoints a chain of subordinates (like a general manager, manager, and section in-charges).
Because the Tenth Intellect ('Ashir) caused the others to err, Allah charged him with the duty of reforming them.
Those who persistently refused were cast down (qubut) from the spiritual realm, and as they fell some repented.

Three groups resulted from the fall: immediate repenters placed in the realm of fixed stars (kawakib), the stubborn musirr and mustakbir thrown below the earth into minerals and ores, and the doubters placed in the four spheres of fire, water, air and soil.
The flickering of fire, the cyclones of air, the roaring of water and the unsettled dust of soil are all signs of the doubt of those placed in the four spheres.
The Tenth Intellect (aql al-'ashir), remaining high above, is the complete mudabbir al-'alam (governor of the world) and appoints in-charges over the great departments below.
The four generative realms of creation are ma'dan (mineral), nabat (vegetable), haywan (animal), and insan (human).
The mill of creation runs as plants draw from minerals, animals eat plants, and humans eat animals, each body growing from the one below.
What moves from above to below is called haram (forbidden), and what moves from below to above is halal (permissible).
The seven planets, from Saturn down to the Moon, were appointed as in-charges over the world.

Saturn (Zuhal), whose nature is to freeze, was given the first 1,000 years and spread ice over the entire world; Jupiter (a good star) then melted it, Mars spread mist, and the Sun cleared it, Saturn remaining king through 7,000 years.
Each planet in turn ruled its own 7,000-year cycle, so that after about 49,000 years the world was fully cultivated and plants were born, but the human being had not yet been created.
The human being is the real purpose of the universe (maqsad-e-kainat), affirmed by 'Lawlaka lama khalaqtu l-aflak' (Were it not for you, O Prophet, I would not have created the celestial spheres).
The human is a branch of the animals (haywanat) but higher: a plant has the power of growth (quwwat-e-numu) but cannot walk, an animal moves but cannot speak, and the human speaks.
Since there was no mother or father, the first humans were drawn from the extract of the best, praiseworthy animals (haywanat-e-mahmudah) at their natural death (taba'i maut).
Womb-like craters or pits formed at specific places in the earth, the best of them at the Ka'batullah in Makkah, then Madinah, then Baitul Muqaddas (Jerusalem).
Rising and condensing vapors formed an oily, sticky semen-like substance which, mixing with the earth's water (the woman's substance) and clay, produced a human when both waters mixed.
Twenty-eight pits formed in the Makkah area, each producing one human from the man's nutfah combined with the woman's substance and clay.

The first human stood in his pit for up to a year (or ten years), sucking his thumb against hunger as children naturally do, then emerged to eat ready-made paradise-like fruits such as grapes and pomegranates.
The first strong water produced 28 men; the remaining weaker water then produced 28 women, one male and one female from each pit being like siblings who could not marry each other.
Men and women from different pits intermarried (an interchange), and in this way the human race spread across the world.
The tallest of the first men, the very first man of this world's creation, is called Shakl al-Kull, and those who lived with him were people of high caliber.

Twenty-eight is the best digit: with every Imam there should be the Imam plus 27 dignitaries (12 Da'is with the Imam and 12 in the world make 24, plus Ma'dhun, Da'i and Bab al-Abwab make 27, and the Imam himself completes 28).
The 24 rak'at of Laylat al-Qadr correspond to the 24 Da'is (12 with the Imam and 12 in the world), and the 12 rak'at each of Salat al-Layl and Tahajjud correspond to the two sets of twelve.

The pattern of 28 should always be in effect with every Imam, grounded in the fact that the first human creation produced 28 at Makkah, then at Jerusalem, Madinah, Jabal al-Rahmah and Jannat al-Baqi'.
The Quran refers to a kind of human creation like a plant ('We made you grow like a nabat'), a creation that does not happen always but occurs at the start of a Kaur.
When 16,000 crore years (a kawr) are completed, the whole world ends and creation again occurs the plant-like way, called the creation of a Kaur, from which the next Kaur begins.

Mawlana Zainul Abidin told a woman named Umm-i Nida that one mawr has passed and of the second mawr 399 tawrs have passed with about 4 lakh remaining; he would tell what had passed but not what remained.

In the current state, the 400th tawr's first dawr has begun, of whose seven days/nights about seven have passed and the seventh night is ongoing, having started when Adam's tenth 'alam ended 7,000 years ago.
The seventh night will end only when the Qa'im comes, at which point the dawr itself changes, the tawr completes, and the kashf of the second dawr occurs.
After the Qa'im comes, a completely peaceful, clear era of 50,000 years of comfort and relief begins, free of all present disturbances.
After the 50,000 peaceful years, the era of trial returns because mutual wrongs must be requited, for Allah's justice ('adl) is certainly established and no one can escape.
We came into the world to repay our accounts by retribution, per 'al-uzunu bil-uzuni wal-nafsa bil-nafsi wal-'ayna bil-'ayni' (ear for ear, soul for soul, eye for eye); no qisas can be escaped.
The correct religion is the din of mabda wa ma'ad, where mabda means the beginning and ma'ad means the end/return.

Only one who takes the 'ahd (covenant) on the hand of the Imam al-Zaman, a mustajib or mu'min, is right and perfect; all others (Christian, Hindu, Jew) are upon untruth in our view and will be punished.
Giving guidance (hidayat) is the work of Allah alone; the believer can only explain and cannot change anyone's heart (qalb).
Ayat al-Kursi's phrase 'min al-zulumati ila al-nur' describes coming from darkness into light, or conversely leaving light for darkness.
After clinical death the believer is first questioned about namaz, and if namaz is sound then about zakat, roza and hajj.
Ma'ad is the final outcome; the believer's portion of it is the certainty of ascent, in which both the body (jism) and the soul (ruh) must progress.
A human has not one soul but three nufus (souls): the nafs-e-namiyah, the nafs-e-hissiyah, and the nafs-e-natiqah.
Sulala is the gist or extract that comes from the father (the semen).
The nutfa is confirmed when the father's fluid transfers to the mother and mixes with hers, the father's being dominant.
The embryo passes through seven stages: nutfa, 'alaqa, mudgha, 'izam, lahm, and khalq-i-akhar.

Each month of pregnancy is governed by a planet: the first by Saturn (which freezes and confirms the nutfa), the fourth by the Sun (when movement begins), the fifth by Venus (the skeleton), the sixth by Mercury (skin and flesh), and the seventh by the Moon (when it is perfected and can live).
The eighth month is dangerous because it returns to Saturn, which may freeze and kill the child, while the ninth month belongs to Jupiter, the best star, when the child is born.
Of the many life-germs that rise, only one is useful and the rest fall away, and that one which gets stuck is the 'alaqa (that which hangs), in agreement with science.
The seven embryonic stages correspond to seven prophets: Adam, Nuh, Ibrahim (the 'alaqa), Musa (the skeleton/fifth), 'Isa, and Muhammad.

The world's shari'ah, begun with Adam, was completed as a skeleton by 'Isa's time, and the Prophet's Muhammadi shari'ah clothed it with flesh, per 'fa kasawna l-'izama lahma' (We clothed the bones with flesh).
Janab-e-Hadd blows the spirit (ruh) into the prepared child so that it may live and emerge.
The first and lowest soul is the nafs-e-namiyah (vegetative/growth soul), the power of growth that enlarges the child in the womb.
The second soul is the nafs-e-hissiyah (sensitive/animal soul), seen in the newborn's activities of crying, laughing and moving its hands.
The third and highest soul is the nafs-e-natiqah (rational soul), received around age 13-14 when 'aql arrives, through the taking of the 'ahd, marking the spiritual birth.
The sign of adulthood in the shari'ah is becoming 'aqil (rational) and able to produce semen (mani), i.e. able to produce a human like oneself; at that point a hadd should be given to him.

The three births have three separate ends: the body goes to the grave, the nafs-e-namiyah becomes rij'iah, and the nafs-e-hissiyah together with the natiqah goes to barzakh to gather with one's elder.
An individual progresses not alone but by joining an elder, attaching to the one ranked just above him in the jama'at while the one just below attaches to him.
The elders of the jazirah are called malik (master) because our possession (milkiyat) rests with them, and the chain reaches up to the muqaddasin and then to the Imam.
Those without the covenant ('ahd) are ghair-e-haqq whatever their religion; though some hold a better creed than others, all are wrong in our view and will receive punishment accordingly.
Both a da'wat-e-haqq (call to truth) and a da'wat-e-zalal (call to error, e.g. that of the Dawoodis) run in the world, the latter misguiding people.
After death we are 'transferred' (muntaqil) to one higher than us, but the corrupt one is gradually taken down, stripped of human, then animal, then vegetable, then mineral faculties.
There are seven descending levels (darkat) of punishment: humanity, then bears/monkeys, then beasts, then reptiles, then birds, then vegetation, and finally minerals.
Each of the seven darkat contains 70 qamis (forms/shapes), each form being a different created shape.
After reaching the seventh level, if punishment remains, comes the intermediate punishment of the North and South Poles, regions of cold where penguins, sea horses and whales abide in torment.
The polar punishment lasts 5,000 to 20,000 years, after which, if the term still remains, comes the final third-degree punishment of stone.
The Qa'im will come to settle the account; before him comes Mehdi, and Mehdi and Qa'im are paternal cousins just as the Prophet and 'Ali were.
Mehdi is in the ascending line of the Prophet, and Qa'im is in the line of Janab-e 'Ali.
Qa'im will emerge from an area in Yemen and go to Madinah, where he performs ziyarat at the Prophet's grave (his ancestors), then proceed to Makkah.
At Madinah the Qa'im will order the Prophet's grave opened, and Abu Bakr and 'Umar, buried beside him as the two apparent corruptions of Islam, will emerge alive and be crucified on erected gallows.
Just as the auspicious Jupiter is flanked by Saturn and Mars, the Prophet is flanked in his grave by two who are like Mars and Saturn (Abu Bakr and 'Umar).
The Qa'im will come accompanied by 313 men, himself being the 314th, and will proceed from Makkah to the plain of Mina, four kilometers away.

At Mina (the place of slaughter, with the Bab al-Ghanam and Bab al-Baqar) the great offenders such as Fir'awn, Namrud, Qabil, Yazid and the killer of 'Ali will be slaughtered by the Qa'im himself like camels, while the great du'at and prophets slaughter the rest like goats.
This slaughter is a third-degree punishment; those who committed only minor mistakes are spared and then offered the da'wah, accepting or not.

Corrupt people possess only one soul, the Ruh al-Khabitha (vile spirit), whose invisible form (Surat al-Khabitha) is locked at Ras and Dhanab, the two invisible nodes near the moon known as Rahu and Ketu, shaped like a snake's head and tail.
When the corpses are gathered, the Surat al-Khabitha is commanded down to burn its own bodies, and as Allah commands rain to fall, the stench of the corpses becomes the ultimate punishment.
The winds carry the debris down to Jahannam/patal below the earth, the third-degree 'azab-i akbar (greatest punishment) that the du'at decline even to describe.

Below the earth the punished become deformed beings (with four hands and ten heads) who strike and fall endlessly, 'la yamutu wa la yahya' (neither dying nor living), for one parardha year of 16,000 crore years.
The believers watch the judgment unfold as if on TV, and the believer's own body, having obediently prayed and given zakat, also earns its reward.
Each part of a person, the spirit, the body, and the rational soul, has its own separate paradise, which is why jannat is spoken of in the plural.

Knowledge ('ilm) and action ('amal) are the two wings of flight; learning without acting, or acting without understanding, yields no benefit; Hazrat Sadiq Sahab prayed for strength in the wings to reach the nasheman (nest).
Per 'ya ma'shar al-jinn wal-ins... an tanfudhu min aqtari 's-samawati wal-ardh... illa bi-sultan', one cannot pass beyond the heavens and earth except with a sultan, namely the Imam.

The Qa'im of each level differs (the Qa'im of the Sidrah, the 'Arsh, the Kursi, the Lauh, the Qalam); progress within a level is merely relative, but true paradise is passing from here to the sky, achieved only by the master of mawr who pierces the heavens with the whole essence (qalb).
The batin of the sky (asman) is that, just as there are seven skies, there are seven Natiqs (Adam, Nuh, Ibrahim, Musa, 'Isa and the rest).
Allah makes rain fall upon His earth, meaning upon Janab-e-Wasi; as Harun received from Musa, 'Ali receives from the Prophet and all of us receive from 'Ali.
The earth signifies the existence of every imperfect thing and is the example of Hazrat 'Ali.
Per 'Kullu shay'in yarji'u ila aslihi' (everything returns to its origin), every thing falls toward the earth unless forcibly stopped, and likewise everything must ultimately return.
Just as the earth has a gravity pulling everything to it, 'Ali has a special force pulling everyone toward him, so the whole world must ultimately come to 'Ali.

Zain al-'Abidin explained 'yaliju al-jamalu fi sammi al-khayati' (a camel passing through the eye of a needle): the world is the camel's bulk and the needle's eye is our Ahl-e-Shari'at, through which every person must in time pass.
On the Day of Qiyamat the judgment at Mina takes place at the time of Hajj, and those brought there are not only Muslims but whoever is to receive punishment.

Imam is superior and Nabi is of lesser rank; the chain of Imamah (mustaqarr/mustaqirr) is never broken and requires a son, while a Nabi or Da'i is a mustawda' (caretaker) whose son does not inherit the rank.
Musa's Imam (the Qudd of Musa, alif-dal) was greater than Musa, and all that Musa did before Fir'awn's court was carried out from the Imam's side.
The Imams are hidden because it is the time of night (satr); the chain of night and day is the chain of kashf and satr.

In the 50,000-year kashf, corruption begins after 47,000 years, leaving a special 3,000-year decline in which people's creed changes and they turn from the Imam to amils, astrologers and ta'weez-makers.
Just as evening (with both light and darkness) precedes night, a transitional period precedes the 7,000-year satr; the ascending durations are dawr, then tawr, then mawt/mawr.

Whatever is known comes from a small starter, like the khamir (leaven) added to milk to make yogurt; here it is the khamir of nadamat (regret), connected with the needy one (muhtaj) and named qadim (ancient/eternal).

Beyond the three nufus there are higher souls such as the nafs-i-ilahiyyah (divine soul) and nafs-i-qudsiyyah (holy soul) belonging to the Imams and the buzurgan-i-din, which do not concern ordinary believers.
Nasut is the visible bodily state or form (paikar) and Lahut is the invisible; thus the Imam (Nasut) is visible while Imamat (connected to the suwar/forms) is not.
The Rij'iyyah is the nafs-i-namiyyah remnant (baqaya-i-namiyyah) that remains connected to the buried body and, after about three days, departs and becomes the Nasut.
Because all are sinners with some flaws, the nafs-i-namiyyah does not wholly perish at death; the body's connection with it remains in the grave to be purified by the higher soul pulling the lower.
The nafs-i-natiqah, received at the 'ahd and containing belief in the madhhab and the Imam-i-zaman, is the believer's guardian (sayiban) that saves him and influences the hissiyah to perform deeds.
At death the nafs-i-natiqah, being from the 'alam-i-amr, draws the hissiyah upward to become like itself, the proportion drawn depending on how one has lived and prayed.
Those with bad habits or illnesses leave more of the hissiyah behind in the grave, and the lower namiyyah remains there.
The torment of the grave ('adhab-i-qabr) is the suffering of the remaining baqaya-i-namiyyah at being buried, and for believers it lasts only three days as a great mercy from Allah.
The namaz of Wahshat al-Qubur and the talqin given to the deceased serve to help the namiyyah remnant depart from the grave.
A janaza should be lifted from the feet and one should not walk in front of it, because the Rij'iyyah is present; for the great ones (buzurgan) the remnant departs before reaching the grave.
The Imam is a luminous creation (nuri makhluq) with no body of his own; to come into the world as our guide (hadi) he requires a body.
The original veiled one (asl muhtajib) sends its hijab, a reflection and shadow (partaw, sayah), into the world, and this hijab is given a body formed from the nufus of all the believers.
Our nafs and the Imam's body are of the same substance (jawhar); the believers' Rij'iyyat and nufus become the Imam's body, so 'Kasayifuna lata'ifuhum' (our crude things are their subtle things).

There are three Nasut: the Nasut-i-taba'i (the lowest, formed from the believers of the jaza'ir), the Nasut-i-dhilli (shadow, formed from higher ranks and the believers of the hadarat), and the Nasut-i-khass (the very high, formed from the afadil of the hadarat).
The believers born in the hadarat (with the Imam) are free of corruption (fisad), while believers in the world are subject to fisad such as illnesses, colds and injuries.
Fisad is universal in this world, afflicting even da'is and all hudud-i-din except the Imam; those born free of fisad are born in the hadarat.
The Nasut-i-dhilli is controlled by every Imam's mother, since the wife of one Imam is the mother of the next.
The Nasut-i-khass is so high that, as Sayyidna Hasan 'Ali said, its test (imtihan) does not even occur in the world and it can scarcely be perceived.
Sayyidna 'Ali's Nasut-i-taba'i was higher than the Nasut-i-khass of other Imams, so high it could not be seen by ordinary eyes.
The Imam has the power to assume one thousand hijabs (veils/degrees) to descend to the eye level of the beholder; 'Ali prayed the Fajr namaz simultaneously in several cities to display his stations.
Prophets and 'Ali have three main hijabs, the first being the Hijab-e-Tanasul (the veil of procreation, lived through wives and children).
What was seen of 'Ali in Kufa was the Hijab-e-Hijab-e-Tanasul, a thrice-lowered veil, not the taba'i, dhilli or khass form, since he had to lower himself this far for people to receive guidance.
Sayyidna 'Ali ibn Dhiyab's book of hijabs details where the hijabs are, when they came into the world, and the nature and work of the muhtajib (the veiled one who is one's origin/asl).

The muhtajib is one's origin: here he came as 'Ali Murtada, but there he is the 'Ayn-i-'Adhimah, the 'ayn (from 'Ali) and the mim (the Prophet's name), 'Ali Murtada being the reflection (partaw) that descended.
The Prophet's names (Muddaththir, Muzzammil, Taha, Yasin) and 'Ali's titles (Abu Turab, Mustafa, Abul-Hasan) are all hijabs, as Sayyidna Ja'far used to say.
There is also a Nasut-i-kulli, not for everyone, which is the essence (khulasa) of 10-12 Imams gathered and given to a very high-ranking Imam.
Lahut is the original form (asl paikar); our suwar (forms) ascend and become Lahut, it being the form and not the ruh that rises.

Imam and Imamat are distinct: a son such as Ja'far al-Sadiq is not an Imam until nass (designation) occurs, and 'Ali Akbar and 'Ali Asghar are called Imam only out of respect, the true Imam being Mawlana Zayn al-'Abidin.

After death the suwar/Rij'iyyah parts ascend through the planets (qamar, Zuhal, Zuhra, Shams, Mushtari, Mirrikh) to the qalam and then to the kamil, remaining there until the Imam wills his successor-son's birth.

When the Imam wills his successor's birth, the gathered Rij'iyyat (as water or juice) permeate a pure paradise fruit (grape, pomegranate or apple), which the Imam eats and gives to his wife, so the next Imam is conceived from their union.
The Imam's conception is wholly different in its chemistry and physics, and during pregnancy his wife continually receives madad (sustenance) from above for nine months.
After death one's belief and conception (tasawwur, the work of the natiqah) forms a spiritual form (suwar-i-ruhaniyyah) that becomes one's higher rank (hadd-i-'ali).

There are two types of suwar, the suwar-i-'amali (form of deeds) and the suwar-i-'ilmi (form of knowledge); both outward action ('amal) and inward knowledge ('ilm) are the wings for flight and both must be present.
Every believer has a hadd-i-'ali (one rank above) and a hadd-i-adna (one rank below), and one's exact seat/number is known to the Imam, for 'Ind Allahi Ilm' (with Allah is the knowledge).
The chain of hadd-i-'ali and hadd-i-adna ascends to the very top and is what the Wahhabis most dislike.

At death the namiyyah and hissiyah are left behind, the namiyyah becoming Rij'iyyah (or the hissiyah joining the natiqah and purifying), and one's deeds (namaz, roza, hajj, zakat, charity, good character) combine into a suwar that goes to one's hadd-i-'ali.
There is no distinction of men and women in the hadd ranks; even a da'i's hadd-i-'ali can be a woman.
One's suwar joins the suwar of the hadd-i-'ali (one plus one doubling), while the nafs becomes its mujawir (neighbor); the nafs can be corrupted but the suwar cannot.

On the hadd-i-'ali's own good death the joined suwars ascend to a third, a fourth, and so on up to the great one of the jazirah (the malik), then to the da'i (Malik-i-Jami'), the original owner of everything.
There are four types of doors (abwab): Lahat, Bath, Musalsal and Indamaji, and the Bab al-Abwab is the door of all doors.
The Bab al-Abwab, with whom the suwarat of all twelve jaza'ir gather, is the Fasl al-Khitab (decisive speech), so that whatever leaves his mouth comes to pass.

The believers' spiritual forms ascend through hudud, suwar, du'at, the da'i and the Bab al-Abwab, the things of the twelve jaza'ir being collected via four da'is up to the Bab al-Abwab and then the Imam.
To transfer Imamat, the Imam first takes the suwarat from the Bab al-Abwab (whose departure then becomes necessary as his duty is done) and hands the trust of Imamat to his son by nass.

The haykal (the assembled Lahut/Imam form) is wholly human in shape though invisible, with each part of the believers set against the corresponding part, and the Bab al-Abwab is set against the heart (qalb).
